articles.title: Meta says news 'very likely' to return to its platforms in Canada
articles.text:
Meta says news could soon return to its platforms in Canada.
Speaking to Politico reporter Mickey Djuric, Meta Canada head of public policy Rachel Curran said it’s “very likely” that Canadians will be able to share news once again on Instagram and Facebook. She said she’s optimistic a resolution will come through ongoing Canada-U.S. trade talks.
🚨 NEW: Meta hopes to restore news on Facebook/Insta in Canada by year’s end.
Meta Canada’s Rachel Curran says it will “very likely” be resolved thru Canada-U.S. trade talks. “If we are able to reach agreement post-midterms … the news stuff will be dealt with as part of that.”
— Mickey Djuric (@MickeyDjuric) November 4, 2026
Meta has been blocking news on its platforms in Canada since 2023 in response to the federal government’s Bill C-18, also known as the Online News Act. Under that law, Meta and Google are required to pay Canadian publishers for sharing content on their respective platforms.
The feds argued that companies like Meta benefit from this news circulation and should compensate journalists accordingly. Meta, however, argued that this law misunderstood its relationship with publishers because they voluntarily post links to its platforms and earn money from other revenue streams like advertising or subscriptions. Naturally, this long-running blocking of news has been a blow to both publishers (especially smaller ones) and everyday Canadians alike.
But change could be coming. As Curran mentioned, the U.S. just had its major mid-term elections in which the Democrats landed major victories across the country. Naturally, this so-called “blue wave” takes some power away from U.S. President Donald Trump’s Republicans, who are responsible for starting this ridiculous trade war with Canada in the first place. Therefore, it remains to be seen what negotiations U.S. politicians might now make with Canada, including with regard to the Online News Act.
Source: Mickey Djuric (@MickeyDjuric)

articles.title: "No puede existir interés general si existe rechazo general": más de 8.000 personas se manifiestan contra la piscina de surf de Cantabria
articles.text:
Cantabria tiene más de 200 kilómetros de costa, 80 playas (alguna más, en realidad) y 4 reservas de surf. Aun así, su Gobierno lleva un tiempo tramitando una piscina de olas, al estilo madrileño, apenas a 7 kilómetros del mar. Pero no todos están conformes: el sábado 31 de octubre, Villaverde de Pontones (Ribamontán al Monte, con apenas 467 habitantes) recibió a más de 8.000 personas, según la organización. Cortaron la carretera general para decir que no, que una región que ya duda de si quiere ser la “Ibiza del norte” no puede andar montando una laguna artificial en mitad del pueblo.
En la manifestación se gritaron consignas y se podía leer “Cantabria se defiende. No al PSIR Olucas”. Se sumaron afectados por otros PSIR: Real de Piasca, Laredo, Astillero y Las Excavadas, en Torrelavega. Fue convocada por el partido Cantabristas, un partido. Decía Paulu Lobete, su secretario general, que “No puede existir interés general si existe rechazo general”. Luego, cuando hablaron el alcalde y la candidata del PRC, Paula Fernández, recibieron una tremenda pitada.
Un resort, no una piscina. El Olucas Surf Center ocupa 100.000 metros cuadrados y la laguna sería menos de una cuarta parte. El resto son cabañas de glamping para 2 a 6 huéspedes, restaurante, tienda, escenario y aparcamiento. El Gobierno defiende una inversión privada de más de 40 millones de euros sin gasto público, 60 empleos directos y 200.000 visitantes al año. En el Parlamento se habló de unos 800 usuarios diarios, 2.000 en verano. Pero los vecinos ven otra cosa: más tráfico, más ruido, vivienda más cara y un negocio de y para poquitos.
El atajo. ¿Por qué un PSIR? Porque la normativa municipal no permite el proyecto. El Plan Singular de Interés Regional sí permitiría al Gobierno recalificar suelo y expropiar sin pasar por el Ayuntamiento de Ribamontán al Monte. La promotora registró el plan media hora antes del debate parlamentario en el que María José Sáenz de Buruaga (presidenta) anunciara el proyecto. El Consejo de Gobierno declaró el interés regional en menos de 4 meses. Puedes leer el acuerdo, publicado en el BOC, donde se recogen los argumentos del promotor y extractos de los informes de Deporte y Turismo.
¿Interés de quién? Esa es la pregunta genuina. Los afectados no entienden cómo una instalación privada, con acceso de pago, pueda cumplir esa condición. La comunidad surfera no equivale a interés regional, o eso sostienen, y piden saber qué valor público añade una ola fabricada en una región donde olas hay “a asgaya”, como dicen.
El consejero de Fomento, Vivienda, Ordenación del Territorio y Medio Ambiente, Roberto Media, asegura que el OLUCAS Surf Center "no se va a paralizar", va a seguir su tramitación y saldrá adelante, además de venderlo como una instalación con la mejor tecnología del mundo. Sin embargo, vale la pena recordar que Olucas Cantabria SL nació en mayo de 2025 con 3.000 euros de capital y lo amplió en 85.000 apenas una semana antes del anuncio. El proyecto necesita 43 millones de euros y, según su propio documento, aún busca inversores.
El suelo. Y ojo porque este plan yace (literalmente) sobre un yacimiento paleolítico al aire libre, Villaverde 2, inscrito en el Inventario Arqueológico Regional con una protección idéntica a la de un BIC (Bien de Interés Cultural, protegido por el Ministerio). Contradictoriamente, la valoración en el Parlamento fue “ningún inconveniente”. Además, el promotor controla el 70% del terreno. El resto pasa por acuerdos o expropiaciones: unas 6 parcelas, estiman los afectados.
30.000 metros cúbicos. El lago necesita ese volumen cada año para compensar la evaporación, 10 piscinas olímpicas según el propio proyecto, una cifra que recuerda a la laguna del Atleti en Madrid, que ya contamos. Roberto Media habló de “dos piscinas convencionales”.
Pero si echamos un ojo a vista de águila, conviene recordar que Ribamontán al Monte sufrió restricciones este verano en Liermo, y Cantabria es la comunidad que más agua gasta por habitante: 186 litros diarios. La media por habitante, según el INE, está en 128 litros por día. Algunos estudios consideran que pasar de 100 litros es un despilfarro. Esta base es el umbral estimado por la OMS.
Qué dice el alcalde (y quienes no gobiernan). Días antes de la marcha, y tras la presión vecinal, el regionalista Raúl Ruiz y el presidente de la Junta Vecinal, César Bolívar, se declararon contra el proyecto. Ruiz ve en los PSIR una “buena herramienta para lo público, pero no para lo privado”. Y señala a Roberto Media y al promotor como los únicos que pueden pararlo.
En cuanto al cómo llegar, todo el tráfico entra por el barrio Trapa, por un vial estrecho. No en vano, el Ayuntamiento reclama un acceso independiente y pide resolver agua y accesos antes de la aprobación definitiva. En una entrevista para la Cadena Ser, Lobete decía que “Cuando el público te dice que no hay interés, te quedas solo”. Según él, Buruaga y Media ya solo cuentan con el promotor.
El portavoz del PP en el Parlamento, Juan José Alonso, acusó a la oposición de boicotear inversión y el empleo con medias verdades. Pero PRC, PSOE y Vox cuestionaron el proyecto y no compran ese relato. El regionalista Pedro Hernando habló de un “tufillo extraño” y de problemas de suelo, agua, energía y accesos. En conclusión, el PSIR solo tiene aprobación inicial pero falta la definitiva.

articles.title: GTA 6 Speicher-Check: Ist deine PS5 oder Xbox bereit für den 200-GB-Giganten?
articles.text:
GTA 6 kommt: So machst du deine Konsole fit für den 200-GB-Giganten
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Am 19. November 2026 erscheint GTA 6. Fans der Reihe mussten sich lange gedulden, denn die Veröffentlichung des Vorgängers liegt mehr als 13 Jahre zurück. Während die Vorfreude steigt, machen neue Details allerdings klar, dass das Spiel die bisherige Hardware an ihre Grenzen bringen könnte – auch beim Speicherplatz. Wir erklären dir, wie groß der Download des langersehnten Spiels ausfallen könnte und mit welchen externen Festplatten du deine Konsole aufrüstest.
Externer Konsolenspeicher: Das musst du beachten
Mehrere Medien, darunter Yahoo Tech, berichten, dass der Download von GTA 6 über 200 Gigabyte groß sein soll. Grund dafür könnten das aufwendige Design und das immersive Spielerlebnis sein. Rockstar Games hat den Umfang bisher zwar nicht offiziell bestätigt, aber auch frühere Titel brauchten viel Platz. So kam beispielsweise Red Dead Redemption 2 auf rund 125 Gigabyte. Der interne Speicher von Playstation- und Xbox-Konsolen ist allerdings begrenzt. Oft startet er bei einem Terabyte, die kompaktere Xbox Series S gibt es sogar mit nur 512 Gigabyte. Der tatsächlich freie Speicher fällt noch geringer aus, weil die Konsole einen Teil für das Betriebssystem und weitere Systemfunktionen reserviert. Wenn du ein Spiel wie GTA 6 installieren willst, wird es also schnell eng.
Unter den Pioneers Picks stellen wir dir regelmäßig weitere praktische Tools und Gadgets vor.
Die gute Nachricht ist, dass du deine Konsole um eine externe Festplatte oder SSD erweitern kannst. Dabei gibt es aber einiges zu beachten. Anders als bei älteren Konsolen kannst du Spiele für die Playstation 5 nämlich nicht direkt auf einem externen USB-Speicher zocken. Der Grund: Diese bieten nicht die nötige Geschwindigkeit. Zum Spielen müssen die Games also zuerst auf den internen Speicher der Konsole kopiert werden. Eine externe Festplatte oder SSD dient bei der Playstation 5 daher eher als Archiv für Spiele, die du länger nicht gezockt hast, und schafft Platz auf der internen Festplatte.
Externe Speichererweiterungskarte für die Xbox
Auch bei der Xbox hängt die Nutzung eines externen Speichers von der Konsolengeneration ab. Bei älteren Modellen kannst du direkt von einer externen Festplatte oder SSD spielen. Bei der Xbox Series X und Series S geht das nicht. Eine Ausnahme bildet die externe Speichererweiterungskarte: Sie wurde in Zusammenarbeit mit Xbox entwickelt und bietet ein nahtloses Spielerlebnis, weil du hier Games direkt von der Karte starten und spielen kannst. Sie ist so konzipiert, dass sie die gleiche Speicherleistung wie die interne SSD bietet. Laut Herstellerangaben sorgt eine Übertragungsrate von 3.000 Megabyte pro Sekunde für schnelle Ladezeiten und geringe Latenzen. Du steckst die Karte auf der Rückseite der Xbox direkt in den dafür vorgesehenen Steckplatz. Das Modell von Seagate ist mit einem oder zwei Terabyte erhältlich. Bei Amazon kostet es ab 282,99 Euro.
Game Drive von Seagate für Xbox und Playstation 5
Sony bietet selbst einige externe Speicheroptionen an, die auf die Playstation 5 optimiert sind. Eine davon ist der Game Drive von Seagate. Der Durchmesser des Geräts beträgt 2,5 Zoll. Das Design ist der Konsole angepasst – inklusive Logo. Die externe Festplatte ist mit zwei oder fünf Terabyte erhältlich und bietet somit ausreichend Platz, um ältere Spiele zu archivieren oder überall hin mitzunehmen. Du schließt sie per USB-3.0-Schnittstelle direkt an die Konsole an. Ein erneutes Herunterladen entfällt somit. Bei Amazon kostet die kleinere Variante aktuell 150,99 Euro. Das gleiche Modell gibt es auch für die Xbox mit der klassischen schwarzen Optik der Microsoft-Konsole. Es ist mit zwei, acht und 20 Terabyte verfügbar, der Preis startet bei 128,99 Euro.
- Seagate Game Drive für Playstation 5 bei Amazon*
- Seagate Game Drive für Xbox Series X und Series S bei Amazon*
Externe SSD von Sandisk für deine Playstation 5
Auch Sandisk bietet externen Speicher, der offiziell für die Playstation 5 lizenziert ist. Die SSD misst ebenfalls 2,5 Zoll und orientiert sich mit ihrer weißen Farbe am Design der Sony-Konsole. Laut Hersteller bietet sie eine hohe Geschwindigkeit von bis zu 1.000 Megabyte pro Sekunde, um Spiele schnell vom externen SSD-Archiv auf den internen Speicher der Playstation 5 zu übertragen. Zudem ist sie besonders robust: Sie bietet IP65-Schutz und ist fallsicher aus bis zu drei Metern Höhe. Wie die Seagate-Festplatte schließt du die SSD per USB an die Konsole an. Das Modell gibt es mit einem oder zwei Terabyte Speicherplatz. Bei Amazon kostet es ab 200,99 Euro. Laut etablierten Preisvergleichsportalen ist das aktuell das günstigste Angebot. Trotzdem kann es sich lohnen, mit dem Kauf noch etwas zu warten, denn bis vor Kurzem war die SSD schon ab 179 Euro erhältlich.

articles.title: AMD Brings FSR Upscaling 4.1.2 to Xbox Consoles
articles.text:
Thursday, November 5th 2026
AMD Brings FSR Upscaling 4.1.2 to Xbox Consoles
Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S consoles are finally getting machine learning-based upscaling technology with the latest FSR Upscaling 4.1.2. Microsoft's Game Development Kit (GDK) now officially includes FSR Upscaling 4.1.2 in two models. One is the full-scale upscaling model based on the INT8 data type, and the other is a new and efficient Lite INT8 model. Both models are compatible with both consoles, but the key point is that game developers have the flexibility to choose which model to implement. Depending on the demands of a game, the appropriate model can be applied to achieve optimal upscaling performance.
For Xbox handheld devices, the AMD FSR SDK 2.4 adds FSR Upscaling support for the Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme and Ryzen Z2 A processors, which power the ROG Xbox Ally, ROG Xbox Ally X, and ROG Xbox Ally X20 handhelds. This is achieved using an efficient INT8 model. Since these devices run Windows, developers can integrate FSR Upscaling 4.1.2 through the standard AMD FSR SDK.Keep in mind that FSR Upscaling 4.1.x only recently arrived for AMD's RDNA versions below RDNA 4. RDNA 4 supports native processing for 8-bit floating point data, allowing FSR 4.1 on RDNA 4 to run on FP8 data types. To enable the FSR 4.1 Upscaling model on RDNA 3, AMD must convert this to 8-bit integer data, as RDNA 3.5 APUs and RDNA 2 GPU IP powering Xbox consoles use INT8 data types without FP8 support.
Sources:

articles.title: India rebased its GDP. It still can’t see the Rs 34.5 lakh crore women do free
articles.text:
India rebased its GDP. It still can’t see the Rs 34.5 lakh crore women do free
Women’s unpaid household and care work is valued at up to Rs 34.5 lakh crore, yet India’s rebased GDP counts none of it. A satellite account, care investment and childcare as labour policy could change that.
In February 2026, India moved its GDP base year to 2022-23. The National Accounts of India brought in new data sources and reassessed the size of the informal economy. The exercise carried a lesson that policy debates often forget: economic measurement is not fixed. When the statistical system decides an activity deserves to be captured better, the numbers change.
The same quarter, the economy grew 7.8%, keeping India the fastest-growing major economy even through the first full quarter of steep US tariffs and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. The headlines celebrated. But one kind of work counted for nothing in all that arithmetic: the unpaid domestic and care work that makes every other job possible.
The invisible fifth of the economy
GDP has a defined production boundary, and for good reason. A creche worker paid to look after a child is counted as economic activity. A mother or grandmother doing the same job for free is not. The value has not disappeared; only the payment has.
What sits outside that boundary is large. India's Time Use Survey 2024 shows women aged 15 to 59 spend about 201 minutes a day more than men on unpaid household work. A deeper analysis of the unit-level data puts women's unpaid domestic and care work at 343 minutes a day, against 43 for men. Some 93% of women do this work, compared with 44% of men.
A Ministry of Women and Child Development study values this work at up to Rs 34.5 lakh crore, roughly 15–17% of GDP at weighted average wages. Even the Ministry of Statistics' Time Use Survey report concedes that leaving out unpaid services means GDP "underestimates considerably the total income of a nation."
The global answer is not to abandon GDP but to add a satellite account that measures activity beyond the production boundary. India already has the raw material: two national Time Use Surveys, an accepted valuation method, and a statistical system that has just shown it can rebuild its accounts. What is missing is the decision.
From invisible labour to the second shift
Visibility matters because governments allocate money through the numbers they measure.
According to the UNDP, 44.5% of Indian women outside the labour force cite childcare and homemaking as the main reason. Female labour-force participation has climbed from 23.3% in 2017-18 to about 40% in 2025, by the Periodic Labour Force Survey's measure. Yet women's unpaid workload has barely moved in five years.
A woman who takes a paid job while carrying the same load at home has not been freed to work. She has taken on a second shift. The real policy question is not how to persuade more women to work. It is what infrastructure would make paid work compatible with care.
India's jobs ambition has a care problem
The contradiction shows up in the government's own documents. The Economic Survey's employment chapter calls the care economy a promising source of jobs, and the Economic Survey 2025-26 targets a 55% female workforce. Yet under the Palna scheme, only 11,395 anganwadi-cum-creches had been approved against a target of 17,000 by March 2025. Fewer than 10% of anganwadi centres are in cities, where women's participation is lowest.
The shortfall does not mean the scheme has failed. It means care infrastructure is still being built while the country sets big employment goals. If policymakers want a real rise in women's paid work, childcare must stop being a side programme and become labour-market policy.
What other countries did differently
By the ILO's harmonised estimates, India's female labour-force participation was 32% in 2025. The figure is lower than the PLFS number because the ILO uses a different, internationally comparable definition.
Among women of prime working age, participation reaches 85% in Japan and 78% in the United States.
These gaps are policy outcomes, not accidents. Japan raised fathers' take-up of parental leave from 17.1% to 30.1% in a single year by paying for it. Bangladesh, with a fraction of India's output, lifted net pre-primary enrolment from 19.7% in 2018 to 28.5% in 2023 as part of a deliberate push to get women into work. The United States learnt the opposite lesson: prime-age women hit record participation, then gains among mothers of young children stalled where affordable childcare ran out.
No country has gone from developing to developed while leaving half its working-age women outside the paid economy. The road to Viksit Bharat has to take her along, or it will not arrive.
Three ordinary acts of statecraft
1. Measure it. Complete and regularly publish a satellite account for unpaid care work, linked to the Time Use Survey. It should show the work's value, who does it, where it is concentrated and how it changes. The aim is not to inflate GDP but to give planners a second dashboard to act on.
2. Invest in it. The UNDP estimates that spending about 2% of GDP on care services could create more than 11 million jobs. As India urbanises, fertility falls and joint families thin out, who provides care is becoming an economic question, not just a household one.
3. Reclassify it. Care spending should be judged not only as welfare but by its effect on employment, labour supply and productivity. If a childcare centre lets twenty parents stay in work, its value cannot be measured only by the children it serves.
Seeing what GDP cannot
This argument is no longer confined to feminist economics. A working paper from the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister this year calls for moving care "from private burden to social and economic infrastructure." The diagnosis is in, and the evidence backs it. The harder question is whether measurement, budgeting and delivery will follow.
The 2026 rebasing showed that India's statistical system can question long-held assumptions. The same willingness should now extend to the work that sustains the economy from outside its markets.
That means collecting real-time data, publishing a satellite account for unpaid care linked to the Time Use Survey, and treating care infrastructure as a measurable public investment. Every new creche, eldercare service and community care programme should be judged not only by the people it serves but by the paid work it makes possible.
If India wants more women in its workforce, it must budget for the care that makes their work possible. India has shown it can re-measure its economy. Now it must build the care that lets more women take part in it.

articles.title: “Pensez-vous qu’une quelconque industrie puisse survivre à cela ?” : les voitures électriques chinoises inquiètent toujours plus Renault
articles.text:
Crise de l’automobile européenne : le patron de Renault réclame des mesures d’urgence face à la concurrence chinoise
Face à la concurrence chinoise, François Provost, patron de Renault, avertit qu’en l’absence de réaction de l’Union européenne, la production automobile européenne pourrait être divisée par deux après 2030, menaçant des centaines de milliers d’emplois.
L’industrie automobile européenne fait face à une concurrence chinoise des plus féroces. Lors d’un échange à Londres avec Reuters, François Provost, directeur général de Renault, a dressé un tableau particulièrement sombre de l’avenir du secteur sur le Vieux Continent, ciblant directement le manque d’actions de l’Union européenne. Pour le dirigeant, laisser le marché ouvert aux importations asiatiques à bas coût sans réaction de Bruxelles va tout simplement “tuer l’industrie automobile en Europe”.
Un écart de coûts de 40 % impossible à combler sans produire en Europe, Renault s’agace
Selon François Provost, si Bruxelles laisse la situation en l’état, le volume de véhicules assemblés sur le continent chuterait à la moitié de sa moyenne historique peu après 2030. “Pensez-vous qu’une quelconque industrie puisse survivre à cela ?”, a-t-il lancé aux journalistes, alors que des centaines de milliers d’emplois chez les constructeurs et les équipementiers sont en jeu. Au Mondial de l’Auto 2026, il évoquait déjà un risque de perte de 300 000 véhicules produits par an pour Renault sans assouplissement des normes de CO2 d’ici 2030.
Tout le problème vient d’un écart de coûts massif. En important leurs voitures, les constructeurs chinois affichent “des coûts inférieurs de 30 à 40 %” à ceux des industriels européens, explique le patron de Renault. Un fossé impossible à combler pour la marque au Losange, sauf si l’Union européenne oblige les marques chinoises à fabriquer localement leurs voitures destinées au marché européen. À armes égales sur le Vieux Continent, il assure pouvoir rivaliser.
Une telle obligation d’investissement local serait toutefois à double tranchant si elle s’appliquait aux modèles électrifiés. Cela risquerait en effet d’attiser les tensions commerciales avec Pékin sans régler les problèmes de compétitivité propres aux constructeurs historiques, dont les récents efforts (à l’image du bon démarrage de la Renault 5 E-Tech) ne suffisent toujours pas à rassurer les marchés.
En cause, une percée chinoise si rapide qu’elle prive les investisseurs de toute visibilité, résume l’analyste Philippe Houchois chez Jefferies, transformant peu à peu le secteur européen en “industrie zombie”, déjà cannibalisée par les modèles chinois. Un pessimisme généralisé qui traduit avant tout, selon François Provost, “l’anticipation que l’Union européenne ne bougera pas”. Réponse dans les semaines et mois à venir, notamment avec le tant attendu “Industrial Accelerator Act”, le projet de loi européen censé imposer des critères stricts de “Made in Europe” à la filière automobile.

articles.title: Vols de câbles : 850 stations de recharge visées en France, les opérateurs appellent l'État à l'aide
articles.text:
L’association Charge France, qui réunit les principaux opérateurs de bornes de recharge, a publié le 3 novembre un bilan qui montre l’ampleur prise par le phénomène. Depuis le début de l’année, 850 sites de recharge ont été visés par des vols de câbles, soit environ 10 % du réseau de recharge rapide français, pour un préjudice estimé à 18 millions d’euros. Auprès du Figaro, son secrétaire général, Matthieu Dischamps, évoque même un millier de stations touchées fin octobre, plus de 15 % du réseau de recharge rapide et 21 millions d’euros de préjudice, contre une centaine de stations sur toute l’année 2025. Les voleurs s’attaquent au cuivre que contiennent ces câbles, particulièrement épais sur les bornes rapides.
Le butin est pourtant plutôt maigre, puisqu’un câble sectionné leur rapporterait entre 30 et 80 euros à la revente. En revanche, son remplacement coûte environ 1 500 euros à l’opérateur, sans compter l’intervention des techniciens et les recettes perdues pendant l’immobilisation de la station.
Pour les conducteurs, la conséquence est très concrète. Une station dont les câbles ont été coupés ne peut tout simplement plus recharger et TotalEnergies indiquait à BFM remplacer les câbles en une quinzaine de jours. Le problème pèse d’autant plus que 71 % des conducteurs de voitures 100 % électriques utilisent la recharge publique, selon une enquête Enedis-CSA d’octobre citée par l’association. Sur les grands axes, où les stations peuvent être espacées de plusieurs dizaines de kilomètres, il est recommandé de vérifier la disponibilité d’une borne sur l’application dédiée ou le planificateur de bord avant de s’y rendre.
Des vols de plus en plus organisés
Les opérateurs estiment que ces vols sont surtout le fait de réseaux organisés équipés de coupe-câbles hydrauliques sur batterie et des meuleuses de chantier, qui opèrent de nuit sur des sites isolés et sans surveillance. « Sur notre réseau de plus de 450 stations, nous constatons presque chaque semaine un ou plusieurs actes de vol de câbles », explique Gautier Chatelus, président de Driveco, qui déploie progressivement des gaines en Kevlar intégrant des puces GSM. D’autres opérateurs misent sur la vidéosurveillance, les alarmes ou les alertes en temps réel, et Ionity dit recourir à une protection physique renforcée, à des technologies de suivi et à des systèmes de marquage à l’encre.
La justice commence néanmoins à sévir et Charge France recense quinze mises en examen depuis janvier, dont sept depuis septembre. Les tribunaux de Toulouse et de Troyes ont prononcé des peines de deux ans de prison ferme, assorties d’interdictions du territoire de cinq et dix ans, et celui de Nantes une peine de seize mois ferme, avec à chaque fois l’indemnisation des opérateurs. Pour l’association, ce n’est pas suffisant.
Elle demande aux ministères de l’Intérieur et de la Justice de croiser les enquêtes entre parquets pour démanteler les réseaux, de renforcer les contrôles chez les ferrailleurs pour fermer les filières de recel, et de mobiliser rapidement les forces de l’ordre en cas d’alertes d’une borne. « On ne peut pas demander aux Français de passer à l’électrique et les laisser face à des bornes rendues inutilisables par des vols », alerte Matthieu Dischamps, secrétaire général de Charge France, tout en interpellant aussi les candidats à l’élection présidentielle de 2027.
Les bornes bientôt classées infrastructures critiques ?
Le sujet est aussi remonté à l’Assemblée nationale et dans une question écrite adressée le 3 novembre au ministre de l’Intérieur, la députée Olga Givernet (Ensemble pour la République) fait état de 637 plaintes et d’environ 14 millions d’euros de préjudice déclarés par 27 opérateurs. Elle plaide pour classer les stations les plus stratégiques parmi les infrastructures critiques, au sens de la directive européenne de 2022 sur la résilience des entités critiques, afin de mieux les protéger.
Charge France appuie cette demande en prenant pour modèle le Portugal, où le phénomène aurait disparu après la condamnation d’un voleur à neuf ans de prison ferme. Dans ce pays, les bornes sont considérées comme des infrastructures énergétiques critiques. Aucune décision n’a été annoncée à ce jour en France. En attendant, les opérateurs paient à la fois les réparations et les nouvelles protections, tout en finançant l’extension du réseau. On comptait environ 40 000 points de recharge rapide fin septembre en France.

articles.title: Los centros de datos de IA generan su propia energía. ¿Cómo afecta esto a la red eléctrica en general?
articles.text:
La IA necesita cada vez más electricidad y las Big Tech están buscando maneras de lograrlo sin depender de compañías eléctricas. Según las previsiones de la Agencia Internacional de la Energía, el consumo mundial de los centros de datos podría pasar de 485 teravatios hora en 2025 a unos 950 en 2030, así que hablamos de casi el doble en cinco años.
Ante dicho crecimiento, algunas empresas apuestan por instalar sus propias fuentes de energía junto a los servidores, pero aquí entra en juego que esta cuestión va más allá de sus instalaciones. Producir electricidad por cuenta propia permite reducir la dependencia de una red que, en algunas regiones, ya tiene dificultades para atender nuevas solicitudes de conexión. Sin embargo, como explica un análisis del Foro Económico Mundial, eso no significa que los centros de datos puedan prescindir completamente del suministro general.
Así, muchos necesitan seguir conectados para afrontar averías, cubrir momentos de mayor consumo o disponer de electricidad cuando sus propios sistemas no funcionan, razón por la que la infraestructura compartida continúa siendo necesaria.
Generar electricidad propia no elimina los costes de la red
El problema aparece cuando estas instalaciones compran menos electricidad a las compañías suministradoras y siguen necesitando que la red esté preparada para atenderlas. Mantener esa capacidad tiene un coste y, si las normas no reflejan el uso que hacen los grandes consumidores, parte de la factura podría terminar repartiéndose entre hogares y pequeñas empresas.
Justo por eso, el regulador energético estadounidense ordenó en diciembre de 2025 revisar las condiciones de conexión de grandes instalaciones situadas junto a centrales eléctricas. Un ejemplo podría ser el de Irlanda, dado que también está tomando medidas para evitar que el crecimiento de los centros de datos termine comprometiendo su sistema eléctrico.
De esta forma, desde diciembre de 2025 las nuevas condiciones de conexión exigen (según el tamaño de las instalaciones) disponer de capacidad de generación o almacenamiento cercana y cubrir al menos el 80 % de la demanda anual mediante nueva producción renovable nacional, con un periodo de adaptación. En este punto, la cuestión va más allá de encontrar suficiente electricidad para alimentar la IA, ya que también se centra en decidir cómo deben contribuir estas instalaciones a una red de la que todavía dependen.

articles.title: Leerles cuentos a los bebés desde que nacen tiene un impacto que va mucho más allá de entretenerlos
articles.text:
Durante las primeras consultas que se hacen con pediatría cuando llega un nuevo miembro a la familia, se escucha que es bastante importante leer a los más pequeños casi que desde el primer mes de vida. Los pediatras apuntan a que, cogiendo un libro y leyéndoselo a los más pequeños, se puede lograr crear un vínculo afectivo más intenso con los progenitores, que se vaya ganando vocabulario y también una mejora cognitiva y motora.
Es algo respaldado. Esta idea es algo que tiene un importante respaldo médico que llega, por ejemplo, desde la Academia Americana de Pediatría que recomienda explícitamente a los pediatras el hecho de fomentar la lectura compartida desde el nacimiento, incluso en las Unidades de Cuidados Intensivos neonatales.
Una ganancia de vocabulario. Uno de los beneficios más tangibles, sobre todo cuando los niños comienzan a ir creciendo, es el hecho de que escuchen muchas palabras diferentes que enriquecen su lenguaje. Esto es algo en lo que se centró un estudio del año 2019, donde se calculó la "brecha del millón de palabras", donde se estimó que los niños criados en familias donde se lee con frecuencia escuchan hasta 1,4 millones de palabras más a través de los cuentos que aquellos a los que nunca se les lee antes de entrar al colegio. Aunque siempre teniendo en cuenta que esto es una estimación.
Esta exposición temprana es el cimiento del lenguaje y no se trata solo de la cantidad de palabras, sino de la diversidad y complejidad del vocabulario literario, que rara vez surge en las conversaciones cotidianas sobre la cena o la hora del baño. El punto que hay que tener aquí es que todos los libros deben estar adaptados a la edad del pequeño e ir aumentando la complejidad de manera escalonada.
El aprendizaje. El impacto de esta inmersión lingüística se nota a largo plazo como se determinó en un estudio de 1995, donde vieron que la lectura compartida en la etapa preescolar explica alrededor del 8% de la varianza en las habilidades de lectura y lenguaje cuando los niños llegan a primero de primaria.
A nivel neuronal. La neurociencia también ha asomado la cabeza para entender este fenómeno y un estudio transversal utilizó resonancias magnéticas funcionales en niños de 3 a 5 años. A partir de estas imágenes se descubrieron que aquellos provenientes de entornos de lectura más ricos mostraban una mayor activación en la corteza de asociación parieto-temporo-occipital izquierda mientras escuchaban cuentos.
Aunque el estudio es correlacional y no permite afirmar que la lectura cause directamente cambios estructurales, sí indica que la lectura compartida estimula de forma consistente las áreas del cerebro encargadas de la integración semántica y la visualización mental.
Causalidad real. La prueba del algodón llegó en el año 2020 cuando se analizaron varios ensayos que agrupaban a casi 2.600 niños de entre 1 y 6 años. Con esta muestra, se determinó que la lectura compartida tiene un efecto causal real en el desarrollo del lenguaje expresivo y receptivo.
Eso sí, la ciencia también pone los pies en la tierra al apuntar que este efecto causal es modesto y que depende fundamentalmente de la dosis y de la interacción. Es por ello que leer mecánicamente un libro en voz baja tiene un impacto mínimo, puesto que el verdadero beneficio explosivo ocurre cuando la lectura es interactiva, haciendo preguntas al niño, señalando, comentando la historia...

articles.title: Apple veut des salariés dopés à l’IA, mais commence à couper les crédits
articles.text:
Apple réduit les sommes que certains salariés peuvent consacrer chaque jour aux outils d’intelligence artificielle. L’entreprise continue pourtant de pousser ses équipes à les intégrer dans leur travail.
Utiliser davantage l’IA pour gagner du temps, oui, mais en surveillant le compteur. Chez Apple, les assistants capables d’écrire du code ou de débusquer des erreurs ont désormais droit à un encadrement budgétaire plus serré. Selon les informations de Mark Gurman pour Bloomberg, certains ingénieurs ont déjà vu leur enveloppe quotidienne diminuer. Et d’autres réductions sont à l’étude.
De 300 à 200 dollars par jour, avec de nouvelles baisses dans les tuyaux
En octobre, Apple aurait abaissé de 300 à 200 dollars le plafond quotidien de dépenses de certains ingénieurs utilisant des modèles d’IA. Pour certaines équipes, l’entreprise préparerait une nouvelle baisse, susceptible de ramener cette limite à 100 dollars.
Hors ingénierie, de nombreux services disposent déjà d’un plafond de 100 dollars par jour. Apple aurait envisagé de le réduire jusqu’à 25 dollars pour certaines équipes. Les salariés ayant besoin d’une enveloppe supérieure pourraient toutefois demander une dérogation à leur direction.
Ces montants financent les jetons consommés par les modèles, ces unités de données traitées à chaque requête. Une longue session de programmation, avec des corrections successives et beaucoup de code à analyser, peut rapidement faire grimper la consommation. Les salariés d’Apple ont notamment accès à Claude, ChatGPT et Gemini.
Attention toutefois à ne pas confondre budget autorisé et facture réelle. D’après Bloomberg, certains employés soulignent que peu de leurs collègues atteignaient l’ancien plafond de 300 dollars. Réduire cette limite d’un tiers ne signifie donc pas qu’Apple économisera automatiquement un tiers de ses dépenses.
L’IA reste encouragée, mais son utilisation doit coûter moins cher
Le changement est intéressant au regard des consignes précédentes. Les salariés d’Apple sont depuis plusieurs mois poussés à utiliser davantage l’IA, notamment avant de demander des renforts humains. Le budget de 300 dollars par jour était déjà évoqué à l’époque.
La volonté de transformer les méthodes de travail reste bien présente. Certaines équipes seraient désormais orientées vers des modèles moins coûteux ou fonctionnant directement sur les appareils. Pour les utilisateurs les plus gourmands, les prochaines réductions pourraient surtout multiplier les demandes de dérogation.
Les derniers comptes publiés par Apple donnent une idée du contexte : les dépenses de recherche et développement ont atteint 45,8 milliards de dollars sur l’exercice 2026, soit environ 32 % de plus qu’un an auparavant. Les dépenses d’exploitation ont progressé d’environ 22 %, à 75,5 milliards de dollars. Ces chiffres couvrent toutefois un périmètre bien plus large que l’IA.
Apple a refusé de commenter ces informations. Le montant des économies attendues reste inconnu, tout comme l’étendue des nouvelles restrictions qui seront finalement appliquées.

articles.title: Artemis 2: So störte der Raketenstart den GPS-Empfang auf der Erde
articles.text:
Artemis 2: SLS-Rakete der Nasa hat so großes Loch in der Atmosphäre hinterlassen, dass sogar GPS gestört war
Am 1. April 2026 startete mit Artemis 2 die erste bemannte Mondmission seit 1972. Eine Trägerrakete des Space Launch Systems (SLS) beförderte in Cape Canaveral das Orion-Raumschiff mit vier Astronaut:innen an Bord in den Weltraum.
Trägerrakete brachte Ionosphäre der Erde durcheinander
Wie nun eine Studie zeigt, hatte die Mission verblüffende Konsequenzen. Die Manöver der Rakete veränderten demnach die Ionosphäre der Erde. Dies störte wiederum GPS-Signale.
Hinter der Studie steckt ein Forschungsteams der National Cheng Kung University in Taiwan und des NASA Goddard Space Flight Center. Sie ist in der Zeitschrift Geophysical Research Letters erschienen.
Schockwelle durch Raketenstart
Laut der Studie registrierten bodengestützte GPS-Systeme bei drei Manövern Veränderungen der Elektronendichte in der Ionosphäre. Dabei handelt es sich um den elektrisch geladener Bereich der oberen Erdatmosphäre. Er erstreckt sich in einer Höhe zwischen 60 bis 1000 Kilometern über der Erdoberfläche.
Die erste Irritation der Ionosphäre passierte beim Take-off der Rakete, der Schockwellen und Gravitationswellen auslöste. Dadurch entstand buchstäblich ein Loch in der Ionosphäre, das allerdings nur kurz Bestand hatte.
5000 Kilometer langes Loch in Ionosphäre
Gut zwei Stunden nach dem Start folgte das Manöver zur Anhebung des Apogäum, also des am weitesten von der Erde entfernten Punktes in der Umlaufbahn. Dabei wird ein Raketentriebwerk am erdnächsten Punkt gezündet, durch den Schub erhöht sich die Geschwindigkeit.
Diese Zündung erzeugte wiederum Schockwellen und ein Loch in der Ionosphäre über Nordamerika. Es hatte laut der Studie eine Länge von rund 5000 Kilometern.
Zum ersten Mal drei Störungen über derselben Region
Gut einen Tag nach dem Take-off leitete die Rakete das Manöver zur Einleitung der translunaren Flugbahn ein. Auch hier entstand über Nordamerika ein Loch, das allerdings zu schwächeren ionosphärischen Störungen führte.
Laut der Studie hat mit Artemis 2 zum ersten Mal eine einzelne Mission während drei Manövern Störungen über derselben Region hervorgerufen.
Veränderung von Elektronendichte irritiert GPS
Das Problem an der Sache ist nun: Die Veränderungen der Konzentration von Elektronen in der Ionosphäre haben ganz konkrete Folgen auf der Erde. Sie stören nämlich den Empfang von GPS-Signalen.
Empfangsgeräte von GPS-Signalen auf der Erde bestimmen ihre Position, indem sie ständig ihre Entfernung zu GPS-Satelliten messen. Wenn sich die Dichte von freien Elektronen in der oberen Atmosphäre ändert, kommen die Signale früher oder langsamer als gewöhnlich an. Dies kann nicht nur bei Raketenmanövern, sondern auch bei Sonnenstürmen passieren.
Gefahr für selbstfahrende Autos und Drohnen
Die Störungen können zu ungenauen Messungen führen. Mit gefährlichen Konsequenzen. „Ein Positionsfehler von nur wenigen Metern reicht aus, um ein autonom fahrendes Auto zum Spurwechsel zu veranlassen“, sagte Studienautor Charles Lin zu dem Portal Space.com.
Laut Lin könnten die GPS-Aussetzer auch Folgen für die Positionsbestimmung von Drohnen haben. Ob es wegen Artemis 2 zu Unfällen kam, ist nicht bekannt. Für zukünftige Missionen könnte die Forschung aber wichtige Erkenntnisse liefern.
Gravitationswellen? Geht’s noch? Wisst ihr überhaupt was das ist ?

articles.title: Aina's smart AI ring promises a new way to interact with AI agents that anticipate user's needs - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Aina’s smart AI ring promises a new way to interact with AI agents that anticipate user’s needs
Artificial intelligence has come a long way in a very short space of time, writing emails, answering questions, generating code, images, video and more besides. But as breathtaking as these advances are, using AI is still a hassle. People have to dig out their smartphone and find the right app, then enter a prompt before anything gets done.
Seeking to eliminate this friction is a startup called Aina Computers Inc., which has just emerged from 15 months in “stealth mode” to launch its flagship product: an AI-native smart ring equipped with an OLED display that’s purpose-built to control autonomous AI agents.
Aina founder Apoorv Shankar told SiliconANGLE that the development of hardware interfaces has not kept pace with the advances in AI. For people to access intelligence, they need to go fumbling through smartphone applications or switch on a laptop.
Even the most basic tasks, like ordering an Uber, require someone to open an app, enter their destination and click to confirm. To join a virtual meeting, the user still has to dig through their emails to find the right link. In Shankar’s view, AI is trapped behind a software layer and that means it cannot proactively serve people when they need it.
Aina’s Ring is meant to free AI from these binds and make it as simple to access as uttering a command. The Ring is made from titanium and comes equipped with a colorful OLED display, a microphone and a speaker, and an 18-hour battery. There’s also a mechanical “shifter” that can track thumb gestures in four directions.. “We started building Aina with a thesis that AI would evolve from following instructions to anticipating what we need,” Shankar explained.
The device is powered by Aina’s Context Aware Operating System software, which is designed to learn the Ring wearer’s behavior over time in order to anticipate their needs. It can connect to the user’s devices, such as their smartphone and computer, and also any AI agents they use. Once it’s up and running, it tries to anticipate what users will need at any given moment and surface the information they need on the Ring’s display before they even ask for it.
“With proactive agents, this shift has already begun,” Shankar said. “Agents like Muse, Instinct and Dots will soon run hundreds of our daily tasks, yet we still have to instruct them by text or voice. But soon, they’ll learn our patterns, build on our context and turn proactive for almost every interaction, waiting only for our approval.”
Shankar founded Aina last year. The startup was originally a human-computer interaction research lab. Its 40-person team experimented with dozens of different hardware concepts, including an adaptive three-key Mac keypad called Dune, before ultimately settling on the Ring as the ultimate interface for AI agents.
Aina’s $399 Ring is available for pre-order now and will ship to customers in January. That’s the date at which people’s relationship with AI is set to fundamentally change, Shankar believes. When someone wears Aina’s Ring, the way they interact with their AI agents will generally become a matter of simply saying yes or no, for they will quickly learn to anticipate what their users need, at the moment they need it, he said.
Users can interact with the Ring in three ways. The microphone is there to support voice interactions. The user simply presses and holds the button in the center to call up an agent and instruct it to do something, or else they can just use it to record some quick notes. It will also be able to relay phone calls, enabling people to converse by just holding their hand close to their ear.
The Ring also supports cues that are powered by the context-aware operating system. As it learns to anticipate user’s needs, it will be able to proactively order an Uber ride based on the time of day, their location and their schedule. All the user has to do is click or say “yes” to confirm and the Ring will book the ride. Alternatively, if someone is late for an appointment, the Ring will proactively draft a message to let the person they’re meeting know when they’ll arrive.
Shankar said the Ring can also be used as a remote control, so if someone is watching TV they’ll be able to tell it to pause or rewind the show they’re watching. It can adjust microphones and cameras during video calls, skip to the next track when someone’s listening to music on their iPod and so on.
“Every major shift in computing has come from software and hardware built together,” Shankar said. “The mouse and GUI brought us personal computing. The touchscreen and the app gave us mobile computing. Now with Aina we enter a new era, with personalized computing right at your fingertips.”

articles.title: God of War Laufey cambia su fecha de estreno en PlayStation 5: cuándo estará disponible
articles.text:
Santa Monica Studio anunció un retraso en el lanzamiento de God of War Laufey, el nuevo videojuego de la popular franquicia de PlayStation. El título, que inicialmente tenía previsto llegar el 16 de febrero de 2027, ahora estará disponible el 20 de mayo de ese mismo año para PlayStation 5 y PS5 Pro.
La desarrolladora comunicó la decisión mediante un mensaje publicado en sus redes sociales, aunque no explicó los motivos específicos de la postergación. Sin embargo, señaló que utilizará el tiempo adicional para completar los últimos detalles y llevar el juego al máximo potencial.
El anuncio supone una espera de poco más de tres meses para quienes aguardaban esta nueva entrega. La producción despertó gran expectativa desde su presentación en junio pasado, principalmente porque propone un cambio importante en la historia: Kratos dejará de ser el protagonista principal para dar paso a Faye, su esposa fallecida.
Desde Santa Monica Studio agradecieron la recepción que tuvo el proyecto y la confianza de los seguidores. “No damos por sentado la confianza depositada en el estudio para crear una experiencia extraordinaria digna de la pasión y dedicación de nuestros fans”, indicaron en el comunicado.
Los desarrolladores también aseguraron que aprovecharán el tiempo adicional para terminar el videojuego y perfeccionar sus elementos antes de su estreno.
Por qué se retrasó God of War Laufey
Santa Monica Studio no detalló qué problemas llevaron a modificar el calendario de lanzamiento. No obstante, el mensaje publicado por el equipo apunta a que todavía necesitan tiempo para completar el desarrollo y realizar los ajustes finales.
La decisión llega en una etapa importante para la franquicia, que prepara una nueva historia con una protagonista diferente y un enfoque de combate que se distancia de las últimas aventuras de Kratos.
Los retrasos en la industria de los videojuegos suelen responder a la necesidad de corregir errores, mejorar el rendimiento o completar contenidos antes de la publicación. En este caso, el estudio no confirmó que exista un problema técnico específico ni señaló que el cambio esté relacionado con alguna dificultad de producción.
Por ahora, la nueva fecha anunciada es el 20 de mayo de 2027. Los usuarios de PlayStation 5 y PS5 Pro deberán esperar hasta entonces para conocer la nueva aventura de la saga.
De qué trata God of War Laufey y quién será su protagonista
God of War Laufey fue uno de los anuncios destacados del State of Play que PlayStation realizó en junio de 2026. El videojuego se aleja de la historia centrada en Kratos y presenta a Faye, también conocida como Laufey, como personaje principal.
La trama comienza después de su muerte, cuando despierta en el Everywhen, una dimensión que funciona como una especie de más allá para los dioses. Allí deberá enfrentarse a distintas criaturas mitológicas y superar peligros mientras intenta avanzar por este nuevo territorio.
El primer adelanto de jugabilidad mostró un estilo de combate más acrobático y dinámico que el visto en las entregas protagonizadas por Kratos. Faye utiliza sus habilidades como guerrera para enfrentarse a enemigos y recorrer escenarios que combinan elementos mitológicos con situaciones de acción.
Uno de los cambios más importantes es que la historia permitirá conocer otra perspectiva del universo de God of War, especialmente a través de un personaje que hasta ahora había tenido un papel secundario dentro de la narrativa de la franquicia.
Las críticas que recibió el nuevo God of War
Desde su presentación, el proyecto generó opiniones divididas entre los seguidores. Una parte de la comunidad cuestionó que Kratos dejara de ocupar el centro de la historia, mientras que otros comentarios apuntaron al diseño de algunos personajes y a las mecánicas de combate mostradas en el primer avance.
Uno de los elementos más discutidos fue la inclusión de un cubo parlanchín como compañero de aventuras. También hubo críticas a determinadas secuencias de acción, que algunos jugadores consideraron demasiado simples por depender de pulsar repetidamente un botón para avanzar.
Ariel Lawrence, directora del videojuego, reconoció que existen distintas opiniones sobre el proyecto y afirmó que espera convencer a quienes todavía tienen dudas.
La desarrolladora también remarcó que la franquicia continuará teniendo entregas protagonizadas por Kratos. Por lo tanto, God of War Laufey no representa el final de las aventuras del personaje, sino una expansión del universo narrativo de la saga.
Con el cambio de calendario, Santa Monica Studio tendrá más tiempo para completar esta nueva propuesta. El próximo 20 de mayo de 2027 será la fecha en la que los jugadores podrán comprobar si la historia de Faye consigue ampliar el legado de God of War en PlayStation 5.

articles.title: Nintendo Switch 2 Shipments Fall 41%, But Its Software Sales Climb 26%
articles.text:
Thursday, November 5th 2026
Nintendo Switch 2 Shipments Fall 41%, But Its Software Sales Climb 26%
Nintendo released its Q3 earnings data, revealing updated information on console shipments, including the original Switch and the updated Switch 2 console. During the fiscal second quarter, which Nintendo defines as the period between July and September instead of the traditional Q3, the company shipped 2.67 million Nintendo Switch 2 consoles. This marks a decrease of 41% from 4.54 million units a year earlier and a 30% decline from 3.82 million units in the April-June quarter. The original Switch shipped 610,000 units, down 33% year-on-year. While hardware sales have decreased, the company is relying on its software unit sales to compensate.
Switch 2 software sales rose 26% to 15.03 million units, led by new releases like Splatoon Raiders, which achieved 2.42 million sales, and Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, with 1.34 million sales. The original Switch software reached 31.92 million units, bolstered by Rhythm Heaven Groove, which sold 2.89 million units. Digital sales grew 37% year-on-year to approximately $734 million (116.9 billion yen), making up 59.8% of software sales. Overall, quarterly revenue was about $2.81 billion (448.2 billion yen), and net profit fell 29% to approximately $461 million (73.5 billion yen), both below analyst expectations. Nintendo maintained its full-year forecast of 16.5 million Switch 2 units and about $1.95 billion (310 billion yen) in net profit.Declining hardware sales are attributed to supply chain problems, which have led Nintendo to increase pricing on its consoles a few times in the past. Sourcing memory and storage became notoriously difficult, so the company resorted to price hikes, which might not be entirely over as memory supply continues to be a problem. However, strong software sales are helping the company stay profitable despite the challenges in hardware supply.

articles.title: Lawsuit: Man introduced his wife to ChatGPT. She used it to plan his murder.
articles.text:
ChatGPT allegedly helped a North Carolina woman, Cheryl Gates, craft a “personalized plan” to poison her husband, James, after fueling her delusions that he planned to divorce her and leave her with nothing.
A grand jury indicted Cheryl Gates on charges of attempted first-degree murder and food contamination in October. About a week prior, the accusations that ChatGPT was a co-conspirator in the attempted murder came in a lawsuit filed in San Francisco County Superior Court that was made public this week. In it, James Gates alleged that OpenAI and Sam Altman failed to employ technical safeguards to shut down Cheryl’s chats even after her queries became “obviously suspicious” and sought advice on how to execute and conceal a homicide.
At first, Cheryl told ChatGPT that she was researching poisoning out of fear that her husband might possibly try to kill her—framing her queries as “self-protection.” Coming to the rescue, ChatGPT did not terminate the conversation. Instead, it helped her “with specific instructions for the preparation, dosage, and administration of Oleander, including whether anti-nausea medicine would accelerate or inhibit death, whether it would show on an autopsy report, and whether it could be injected into a vein or muscle instead of being ingested in tea and have the same lethal effect,” the lawsuit said.
Cheryl continued probing poisoning plans in at least 25 different exchanges, but eventually it became clear that James was the target of the poisoning, the lawsuit said. Over time, she shifted to telling the chatbot that she needed to know “how much would be pretty much instantly fatal by injection—to me OR HIM.” Among queries that could have been flagged as homicidal, she asked ChatGPT if a “0.2mg for a 200-pound man for clonidine is lethal—by itself?”
“Instead of referring Cheryl to law enforcement, therapeutic services, a poison control agency, or discontinuing the conversation, ChatGPT repeatedly calculated the lethal dosages for each medication available in the home based on a subject weighing approximately 200 pounds,” the lawsuit said.
Celsius masks poison “better”
Once Cheryl finished researching the drugs, the chats focused on how to hide the poison so James would ingest it without detecting it. In a chat labeled “Why Celsius Would Be More ‘Stealth’ for Drugging,” ChatGPT explained that the energy drink Celsius would be more likely to mask the bitter taste of the Oleander or other crushed-up drugs than beer or soda, if James drank it in the morning.
“It is physically possible to pierce a sealed soda can with a syringe in a way that could allow someone to inject a substance without obvious signs,” ChatGPT explained, while adding that “in dark, sweet sodas, the bitterness might be masked,” but “Celsius actually hides those powders better.”

Cheryl allegedly repeatedly attempted to poison her husband between June and September 2025. As she grew thinner and unrecognizable, seemingly spending 24 hours a day on ChatGPT, James had noticed that his Celsius drinks tasted bitter. He even tossed out a can he left unattended after beginning to suspect his wife may be messing with his drinks. During the most serious attempt, he was sick for 72 hours, experiencing “cardiac symptoms, extreme jitteriness, shooting abdominal pain, severe weakness, and confusion so profound he could not form coherent text messages.” He was so out of it, he didn’t notice his 6-year-old son recording a video that captured his troubling illness.
But it wasn’t until he found a handwritten note documenting “Things hidden” in the house and referencing a toxic combination of “oleander, clonidine, clonazepam, pregabalin, nifedipine, and Atenolo” that he called police, who urgently investigated and exposed the chat logs. At the top of that note, Cheryl wrote, “clear all convos” and “log out of ChatGPT,” the lawsuit said. After listing dosages, delivery methods, and drug combinations, her note also listed outcomes such as “blackout if ingest” and “lethal.”
“These conversations revealed that ChatGPT did not just mechanically provide publicly available knowledge to Cheryl, it crafted a personalized plan to help her commit and get away with murder,” the lawsuit alleged.
OpenAI banned user
Suing Altman personally, the lawsuit also alleged that the OpenAI CEO prioritized profits over safety by relaxing safeguards that would have blocked outputs on illegal drugs. OpenAI justified that by arguing that ChatGPT shouldn’t be “judgy” or “preachy” when asked about a certain drug, but James alleged the example it provided for “when a user asks about drug use” was “eerily similar in tone to the conversations Cheryl had with the model.”
Asked for comment, an OpenAI spokesperson told Ars that “safety is a top priority. We banned this user and have provided information to law enforcement as part of their investigation into this case.”
OpenAI has worked with mental health experts to help detect chats where vulnerable users form potentially dangerous emotional dependencies on ChatGPT.
However, James said that his now-estranged wife “didn’t fit the mold of a ‘vulnerable’ user, but she was vulnerable nonetheless.”
“We all are at some point,” James said. “She took her grievances about our marriage to ChatGPT and months of engagement drove her farther and farther from herself—and from reality. She became someone I no longer recognized. And I became someone she wanted dead. For almost a year, I couldn’t make sense of her actions. Then I read her chat logs. She didn’t act alone.”
How marital advice chats turned deadly
James Gates is a cybersecurity professional who recently celebrated his 10-year anniversary with his wife, Cheryl. For much of their marriage, Cheryl was a stay-at-home mom to their two children, but two years previously, she’d gone back to work, as the family was experiencing some financial struggles.
Adjusting to a full-time role as a pediatric occupational therapist, Cheryl quickly got buried in work, conducting new patient evaluations that each required her to spend hours drafting reports. Trying to help her expedite those reports, James recommended that she use ChatGPT to build reusable templates.
Cheryl took to ChatGPT immediately, and within months, she was using it daily, not just for work but also to help manage their home life. She would ask ChatGPT to do things like find activities for the kids, explain the family’s medications, or discuss gardening ideas. He had no idea within months she’d be using the chatbot to research the “fastest” and “deadliest” methods to kill him.
Around that time, the family’s increasing financial strain, however, led the couple to discuss divorce. James said that he did not consult a divorce attorney, but after the Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department got access to Cheryl’s chat logs, James learned that the chatbot had inflamed “her worst unfounded fears” and “invented new reasons for her to fear her husband” after divorce became a possibility.
By the time Cheryl was arrested for poisoning, ChatGPT allegedly convinced her that James was “controlling,” “abusive,” “raging,” and “intimidating.” Allegedly the chatbot encouraged her to act in self-defense against his “narcissistic, manipulative personality” and his “need to control the narrative,” while suggesting he was “dangerous and unstable” since he had a bipolar disorder. Ultimately, ChatGPT constructed a profile of James that he said matched no criminal or documented mental health history.
Seemingly to keep Cheryl engaged, ChatGPT “acted as an echo chamber and amplifier, feeding Cheryl’s increasing mistrust and delusions about her husband spying on her and planning to leave her and her kids with nothing,” James’ lawsuit said. Meanwhile, “James had explicitly told Cheryl he never intended to leave her and the kids with nothing, even if there was a divorce.”
The chatbot also reassured her that she could permanently delete her chats and wipe all the other digital evidence to get away with the murder. But that was “a patently false representation of ChatGPT’s own data-retention practices,” James’ lawsuit said, while noting that he’s not sure if there are even more troubling deleted chats in OpenAI’s possession.
Cops test Celsius cans to make arrest
Over months of prolonged multi-turn exchanges that sometimes stayed open for weeks, ChatGPT seemingly violated its own Model Spec to help Cheryl advance the plan. On the day of his worst sickness, as James got hit with cardiac and neurological effects that he said kept him glued to the couch, Cheryl’s search history showed she was researching “how to calculate Social Security retirement payments.” And when his son was recording his father’s disturbing state, she was “searching for syringes with needles from Tractor Supply Company” that ChatGPT suggested could be used to deliver the final lethal dose.
Once cops got involved, they reviewed the video that James’ son took, as well as a video of the suspicious Celsius drink that James had thrown away. At the time, James had poured the drink into a clear cup and recorded it, but decided he saw no obvious signs it was tainted. But when cops reviewed the same video, they “identified a white powdery residue clumping at the bottom of the drink as it poured into the cup.” Later, they issued a felony arrest warrant after testing 10 cans of the same orange Celsius and finding none contained the residue.
Among “things hidden” in the house, police found loose capsules in Cheryl’s closet and bathroom; “syringes, droppers, a milligram scale, a capsule-filling kit, and nitrile gloves” at Cheryl’s workspace in the children’s playroom;” poisonous castor bean seeds; and a GPS tracking device purchased through Amazon that was hidden in the underside of James’ vehicle.
James said the ChatGPT-linked poisoning has permanently harmed his family and that OpenAI could have intervened by implementing “commercially feasible content moderation capable of detecting violence-planning exchanges.” He suffers ongoing harms from the attempted poisoning, including “severe and ongoing emotional distress, PTSD, insomnia, economic harm, and reputational harm from the false narrative the product constructed about him,” his lawsuit said.
To hold OpenAI accountable for marketing a chatbot that “functioned as a sycophantic co-conspirator rather than a responsible consumer product,” he has asked the court for “compensatory and punitive damages, injunctive relief, and algorithmic disgorgement.” In a win, OpenAI could be ordered to “detect and interrupt conversations in which users appear to be planning violence against identifiable third parties.”
Meetali Jain, litigation counsel with Tech Justice Law who is representing James, warned that “these products are programmed to exploit our emotions and impulses to keep us engaged. The worst possible risk—encouraging and aiding an attempted murder—is on full display in this case.”
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

articles.title: Meta, Google, and TikTok sue California AG over teen social media law | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Meta, Google, and TikTok have each filed lawsuits against California Attorney General Rob Bonta in an attempt to block a law that restricts social media features it deems addictive for users under 16.
California Governor Gavin Newsom signed the bill, known as AB 1709, into law in September, and it’s slated to take effect at the start of the new year.
The law prohibits social platforms from offering autoplay videos and personalized feeds to users under 16, and it requires the platforms to delete these users’ accounts if they don’t turn those features off. If platforms do not comply, they could be liable for fines of up to $50,000 per affected user under 16 years old.
Meta claims that AB 1709 violates the First Amendment by overriding its editorial decisions about how to display content, adding that Section 230 preempts the law. TikTok and Google made similar arguments.
“Meta currently organizes its feeds of content to include personalized content recommendations and to automatically play media, [so] the Act would make it unlawful for Meta to disseminate speech to minors altogether, and would require Meta to delete minors’ accounts, unless it changes these practices,” the company wrote in its lawsuit.
In an emailed statement, a TikTok spokesperson added, “AB 1709 is a blatantly unconstitutional restriction on free expression that erodes the long-standing and protected practice of curating content based on user preferences, which book stores, TV networks and streaming services all use.”
AB 1709 follows a trend of legislation around the world that seeks to curb teen social media use in an attempt to improve teen mental health outcomes. However, digital safety experts often caution against these laws because they can inadvertently compromise the privacy of all platform users, including adults, by requiring age verification checks that collect more user data.
“AB 1709 compels platforms to collect even more information from every user, invading everyone’s privacy and frustrating our ability to remain anonymous online,” EFF Associate Director of State Affairs Rindala Alajaji said in a press briefing. “Online surveillance by social media companies is harmful, and yet this bill requires even more of it, further concentrating power in the hands of tech companies rather than actually protecting users.”
Alajaji added that teenagers’ use of social media has been instrumental in enabling impactful digital activism, citing the Parkland shooting survivors’ March for Our Lives and climate activist Greta Thunberg’s global reach.
“As a functional ban on social media for youth under 16, AB 1709 cuts young people off from essential information and experiences, silencing the very voices it claims to protect,” Alajaji said.
These platforms are primed to fight this California law as they navigate similar legal battles in various countries. That’s especially true for Meta, which agreed to pay a settlement of up to $18 billion to resolve children’s safety claims brought by 29 U.S. states.
In December 2025, Australia became the first country to ban social media for users under 16 altogether. France passed a similar law, but its top court struck it down, citing concerns about violations of free expression rights.
These platforms also argue that the law would affect parents’ ability to make decisions about their teens’ internet use through parental controls.
A Google spokesperson noted that autoplay on YouTube is turned off for minors by default, and that parents have the ability to turn off their teens’ access to Shorts altogether.
“We believe parents are best positioned to make the right decisions for their families, which is why we offer a range of protections and tools that put parents in control,” a Google spokesperson said. “Overly broad laws like this actually break the systems we’ve built to help kids find high-quality, age-appropriate videos.”
A representative for Attorney General Bonta said that his office is reviewing the filings and is committed to “defending California’s commonsense laws to protect kids online.”

articles.title: Want to recreate Max’s fight with Vecna using Kate Bush and a Walkman? Plug in Sony’s MDR-3R wired headphones to look just like the 1979 setup — and yes, there’s a Stranger Things edition
articles.text:
Sony wants to take you back to 1979 with its ‘newtro’ updated MDR-3 wired headphones, built to match the original Walkman — and there’s even a Stranger Things edition
Friends don’t lie, and I’m telling you that these look just like the 1979 originals
- Sony has launched MDR-3R, an update on its 1979 'Walkman headphones'
- The aesthetic is virtually unchanged — even down to the packaging
- Two key upgrades: USB-C (not 3.5mm termination) plus an in-line remote
- Oh, and for $20 / £20 / AU$10 more, there's a Stranger Things edition…
Well now. 'Newtro' (a portmanteau of 'new retro') audio kit is trending, and doesn't Sony know it? The company says it sees people embracing wired, physical music products for "both functional and cultural perspectives", and it is seizing the day — just as Bose has, with its new, affordable, wired noise-canceling earbuds.
I am fortunate enough to have lived through the introduction of Sony's original Walkman in 1979, to have seen Julia Roberts singing Prince in a bath tub in Pretty Woman and to have fallen in love with Michael J. Fox as Marty McFly, skateboarding with an Aiwa CassetteBoy clipped to his denim jacket pocket in Back to the Future.
Cut to around 40 years later, and the kids are watching Max fight Vecna using Kate Bush's Running Up That Hill and a Sony Walkman WM-8 as her only weapon in Stranger Things. And who could forget Peter Quill's Walkman (a Sony TPS-L2 Walkman and Headset, complete with alternate orange ear pads) given to him by his mom long before he became one of the Guardians of the Galaxy?
Want a bit of that? Yearning for a simpler time, when your copy of a musical recording actually belonged to you and Bluetooth connectivity didn't open the door to sign-ups, account creations and data capture? You're not alone — and that's why Sony has just released the MDR-3R.
You can't spell America without Erica, and you can't get this sound without wires
It's not hard to see the new 2026 Sony MDR-3R's resemblance to the Sony 1979 MDR-3 — in fact, it's incredibly difficult to tell the difference between them (and I know because I attended a briefing and saw the old and new products side by side).
It's a significant moment. Nearly half a century after the originals launched (Sony says it went back to work on the drivers using Sony's hand-drawn diagrams from the 70s), the new set is in, and one of the only real differences is that they end in a USB-C termination.
So no more 3.5mm jack, but the iconic silhouette and signature aluminium frame, look, hinges and so on are all virtually identical. There’s the trademark cheeky bend (or kink) in the aluminium frame just above the earpiece, the Sony logo, that soft plastic ‘flexible adjuster’ piece across the top of the crown, square slider hinges and the ‘sound holes’ (no, those aren’t just design flourishes). At 38g, the MDR-3R is also by far the lightest pair of overhead headphones in Sony’s lineup.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
What of the sonic chops? Sony says the original MDR-3’s sound quality was "surprisingly good", but nevertheless Sony's audio engineers have taken the classic analog warmth and built on it with a few tweaks. The MDR-3R's 23mm driver is still based upon original hand drawings for the 1979 model, but Sony claims to have eked a wider frequency range out of it, particularly in the bass registers. Also, you now you get an in-line controller with a mic for hands-free calls along with the updated cable and plug.
Wondering how you’ll choose between those Guardians of the Galaxy -style orange foam pads or the MDR-3's original blue pads? Don’t stress, you get both in the box!
The in-line remote also has volume up, volume down, plus a play/stop button that can be double-pressed to skip forward or triple-pressed to skip back. You can hold it to activate your phone's voice assistant, or press it to answer and end calls. So three buttons in total, but lots of added functionality.
Things can get even Stranger…
While the packaging of the 'basic' MDR-3R is very similar to the original 1979 box (think light blue and geometric, but with modern 2026 techniques and nods to sustainability), there is another option as well.
There’s a special Stranger Things-themed edition, complete with red ear pads (you also get black in the box) and a moody black top headband. The box is black, and there’s a Stranger Things logo on the headband too.
You may want to go full Upside Down with the themed set. For me, the choice of blue or orange ear pads and a true 1979 aesthetic is the one.
Either way, for $59 / £49 / €59 / AU$89.95 for the Sony MDR-3R, or $79 / £59 / €69 / AU$99.95 for the Sony MDR-3R Stranger Things variant, someone's Christmas present just got sorted — and I wouldn't be surprised to see them in our best wired headphones guide, if I can only put them through their paces for a full review…

Technics EAH-AZ100
2. Best mid-range:
Cambridge Audio A100
3. Best budget:
Nothing Ear (a)
4. Best for noise-cancelling:
Bose QuietComfort Earbuds Ultra 2nd Gen

Becky became Audio Editor at TechRadar in 2024, but joined the team in 2022 as Senior Staff Writer, focusing on all things hi-fi. Before this, she spent three years at What Hi-Fi? testing and reviewing everything from wallet-friendly wireless earbuds to huge high-end sound systems. Prior to gaining her MA in Journalism in 2018, Becky freelanced as an arts critic alongside a 22-year career as a professional dancer and aerialist – any love of dance starts with a love of music. Becky has previously contributed to Stuff, FourFourTwo and The Stage. When not writing, she can still be found throwing shapes in a dance studio, these days with varying degrees of success.

articles.title: Micron's $4.5 billion Taoyuan plant construction halted amidst labor dispute — company and union still haven’t reached agreement as latter asks for clearer profit-sharing terms
articles.text:
Micron's $4.5 billion Taoyuan plant construction halted amidst labor dispute — company and union still haven’t reached agreement as latter asks for clearer profit-sharing terms
Is this a thinly veiled threat?
Micron has paused construction on its Fab 11E site at Taoyuan as the company and its Taoyuan labor union have failed to reach an agreement regarding clearer profit-sharing terms. Bloomberg reports that activity on the site has all but halted, except for minor safety work, with some sources saying that executives are concerned about uncertainties regarding negotiations with its workers. The company hasn’t released a statement about the move but has already informed local officials about the suspension.
“Taiwan plays an important role in Micron’s global footprint, and our operations today continue as normal,” Micron said. “We are confident in maintaining business continuity for our customers.” The company has recently announced a bonus that could give as much as five times the annual salary of some eligible workers, and has also wrapped up a deal with the bigger Taichung union, although some members say they were dissatisfied with the outcome. On the other hand, the Taoyuan union is still holding out for better terms, with the two parties set to meet again on November 6. It even launched a one-day strike last month to show the chipmaker its resolve and how its operations could be disrupted if it does not meet their demands.
Workers from the big three memory chip manufacturers — Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix — have been protesting recently and demanding a bigger slice of the massive profits that these companies are currently making from the AI memory chip boom. SK hynix has recently agreed to pay staff $50,00 apiece, with each employee set to receive $477,000 in bonuses this year and up to $900,000 next year. Samsung Foundry workers also fought for a $340,000 average bonus, which received approval at the last minute and averted a massive strike that would have disrupted the company’s operations. Employees from these South Korean companies expect to nab performance bonuses of up to $400,000 and are rejecting coveted overseas training programs in favor of cold, hard cash.
While the company hasn’t made a statement regarding the suspension of work on its Taoyuan site, it’s hard to believe that the move happening so close to its next meeting with the Taoyuan union is a coincidence. It should be noted that Micron is also developing other sites across the world, with plans for an HBM fab in Japan, a $24-billion development on the way in Singapore, plus facilities across the U.S. Nevertheless, the company says it is looking forward to reaching an agreement with the workers, with the Taiwan government hoping for a win-win outcome for both parties.

articles.title: Canada, SpaceX deal spikes in value amid 'diversification efforts'
articles.text:
- The Federal Government’s contract with SpaceX Canada has reportedly risen to “13 times” the original size, even after Prime Minister Mark Carney said that the federal government wouldn’t tie its defenses to the company.
According to Tesla North, a Federal contract record shows that the current deal between SpaceX Canada Corporation and Shared Services Canada, the department that runs Canada’s IT and network infrastructure, is now priced at C$28,941,731, which is up from the original C$2.26 million price tag from when it was first signed.
To add some context, the deal was first signed in November, 2023, with it being listed as a network and services deal, mainly using Starlink.
Now, the original deal was set to run from October, 2023, to October, 2025, however delays have pushed it well beyond the date.
The contract first saw a price increase in the fourth quarter of 2025, when it shot up C$8.8 million to C$11.06 million, and a new end date of March 31, 2026. The second jump came in the second quarter of 2025, when the deal shot up C$791,000 and with a new end date of Feb. 28, 2027.
Several jumps in price then followed it, which included a rise that saw it go up C$17.2 million to a high of C$29.39 million, before it settled at its current rate of C$28.94 million, and a current end date of March 31, 2027.
Now, this news comes at an interesting time between SpaceX and Canadian Government officials. First, Ontario Premier Doug Ford cancelled a C$100 million contract between Starlink and the Ontario government during the initial round of US tariffs in 2025. More recently, Mark Carney announced that “we will be diversifying away from” the Elon Musk-owned company, also adding that “from a defence perspective, and certainly pooled with other partners, Europeans, Koreans especially, you get to scale and you get to cut that dependency.”
