articles.title: Apple MacBook Pro (14-inch, M6) review: Speedy M6 chip slips into comfortable shoes
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
While the base MacBook Pro design is getting a bit tired, Apple’s new M6 chip gives the 14-inch MacBook even more pep in its step.
Reasons to buy
- + M6 continues Apple’s track record of solid year-over-year performance upgrades
- + Wi-Fi 7 finally makes an appearance
- + Impeccable build quality
Reasons to avoid
- - Memory and SSD upgrades are more expensive than ever before
- - Design is starting to look a bit stale after 5 years
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
It’s that time of the year again, which means that Apple has released yet another refreshed 14-inch MacBook Pro using a legacy chassis. While it looks the same as last year’s M5 models on the outside, it has some key hardware upgrades underneath that address performance and connectivity.
This time around, we have a MacBook Pro using the new M6 chip that was first introduced in the refreshed Mac Mini. In addition, Apple has outfitted the MacBook Pro with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity courtesy of the in-house Apple N1 chip.
Thanks to industry-wide price hikes on memory and storage, Apple’s 14-inch MacBook Pro now starts at $1,999.
Design of the MacBook Pro (M6, 14-inch)
Apple has been using the same design for its entry-level MacBook Pro since 2021, and there are no changes this year (if you want a slightly refreshed design, check out the touch screen-enabled 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pros). It’s still a good-looking laptop, but it’s showing its age. Our MacBook Pro review unit came finished in silver instead of space black. While space black looks great, it’s a fingerprint magnet, so many people might prefer the lighter finish, which better hides your skin oils.
The notch at the top of the display now seems archaic, especially after seeing the Dynamic Island on the pricier MacBook Pros. The notch is always staring back at you, even though I have mostly gotten used to it over the years. The main thing going in the notch’s favor is that it resides in the same space as the menu bar, which limits the visual annoyance.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
My only other niggle with the design is one that I’ve harped about in previous MacBook Pro reviews: the cutout in the keyboard deck that aids in lifting the lid has sharp corners, which can jab your palms while typing.
As with previous MacBook Pro generations, you’ll find three Thunderbolt 4 ports (Thunderbolt 5 is not available on M6 models), a full-size SDXC card reader, HDMI 2.1, a 3.5 mm audio jack, and a MagSafe 3 connector.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Our 14-inch MacBook review unit measures 12.31 x 8.71 x 0.61 inches and weighs 3.4 pounds, the same as last year’s model with the M5. For comparison, the Gigabyte Aero X16 measures 14 x 9.9 x 0.78 inches and 4.2 pounds, while the Dell XPS 14 comes in at 12.19 x 8.26 x 0.6 inches and weighs 3 pounds.
MacBook Pro Specifications (M6, 14-inch)
| CPU | Apple M6 (12-core CPU) | 
| Graphics | 12-core GPU (integrated) | 
| Memory | 16GB unified LPDDR5x memory | 
| Storage | 1TB SSD | 
| Display | 14.2-inch Liquid Retina XDR display with Nano-texture option, 3,024 x 1,964, 120 Hz ProMotion | 
| Networking | Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 | 
| Ports | 3x Thunderbolt 4 over USB Type-C, HDMI 2.1, SDXC card slot, 3.5 mm headphone jack, MagSafe 3 | 
| Camera | 12MP Center Stage camera | 
| Battery | 72.4WHr | 
| Power Adapter | 70W | 
| Operating System | macOS Golden Gate 27.0 | 
| Dimensions (WxDxH) | 12.31 x 8.71 x 0.61 inches (312.6 mm x 221.2 mm x 15.1 mm) | 
| Weight | 3.4 pounds (1.55 kg) | 
| Price (as configured) | $1,999.00 | 
Productivity and Graphics Performance on the MacBook Pro (M5, 14-inch)
Our 14-inch MacBook Pro review unit features a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU version of Apple’s new M6 SoC. This is the same configuration as the Mac Mini that we reviewed in September, except that our laptop review unit includes 16GB of unified LPDDR5x memory compared to 24GB. Rounding out the specs is a standard 1TB SSD.
Slow and steady wins the race in silicon advances. In every productivity benchmark, our M6 MacBook Pro not only outshone the previous-generation M5 MacBook Pro, but it also trounced the prosumer Gigabyte Aero X16 (AMD Ryzen AI 7 350) and Dell XPS 14 (Intel Core Ultra X7 358H) Windows 11 laptops that we pitted it against.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Starting out with the Geekbench 6 synthetic CPU benchmark, our M6 review unit put up a modest 10% gain in single-core performance over the M5 (4,752 versus 4,288). Switching to multi-core performance, that performance delta grew to just over 18%. Of the two Windows 11 laptops, the XPS 14 came the closest, putting up single- and multi-core scores of 2,867 and 16,927, respectively.
Apple appears to have held the line when it comes to SSD performance year-over-year. 2025's M5 MacBook Pro managed 1917.35 MBps in our in-house 25GB file transfer test. Things changed little this year, as our M6 MacBook Pro came in at 1914.23 MBps. The Aero X16 carried the baton for the Windows 11 field with a result of 1,480.57 MBps.
Our Handbrake test consists of transcoding a 4K video file to 1080p. The new M6 MacBook Pro review finished the job in a brisk 2 minutes and 50 seconds, while the M5 version took 3 minutes and 31 seconds to complete the task.
Our stress test for productivity laptops centers around Cinebench 2026, which we run 10 times back-to-back, tallying multi-core scores along the way. The M6 MacBook Pro started with a score of 5,026.55 and hovered around 5,440 for the remainder of the runs.
The M5 includes a 12-core GPU (each core features a dedicated neural accelerator), which promises up to a 30 percent uplift in performance compared to the M5.
Although the base MacBook Pro isn’t what we’d consider a gaming beast, it did manage 53.7 frames per second (FPS) at 1800 x 1125 resolution in Cyberpunk 2077 using the “For this Mac” preset and 32.66 FPS at 3024 x 1890. This compares to 47.65 FPS and 31.47 FPS, respectively, for the M5 MacBook Pro.
Display on the MacBook Pro (M6, 14-inch)
Apple’s M6-equipped 14-inch MacBook Pro continues to use an IPS display with mini LED backlighting. As before, you get a 3,024 x 1,964 resolution panel with a 120 Hz refresh rate.
While the mini LED panel looks good, it’s not nearly as capable as the touch-enabled PROLED XDR display found on its pricier siblings. Although you can equip the MacBook Pro with a nano-texture display for $150, our review unit didn’t have it.
Being that I’m a huge fan of Sylvester Stallone’s Rocky films (well, the first four), I pulled up the second trailer for I Play Rocky, which is set to release later this month. The design aesthetic of the film is, of course, distinctly 1970s, and the mini LED panel did a good job of presenting the muted colors (mostly warm earth tones).
As I’m still in shock over the passing of Patrick Stewart, I watched a sizable portion of Star Trek: First Contact on the screen. Again, the display performed well, with major kudos during the opening battle scene where Federation ships are battling the Borg. The orange explosions, red phaser blasts, and the Borg’s green cutting beams vividly danced across the screen. The blackness of space wasn’t quite as deep as I witnessed with an OLED screen side-by-side, but it’s still good.
Our MacBook Pro review unit was even brighter than last year’s model, if only by a slim margin (571.4 nits versus 558 nits). That performance was still well ahead of the OLED panels in the Windows laptops.
Those similarities extended to color performance, which tracked nearly identically to the preceding M5 MacBook Pro, which was a dead ringer for its M4 predecessor. Our instrumented tests showed 81.5 percent coverage of DCI-P3 and 115.1 percent of the sRGB. Although the XPS 14’s OLED panel was no match for brightness (358 nits), it pipped the MacBook Pro in color performance (89.7 percent DCI-P3, 126.6 percent sRGB).
Keyboard and Touchpad on the Apple MacBook Pro (M6, 14-inch)
As with all the other exterior design elements of the M6 MacBook Pro, the keyboard remains unchanged. To me, that’s a good thing, as it’s one of the things I love the most about Apple laptops. As someone who lived through Apple’s horrible butterfly keys on the 12-inch MacBook and subsequent MacBook Pro models, the return to the venerable switches was a return to sanity on Apple’s part.
Apple isn’t the type of company that would equip its laptops with RGB keyboards, so you’ll get single-zone white LED key backlighting. Although the thought of a MacBook Pro with RGB lighting brings a slight smirk to my face, I’m perfectly fine with Apple’s monochromatic approach.
I used the keyhero.com typing test, as I do with all laptops I review, and settled in with 93 words per minute at 95 percent accuracy. Those figures track with what I achieve with other Apple and Windows laptops.
Like all MacBooks (except for the entry-level Neo), our MacBook Pro features a large haptic trackpad that measures 5 x 3 inches. The glass surface makes gliding with your finger or thumb easy-peasy, and the simulated “click” is satisfying.
Audio on the Apple MacBook Pro (M6, 14-inch)
We’re sure you’re noticing a theme in this review, but the audio system in our MacBook Pro review unit remains unchanged compared to its earlier M5 and M4 counterparts. What that means is that you’ll find a six-speaker system that includes support for major audio formats like Dolby Digital, Dolby Atmos, Dolby Digital Plus, and Apple Spatial Audio.
I’m a sucker for acoustic guitar, and one of the greats of the 2000s is John Mayer. Perhaps my favorite John Mayer song is “3x5” from his debut album, which my girlfriend at the time (now wife) and I played over and over again and witnessed several times in concert. On the MacBook Pro’s speakers, the acoustic guitar packs just as much of a punch as John’s breathy vocals pelting out vivid lyrics like, "Today, skies are painted colors of a cowboy cliché."
I got so lost in the audio experience that I found myself listening to the entire Room for Squares album and being transported back to my college days.
Upgradeability of the Apple MacBook Pro (M6, 14-inch)
While most Windows laptops give you some semblance of upgradeability, allowing you to upgrade at the very least storage, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth, and sometimes memory, you’ll find no such luxuries in MacBook land. There are four pentalobe screws on the bottom of the laptop, but once you remove the cover, there’s nothing of note that’s upgradeable. The M6 chip with its integrated 16GB of memory can’t be replaced, nor can the 1TB SSD – both packages are soldered onto the motherboard. As with all MacBooks, you’ll need to settle on how much RAM and storage you want at purchase time. If you get it wrong, you’ll have to live with that config until it’s time to upgrade your laptop again.
Battery Life on the Apple MacBook Pro (M6, 14-inch)
If there’s one thing that you can count on when it comes to MacBooks, it’s battery life. It’s pretty common for MacBooks to last for 18 or more hours in our battery life test, which consists of browsing the web, running OpenGL tests, and streaming video at 150 nits of brightness.
Our MacBook Pro review unit was no exception, lasting 19 hours and 5 minutes thanks to its 72 WHr battery. This was nearly a one-hour improvement over its M5 counterpart, which is a testament to the efficiency gains that Apple is able to achieve with the 2-nanometer process node.
Heat on the Apple MacBook Pro (M6, 14-inch)
We measured skin temperature on the MacBook Pro during our Cinebench 2026 stress test. Unlike the cheaper MacBook Airs, which are fanless, the MacBook Pro’s two internal fans kick into gear quite quickly to dissipate heat.
The hottest point was near the left exhaust vent, which measured 106 degrees Fahrenheit, with 105 F seen between the G and H keys. Given its distance from the toasty parts of the laptop, the touchpad remained cool to the touch at 78 F. The touchpad was much cooler at 82.8 F.
We use TG Pro to measure internal temperatures while running the Cinebench 2026 stress test. While TG Pro doesn’t have full support for the M6 yet, the Power Manager dies reported peak temperatures of 80 degrees Celsius (C) for the SoC. The overall system temperature, which takes an average of several components (i.e., power supply, battery, SSD, logic board, etc.), was 43 degrees C.
Webcam on the Apple MacBook Pro (M6, 14-inch)
The 12MP Center Stage camera that’s been featured in the last two MacBook Pro generations has made a reappearance this year. All of the superlatives that I had for the M5 MacBook Pro are relevant to my current review unit. Namely, image quality was impressive across the board, in both bright and low-light conditions.
Unlike some other laptop webcams that skew my darker skin color or apply smoothing algorithms that make my skin look like a Tootsie Roll, the camera picked up the wrinkles around my eyes and accurately represented the grays in my beard.
Software on the Apple MacBook Pro (M6, 14-inch)
The M6 MacBook Pro ships with macOS 27 Golden Gate preinstalled. You can liken the shift from macOS 26 Tahoe to macOS 27 Golden Gate to the OS X 10.5 Leopard to Mac OS X 10.6 Snow Leopard transition. In other words, macOS 27 is more about making the operating system more reliable and faster rather than bombarding users with new features. You can read more about macOS 27 Golden Gate in my M6 Mac Mini review.
Just like Windows 11, macOS comes with a slew of apps preinstalled upon first boot. Some of the standouts include GarageBand, Apple’s productivity suite (Keynote, Pages, Numbers), Apple TV, iMovie, and Home (Apple’s smart home application). With the exception of Apple TV, the other apps are productivity utilities meant to enhance the user experience and get work done. You won’t find typical bloatware like app/shortcuts for services like Dropbox or antivirus programs like McAfee as you would on Windows 11 laptops.
Apple MacBook Pro (M6, 14-inch) Configurations and Warranty
When opting for the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 processor, you’re looking at a starting price of $1,999. In addition to the M6 processor, you get 16GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD (the configuration of our review unit).
From there, you can opt for 24GB (+$200) or 32AM (+$400) of RAM, and 2TB (+$500) or 4TB (+$1,500) of storage. There are also two standalone options that you can add: the nano-texture display for $150 and a 96-watt power adapter for an extra $20.
The MacBook Pro has a standard one-year warranty. However, you can pick up AppleCare+ for $99.99/year or $9.99/month. The coverage adds unlimited repairs covering accidents, 24/7 priority tech support, and battery replacement.
Bottom Line
When it comes to everything you see on the outside, Apple’s latest 14-inch MacBook Pro is more of the same: same display, same chassis, same keyboard, and the same great build quality. But true to form, Apple has steadily focused on improving performance year-over-year, and we see that again with the new M6 SoC.
You’ll see anywhere from a 10% to 20% uplift across the board, depending on whether you’re dealing with single- or multi-threaded apps. On top of that, efficiency gains have netted nearly an additional hour of battery life over its M5-powered predecessor. And Apple has finally given the MacBook Pro Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0 support.
The M6 MacBook Pro doesn’t have the OLED touchscreen, more svelte design, or Dynamic Island of the all-new MacBook Pros, but it also started at a price that is $900 less than those systems. With that said, the $1,999 price of our review unit is still a lot of money to ask for a laptop featuring just 16GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD. And you don’t even get an OLED screen at that price.
But given the price of memory and storage these days, $1,999 isn’t exactly out of the ordinary. A Dell XPS 14 configured with an Intel Core Ultra 5 325, 16GB of RAM, 1TB SSD, and a 2.8K OLED display is $2,549. We are truly living in unprecedented times, and while it’s hard to reset our expectations concerning the price of tech, the M6 MacBook Pro remains a solid entry in a highly competitive market.
Brandon Hill is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware. He has written about PC and Mac tech since the late 1990s with bylines at AnandTech, DailyTech, and Hot Hardware. When he is not consuming copious amounts of tech news, he can be found enjoying the NC mountains or the beach with his wife and two sons.

articles.title: BMW bumps battery for the better: The 2027 i7 60 xDrive, driven
articles.text:
When BMW debuted the new 7 Series in 2022, it set a new standard for large luxury sedans, increasingly irrelevant though that class is. Rather than siloing off an electric alternative like Mercedes, with its EQS alongside the normal S-Class, BMW simply made the powertrain an option. Stick with a V8 if you want, or consider the rather good electric version instead—only subtle differences like the badging and lack of exhaust pipes give the game away.
Since then, BMW has brought out a string of even newer electric vehicles for the 5 and 3 Series (plus their SUV counterparts). It has switched from battery packs made of prismatic cells to more energy-dense arrangements of cylindrical cells. The motors are still electrically excited synchronous ones, but now the drive units feature silicon carbide inverters and more compact packaging.
This sixth-generation electric powertrain was designed for the clean-sheet Neue Klasse family, which also threw out the legacy cruft of dozens and dozens of discrete single-function electronic control units for a handful of powerful domain controllers. These computers take over those functions but with much faster processing power—and therefore more capabilities in terms of chassis control or powertrain efficiency—as well as the ability to be more easily updated.
Which could have left BMW with something of a problem—should the flagship be clearly outclassed in terms of power and energy density and range efficiency by, well, all the other EVs in the range? Clearly, the board decided the answer to that was no, and for the 7 Series’ midlife update, the i7 got some comprehensive surgery under the skin.
6th-gen power
Compared to the last i7 I drove, the 2027 model boasts a higher-capacity battery pack, now 112.5 kWh (net) up from 101.7 kWh, although BMW stuck with a 400 V architecture, unlike in the Neue Klasse or the iX5 we recently drove. A less-powerful 50 xDrive and a more powerful M70 xDrive will also be available, but at the first drive, I sampled the midrange 60 xDrive model, which features a combined 544 hp (400 KW) and 549 lb-ft (745 Nm), roughly equivalent to the pre-facelift car.

articles.title: MacBook Pro and iMac M6 are incredibly efficient
articles.text:
I’ve been using the M6 iMac and M6 MacBook Pro for about a week (though I had to take the past couple of days off to use the M5 MacBook PROLED XDR), and I’ve liked them both. Though I mostly spent my time with the MacBook Pro.
I tested the MacBook Pro 14-inch M6 12C/12C 16GB 1TB in Space Black and the iMac M6 12C/12C 16GB 512GB in Green. I liked the look of both of them, especially the Pro 14-inch in Space Black. The typing experience is great with decent key travel, and the Magic Trackpad is very responsive, so it was very easy to switch from my MacBook Air.
I didn’t like how heavy the M6 MacBook Pro was. The MacBook Pro is almost a pound heavier than my M4 MacBook Air, and yes, it’s obvious that the Air would be lighter than the Pro, but I definitely wasn’t ready for just how much heavier the Pro feels. Even the M5 Max PROLED was noticeably lighter than the MacBook Pro M6.
Bumpin’ speakers
I was really impressed by the laptop’s speakers. Music was crystal clear and very loud, easily filling my bedroom. And even with my bedroom door closed, I could still hear it from my living room about 20 feet away, though it wasn’t too loud to interrupt my roommate while he was watching TV. The device has a six-speaker sound system, so watching anime was impactful with the speaker and combined with the nano-texture display, it made the experience great.
Speaking of the nano-texture display, this was my first one (besides the iPhone Duo) and I really liked it. It creates an anti-glare experience, so I didn’t have issues using the laptop in my backyard on the one sunny day we had (winter is coming), and I like how videos and pictures look. It’s no PROLED screen — I definitely missed that device’s screen and Dynamic Island when I switched to the M6, but you’re not paying nearly as much.
Cool to the touch
I like that the M6 felt cool to the touch most of the time, it was very comfortable to keep on my lap. If I was watching anime, working on articles, or even editing photos, the M6 kept cold the whole time. I played Control with ray-tracing and 120Hz turned on, and the device got pretty warm after about 10 minutes. It was nice that it cooled down pretty quickly after I stopped gaming, though.
Speaking of games, the M6 handled Slay the Spire and Control without any problems, besides warming up. Both games looked great with ProMotion turned on, and I liked that there wasn’t any slowdown even though the graphics were turned up a bit.
The speed at which both open apps is great, and downloads are very quick as well. My partner has gotten into designing stickers that he can iron on clothes to add a bit more of his taste to his outfits. He’s been using the M6 iMac with XTool software to create his designs, and he said that the software booted up quickly, there were no issues loading up big projects either, and he noticed that everything flowed quicker than my M4 MacBook Air.
Another thing that’s nice about the M6 iMac is that it’s always there and ready for you. My last iMac had an Intel chip (the 2019 version!), and it would take a moment to boot up. However, the M6 iMac boots up instantly, and you’re right back into what you were doing before.
Battery life on the M6 MacBook Pro is great, lasting me an entire workday, and Fast Charging is a big win, getting me up to 50 per cent in about 35 minutes. I tend to never keep my laptop on the charger, so it was nice that even when I prematurely removed it from the charger, I didn’t have to worry about battery life.
More to come…
It’s only been a week with the M6 MacBook Pro and the M6 iMac, and I spent a few of those days under the weather, so I definitely need to put both of them through their paces some more. But as I use each of the new Apple devices, I’ll report back. I definitely want to try some vibe coding with the M6 MacBook Pro and will definitely need to do some video editing over the next couple of weeks to see how well the M6 performs under some harder pressure.
The M6 MacBook Pro starts at $2.799, while the M6 iMac starts at $2,099, and both come out on November 6.

articles.title: Airbnb says it's launching an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Airbnb has teased its plans to build its own AI travel agent before, but on Thursday the company announced that the new AI feature will launch in the first half of 2027. In the company’s Q3 shareholder letter on Thursday, Airbnb also provided more detail about how the agent will work, what it will actually do, and how it’s different from a typical AI chatbot.
In prior interviews, CEO Brian Chesky sketched out the travel company’s approach to AI, describing a plan to build an AI agent that has a richer interface than a conventional chatbot. He also expressed his opinions about how chatbots aren’t the right interface for travel, noting that people take pleasure in the planning process and in anticipating a trip. Any agent that it built, then, shouldn’t take away from the inspiration and the browsing, he told TechCrunch in an interview last month.
Chesky today reiterated that belief, telling analysts on the earnings call that people won’t use one AI agent for everything.
“Today’s AI agents like Muse and Instinct are good at simple routine tasks like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment. But planning a trip is different,” he said. “Travel is aspirational. Discovering where to go and where to stay is part of the experience. In fact, 80% of travelers say they enjoy spending time researching trips. People want to look at photos. They want to compare homes. They want to make decisions with people they’re traveling with,” he continued. “And I don’t think the general-purpose agents are the best to do that. So that is why we are building our own AI agent,” Chesky said.
Airbnb described its agent as having a personalized interface that’s designed specifically for travel, where it will “build an interface” around a user’s question instead of simply responding as a chatbot would.
“What we are doing is developing a custom-designed AI-native experience that responds to what guests are looking for,” Chesky said. “So instead of relying on traditional chat alone, which is very text-heavy — which, again, is definitely not the way you should plan travel, our agent draws from a library of hundreds of travel-specific interface components — maps, photos, comparisons, calendars, itineraries — and composes them in real time to match what they’re looking for.”
The exec said the agent will feel “a little bit like generative UI” as it’s designed to offer up “the right interface at the right time” for someone’s specific travel needs.
In its shareholder letter, the company touted that its nearly 20 years of experience in bringing hosts and guests together is informing how the agent is built, as it incorporates insights about how people both book and host on its platform. The agent will also be able to help travelers beyond the booking itself.
“Our agent will be able to help guests throughout their trip — from changing a reservation or resolving a payment issue to getting help with refunds, rebooking, or 24-hour safety support. These are things an outside agent can’t easily do on its own,” the company wrote.
Over time, Airbnb expects the agent will be able to help travelers with other aspects of their trip, including not only homes and hotels, but also services and experiences. Services and experiences are two areas that have become a bigger focus for the company following its redesign last year.
While the company previously said to expect its AI agent sometime in the next year, it’s now more specifically committing to roll out the new technology to consumers in the first half of 2027.
The news of the agent’s release was delivered alongside strong third-quarter earnings, with revenue growing 19% to $4.87 billion, topping Wall Street estimates. It also raised its 2026 revenue growth forecast, which it now predicts will be in the high teens, instead of the mid-teens.
“Airbnb is back in growth mode,” Chesky told analysts on the Q3 earnings call on Thursday. “It’s rare for a marketplace of our size to reaccelerate growth, but that’s exactly what we’re doing. Q3 was our fastest revenue growth in more than three years,” he added.

articles.title: Laser statt Funk: Griechischer Satellit schickt Daten per Lichtstrahl zur Erde
articles.text:
Laser statt Funk: Griechischer Satellit schickt Daten per Lichtstrahl zur Erde
Griechenland hat eine optische Datenverbindung aus dem All zur Erde in Betrieb genommen. Der Satellit Ermis-3 stellte aus einer niedrigen Erdumlaufbahn eine Laserverbindung zur Bodenstation HolOGS-1 auf dem Berg Holomondas in Nordgriechenland her. Dabei handelte es sich zunächst um einen Test.
Das Projekt wird von der Europäischen Raumfahrtagentur ESA unterstützt. Ermis-3 ist ein sogenannter 8U-Cubesat, also ein würfelförmiger Kleinsatellit aus acht standardisierten Modulen. Laut ESA kam die Verbindung schnell zustande. Damit sei eines der Hauptziele der Mission erreicht: das präzise Ausrichten, Erfassen und Verfolgen des Ziels, in der Fachsprache „Pointing, Acquisition, Tracking“.
Technik aus mehreren europäischen Ländern
Bei dem Test kam ausschließlich europäische Technik zum Einsatz. Den im März 2026 gestarteten Ermis-3 entwickelte die National and Kapodistrian University in Athen, das Bodenterminal stammt von der Aristoteles-Universität in Thessaloniki. Die Übertragungstechnik lieferte das litauische Unternehmen Astrolight. Getestet wurden die Systeme am Europäischen Raumfahrtforschungs- und Technologiezentrum ESTEC der ESA in den Niederlanden.
ESA-Manager Frederic Rouesnel sagte, das Ergebnis zeige, dass Europa durch die Zusammenarbeit von Industrie, Wissenschaft und Institutionen Innovationen hervorbringen könne. Die ESA habe Programmmanagement, technische Überwachung und ingenieurtechnische Unterstützung beigesteuert.
Hohe Datenrate, aber anspruchsvolle Technik
Bei der optischen Kommunikation überträgt ein Laser die Daten. Der Vorteil: Die Datenrate liegt deutlich über der von herkömmlichem Funk. Dafür ist das Verfahren aber komplizierter: Der Satellit rast mit mehreren tausend Kilometern pro Stunde um die Erde und muss den Laserstrahl dabei exakt auf den Empfänger richten.
Das Zeitfenster für die Verbindung ist zudem kurz. Hinzu kommt das Wetter: Wolken können die Verbindung blockieren, Turbulenzen in der Atmosphäre verschlechtern die Signalqualität. Dennoch verspricht die Technik neue Impulse für souveräne Drahtlosverbindungen auf der Erde.

articles.title: Xbox rediseña su app para PC, que ahora es más simple y hasta un 60 % más rápida
articles.text:
Xbox acaba de presentar una muy interesante renovación de su app para PC. El cliente nativo de la plataforma para Windows no solo estrena un nuevo diseño que la hace mucho más simple y ágil de navegar, sino que también introduce mejoras notorias en su rendimiento, algo que los usuarios llevaban algún tiempo reclamando.
El lavado de cara que ha recibido la app de Xbox para PC es notorio. La división de gaming de Microsoft ha implementado un diseño más limpio, que incluye una mejor navegación de la biblioteca de juegos. También se han optimizado los filtros y la gestión de los títulos disponibles.
Pero no todos los cambios son meramente estéticos. A partir de ahora, la app de Xbox para PC incorpora un buscador unificado, que ahora muestra resultados para juegos, complementos, personas y más. Lo último se vincula con un enfoque más social que hace que el acceso a los amigos sea más directo, permitiendo ver quiénes están jugando (y a qué) o iniciar un chat directamente desde la interfaz principal.
El nuevo diseño se ve interesante y se verá reflejado, asimismo, en la versión web de Xbox y en las apps para jugar desde la nube en cascos de realidad virtual y televisores. Pero no todo se relaciona con una actualización de apariencia, pues hay cambios importantes tras bambalinas.
La app de Xbox para PC por fin mejora su rendimiento de forma drástica
Si llevas algún tiempo usando la app de Xbox para PC, seguramente te has dado cuenta de que su rendimiento no siempre ha sido el mejor. El cliente no siempre ha sido el más ágil para sacar provecho de los recursos del ordenador, aunque eso ahora promete cambiar con esta actualización.
Microsoft dice que su nueva app de Xbox se inicia hasta un 60 por ciento más rápido que la versión para PC previa. A esto hay que agregarle que las ventanas dentro del software se muestran hasta un 65 % más rápido, mientras que la pantalla de inicio, la tienda y el apartado de Game Pass se cargan hasta un 50 % más veloz.
Por supuesto que será potestad de los usuarios poner a prueba los datos que presume la firma de Redmond, aunque muchos todavía tienen que esperar para probarla. De momento, la app rediseñada para PC se ha puesto a disposición únicamente de los miembros del programa Xbox Insider. Así que si todavía no te has enrolado, tendrás que aguardar algún tiempo más antes de poder usarla.

articles.title: Spacetech startup Cosmoserve raises $6M in seed round
articles.text:
Spacetech startup Cosmoserve raises $6M in seed round
Cosmoserve also opened a facility in Hyderabad which will be utilised for satellite servicing and space debris recovery.
Cosmoserve Space, a Hyderabad-based spacetech startup, has raised $6 million in a seed round of funding from Rebright Partners of Japan, Aranya Holdings, and Naandi Ventures.
The round also saw participation from existing investors AUM Ventures and Shakti VC. This funding round has seen Cosmoserve raising over $9 million.
Cosmoserve also inaugurated Base 1 - a facility to design, build, test and operate systems for satellite servicing and space debris recovery. A statement said, this facility will have an orbital rendezvous and capture lab to simulate spacecraft capture operations, a space robotics innovation Lab to develop robotic capture systems; a clean room for satellite integration, a mission simulation and control Centre to manage upcoming missions.
“In our first year we have flown our first payload on an Indian rocket, raised our seed round, and today we open a facility where we can design, build, test and fly our missions under one roof. Debris is becoming the limiting factor for every nation's space ambitions, including India's. Base 1 is where we build the capability to keep orbits usable, for Gaganyaan, the Bharatiya Antariksh Station and every satellite that follows,” said Chiranjeevi Phanindra, Founder & CEO of Cosmoserve Space.
Beyond removing space debris, the company said the facility will support satellite servicing, including in-orbit repairs and refuelling. Cosmoserve currently sources close to 60% of its mission components locally. The company aims to develop more critical technologies in-house through Base 1 and strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities.
According to the spacetech startup, space debris is one of the biggest challenges facing the global space industry. Of the approximately 28,000 satellites in orbit, nearly 10,000 are dead or non-operational.
Beyond these inactive satellites, Earth's orbit is crowded with an estimated 68,000 debris objects. Even fragments can pose serious risks to operational satellites, spacecraft and missions such as the International Space Station (ISS), given the high speeds at which they travel.

articles.title: Exclusive: StrongestLayer launches tools to verify payment requests and block hidden AI instructions - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: StrongestLayer launches tools to verify payment requests and block hidden AI instructions
Artificial intelligence email security startup StrongestLayer Inc. today launched two products aimed at email that can move money or manipulate an AI assistant.
The first product, Intent Workflows, can hold payment, payroll and executive account requests for verification before anyone acts on them. Alongside it comes AI Instruction Intercept, which stops hidden instructions in a message before an assistant such as Microsoft Corp.’s Microsoft 365 Copilot reads them
Intent Workflows targets attacks that carry no malware or suspicious link. In vendor email compromise, a criminal takes over a real supplier’s mailbox and sends new bank details inside an existing thread.
StrongestLayer went through 32,052 attacks that got past existing defenses at 45 organizations in the second quarter. Only 3.6% were payment or bank-change requests. Under a loss model built on the Factor Analysis of Information Risk framework, that small slice accounted for more than 98% of the estimated financial exposure. Sender authentication checks were little help, since 94% of those messages passed them.
Traditional email security asks whether a message looks bad, according to Alan LeFort, StrongestLayer’s co-founder and chief executive. “The costliest attacks are built to look fine,” he said. His company looks at what a message is trying to make happen, which for a wire transfer means “verifying the action instead of betting on a verdict.”
StrongestLayer’s detection still screens every message. Intent Workflows adds a hold for the smaller set of requests that can’t be reversed, with each customer deciding whether those requests wait for verification or go to the security team or a process owner.
Customers can also let a request through with a policy banner, which appears only on tracked requests and spells out the company’s own rule, such as “Bank change: call the number on file.” Payments in scope are held whatever the verdict, so a hijacked vendor account can’t get one through by sounding legitimate.
The software compares each payment request with the payee’s history, and customers pick the threshold, whether that is every payment or only those over $5,000. If nothing has changed, the payment owner confirms in one click, in Microsoft Teams or by email. Any change, or a new vendor, means a call to a phone number already on file, and the email isn’t released until the outcome is logged.
Payroll changes are verified the same way, and executive password, multifactor authentication and account recovery resets go to the identity or security team first, even when the request comes in through the help desk.
The release also takes on a newer problem. Researchers at Aim Security Ltd. found the EchoLeak flaw in Microsoft 365 Copilot last year, and one crafted email was all it took to get the assistant leaking data.
AI Instruction Intercept reads each message first. A reasoning model checks it for hidden instructions against the customer’s own business context, and only after that does the email reach Copilot, Google LLC’s Gemini or a security classifier. Suspect messages are quarantined by default with an explanation of what each instruction was after.
Email is the one route to an AI assistant that “any outsider can use,” said Joshua Bass, StrongestLayer’s co-founder and chief product officer. He argues the inbox is the first place to stop prompt injection, since all an attacker needs is an address.
Both products are available now for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace and run alongside a company’s existing email security.

articles.title: Für GTA 6: Playstation 5 jetzt kaufen – oder lieber bis zum Black Friday warten?
articles.text:
Für GTA 6: Playstation 5 jetzt kaufen – oder lieber bis zum Black Friday warten?
Fast genau 13 Jahre nach dem Start der PC-Version von GTA 5 wird Rockstar am 19. November den Nachfolger GTA 6 veröffentlichen. Doch diesmal läuft beim Release einiges anders. So wird es zum Stichtag keine PC-Fassung geben. Stattdessen kommt das Open-World-Game zunächst für die Xbox und die Playstation 5 heraus. Gamer:innen könnte das vor Probleme stellen. Nicht jeder hat schließlich eine Konsole zu Hause. Für den begehrten Titel kann sich die Anschaffung natürlich lohnen.
Die Frage ist nur: Wann ist der beste Zeitpunkt? Denn rund eine Woche nach der Veröffentlichung des Spiels findet am 27. November der Black Friday statt – auch wenn einige Händler wieder vorab mit längeren Angebotszeiträumen werben dürften. Lohnt sich also das Warten auf einen guten Deal? Das wollten wir wissen und haben uns die Zahlen aus dem Vorjahr angeschaut und bei zwei Preisportalen nachgefragt. Weil die Playstation 5 hierzulande unter anderem laut einer Erhebung von Idealo deutlich gefragter ist, als die Xbox, haben wir uns dabei auf die Varianten der Sony-Konsole beschränkt.
Werden Konsolen zum Black Friday günstiger?
Sowohl Idealo als auch Guenstiger.de haben bereits eigene Auswertungen zur möglichen Ersparnis am Black Friday veröffentlicht. Für seine Erhebung hat Idealo 10.000 Produkte von Oktober bis Dezember 2025 beobachtet. Guenstiger.de hat sich auf 300 Produkte beschränkt und Black-Friday-Aktions- mit Durchschnittspreisen im Oktober 2025 verglichen.
Laut Guenstiger.de können Gaming-Fans durchaus von Black-Friday-Angeboten profitieren. So waren Konsolen im Angebotszeitraum im Schnitt rund zehn Prozent günstiger als noch im Oktober 2025. Dasselbe galt für die zugehörigen Videospiele. Idealo kommt auf andere Werte. Demzufolge seien Rabatte für Spielkonsolen mit im Schnitt vier Prozent eher gering ausgefallen. Umgerechnet betrug die durchschnittliche Ersparnis 21 Euro. Allerdings: Eine genaue Unterteilung nach Modell und Variante haben wir bei Vergleichsplattformen nicht vorgenommen. Um herauszufinden, was das für die PS5 bedeutet, muss man also genauer hinschauen.
Laut Idealo ist der durchschnittliche Preis der Playstation 5 in der Standard- und Digital-Edition und der PS5 Pro im November 2025 jeweils nur um wenige Euro gefallen. Die Standard-Edition ohne dünnes Gehäuse ist sogar um zehn Euro im Preis gestiegen. Deutlich günstiger waren die Konsolen demnach im Angebotszeitraum rund um Weihnachten im Dezember. Hatte die dünne Digital-Edition im November noch rund 405 Euro im Schnitt gekostet, sank der Preis im Dezember auf 349 Euro. Die Standard-Edition kostete im Dezember im Schnitt 490,50 Euro (Vormonat: 519,99 Euro), die dünnere Standard-Edition 438,90 Euro (statt 476,95 Euro) und die Pro 679 Euro (statt 711,99 Euro).
Guenstiger.de sah die Playstation 5 Slim auf Nachfrage im Oktober 2025 bei 490 Euro. Betrachtet wurde dabei der Durchschnitt der besten Preise pro Tag. Zum Black Friday sei die Konsole dann ab 429 Euro angeboten worden. Schade: Die Preisentwicklung aus dem Vorjahr bis heute lässt sich auf der Plattform nicht nachprüfen. Die Verlaufskurve reicht maximal sechs Monate zurück.
Warum es bei der Playstation 5 in diesem Jahr knifflig wird
Was sich aber schon jetzt vermuten lässt: Die Preise von 2025 werden die diversen Varianten der PS5 eher nicht wieder erreichen. Das liegt vor allem daran, dass Sony im April 2026 als Reaktion auf die Chipkrise die Preise für seine Konsolen weltweit erhöht hat. In Deutschland sind die Varianten seitdem im Sony-eigenen Shop jeweils 100 Euro teurer. Auch etablierte Elektronikhändler wie Mediamarkt und Saturn haben hier mittlerweile nachgezogen und bieten etwa die Digital-Edition genau wie der Hersteller selbst für rund 600 Euro an.
Idealo hat ebenfalls steigende Preise im Jahresvergleich erkannt. Im Vergleich zum Durchschnittspreis im Oktober sind die Preise für die Konsolen wie folgt angestiegen:
- Playstation 5 Standard-Edition: rund 240 Euro (oder 47 Prozent)
- Playstation 5 Slim Standard-Edition: rund 165 Euro (oder 34 Prozent)
- Playstation 5 Slim Digital-Edition: rund 180 Euro (oder 43 Prozent)
Abseits von der Preiserhöhung sorgt natürlich auch GTA 6 selbst für eine hohe Nachfrage nach der Konsole. Diese gibt Händlern keinen Anlass dazu, jetzt die Preise zu senken.
Einen noch größeren Ausreißer stellt die Playstation 5 Pro dar. Sie ist um rund 610 Euro im Preis gestiegen. Das ist ein Plus von 84 Prozent. Tatsächlich ist die Konsole vielerorts vergriffen und nur auf Online-Marktplätzen für horrende Preise jenseits der 1.000 Euro zu bekommen. Die Verkäufer erhoffen sich offenbar, dass Fans, die auf den Release von GTA 6 hinfiebern, diese Beträge schon zahlen werden, um das Spiel auf Sonys leistungsstärkster Konsole zu spielen. Mit Besserung bei der Versorgung ist offenbar erst 2027 zu rechnen. Das berichtet Playfront. Das deutsche Magazin hatte nach eigenen Angaben im September 2026 ein Memo des Herstellers an Händler vorliegen.
    „Eine verlässliche Empfehlung, ob sich der Kauf jetzt oder erst zum Black Friday mehr lohnt, ist daher schwierig.“
Und am Black Friday 2026? Da sind mögliche Angebote nicht komplett ausgeschlossen. Immerhin liegt der Termin ja nach dem Release von GTA 6. Doch Experten dämpfen die Erwartungen: „Dass es zum Black Friday tatsächlich günstigere Angebote geben wird, ist angesichts der Gesamtsituation aber eher unwahrscheinlich“, erklärt Florian Kriegel von Idealo. „Eine verlässliche Empfehlung, ob sich der Kauf jetzt oder erst zum Black Friday mehr lohnt, ist daher schwierig.“
Bei Guenstiger.de sieht man ebenfalls steigende Preise, rät Sparfüchsen aber, die eine Woche bis zum Angebotszeitraum noch abzuwarten. „Die aktuelle Preiskurve zeigt einen starken Anstieg, daher würde ich raten, bis Black Friday zu warten beziehungsweise in der Black Week wachsam zu sein“, erklärt Nicole Berg, Head of Communications bei der Preisplattform, per Mail. „Auf jeden Fall sollte man jetzt schon einen Preisalarm einstellen, da manche Händler ja schon sehr früh mit Aktionen starten.“
Playstation 5 nur für GTA 6? Dann sollte es diese sein
Selbst die Experten sind sich also nicht einig, was die beste Strategie beim Kauf der Playstation 5 ist. Wollt ihr die Konsole sicher zum Start von GTA 6 haben, um an Tag 1 loszuzocken, dann lohnt sich derzeit wohl vor allem ein Blick auf die dünne Digital-Edition. Die ist mit rund 600 Euro derzeit die günstigste Variante der PS5. Und ob mit oder ohne Box: GTA 6 gibt es ohnehin nur als Download ohne Disc. Eine Konsolenvariante mit Laufwerk braucht ihr also nicht. Sollte sich das einmal ändern, könnt ihr nachträglich das passende Blu-ray-Laufwerk dazukaufen.
Wer das Spiel nicht sofort spielen will, kann den kurzen Zeitraum bis zum Black Friday aber auch abwarten. Im besten Fall gibt es ein günstiges Angebot oder ein Bundle, das für euch infrage kommt. Die Finger solltet ihr dagegen von der Playstation 5 Pro lassen, solange die Konsole nicht vorrätig ist und deutlich mehr als den von Sony aufgerufenen Preis kostet.

articles.title: Free vient de déployer une nouvelle mise à jour de sécurité pour les Freebox, qu'il faut rapidement installer
articles.text:
L'opérateur Free a déployé, jeudi dans la matinée, une mise à jour du Freebox Server destinée aux Freebox Revolution, Pop, Delta et Ultra, avec un accent mis sur la sécurité.
Une nouvelle mise à jour des Freebox, version 4.13.3, est disponible depuis ce jeudi 5 novembre à 10 heures, et Free garde ses habitudes en matière de sécurité. Des correctifs sont apportés, sans plus de détails. Cette dernière mise à jour arrive tout juste deux semaine après la 4.13.2, au terme d'une rentrée qui a sérieusement remanié le Wi-Fi des box de l'opérateur. Pour en profiter, mieux vaut pousser manuellement l'installation.
Free enchaîne les mises à jour de sécurité sur ses Freebox
La version 4.13.3 du Freebox Server concerne les Freebox Revolution, Pop, Delta et Ultra. En évoquant des « correctifs de sécurité », le détail de la mise à jour de Free tient en quelques mots. L'opérateur ne nomme aucune faille, et c'est de bonne guerre, puisque détailler une vulnérabilité avant que tout le parc soit à jour reviendrait à donner une carte au trésor aux pirates. Sur l'application Free, l'opérateur évoque un « renforcement de la sécurité et de la protection du système ».
Cette version succède à la 4.13.2, sortie le jeudi 22 octobre dernier. Avant, la rentrée avait surtout profité au Wi-Fi. Le 16 septembre, la 4.13.0 rendait les canaux DFS utilisables même en présence de répéteurs. La bande 5 GHz pouvait passer de 80 à 160 MHz, ce qui double le débit théorique. Cinq jours plus tard, la 4.13.1 corrigeait un problème rare dans le choix de la liaison entre les répéteurs et le Server.
Mettre à jour sa Freebox, plusieurs façons d'appuyer sur le bon bouton
À tous les Freenautes distraits, sachez que votre box n'installera rien tant qu'elle n'aura pas redémarré, et c'est à vous de déclencher l'opération. Le plus rapide reste de passer par l'application Free, qui a absorbé Freebox Connect il y a quelques mois. Une fois ouverte, rendez-vous dans vos équipements Freebox, touchez « Serveur internet », puis « Version logicielle » et « Mettre à jour ».
Si vous le souhaitez, vous pouvez directement passer par la box, en utilisant les flèches du Server qui mènent au menu « Redémarrage ». Pour vérifier la version installée sur l'écran du boîtier, passez par « Informations avancées » puis « Version » sur Pop et Ultra, par « Version » sur Delta, ou par « Système » puis « Version » sur Revolution.

articles.title: FBI, CISA warn of cyberattacks targeting refrigeration systems
articles.text:
The FBI and CISA warn that hackers are actively targeting industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems worldwide, potentially causing food spoilage, equipment damage, and fire hazards.
The warning was issued jointly with the U.S. Departments of Health and Human Services (HHS), Agriculture (USDA), and Transportation (DOT), urging critical infrastructure operators to secure vulnerable refrigeration controllers used in healthcare, food production, chemical facilities, and transportation.
"Every organization that depends on refrigeration and monitoring systems should assume it could be a target," said Chris Butera, CISA's Acting Executive Assistant Director for Cybersecurity.
According to a joint advisory published Thursday, attackers are exploiting weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible electronic temperature controllers and commercial refrigeration management systems.
These devices allow operators to monitor temperatures remotely, manage defrost cycles, and control cooling equipment.
"Globally, malicious cyber actors are targeting vulnerabilities and weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible electronic temperature controllers and commercial refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities," CISA warned.
The agencies say attackers may exploit authentication bypass vulnerabilities, arbitrary code injection flaws, or weak configurations to modify temperature settings and force refrigeration equipment into continuous heating or defrost cycles.
Successful attacks can cause inventory losses, reduce equipment lifespan, create fire hazards, and create unsafe storage conditions. Attackers may also reduce visibility into current temperatures, preventing operators from detecting problems.
The warning follows a series of attacks against European refrigeration systems that have disrupted supermarkets and blood storage facilities.
In October, hackers compromised refrigeration controllers at an estimated 250 to 350 French supermarkets, remotely activating defrost functions and raising temperatures in refrigerators and freezers.
A second wave of attacks reported in November affected more than 115 stores across six European countries, with some refrigeration systems shutting down entirely and others raising temperatures to as high as 50°C (122°F).
On November 3, the French Blood Establishment (EFS) confirmed that a cybersecurity incident affecting a refrigeration equipment provider had altered temperature and defrost settings at three facilities used to store blood products.
In response to the ongoing threat, the U.S. agencies are urging organizations to remove refrigeration controllers from the public internet, secure necessary remote access, change default passwords, and apply available security updates.
They also recommend isolating operational technology systems from business networks and enforcing safe temperature limits to prevent controllers from operating outside acceptable ranges.

articles.title: Adif usa maquinistas y trenes comerciales con pasajeros para confirmar ciertos fallos en las vías
articles.text:
Se suponía que las del 29N iban a ser las elecciones de la crisis de la vivienda, el tema que lleva meses encabezando el ranking de principales preocupaciones de los españoles y que, tras un intenso culebrón parlamentario, precipitó el adelanto electoral. Tras la tragedia de Urda ya no está tan claro. La gestión de la infraestructura ferroviaria de alta velocidad (AV) lleva una semana acaparando el debate público. Eso explica que la última exclusiva de ABC haya generado expectación: el diario ha revelado una directriz interna de Adif que anima a utilizar trenes comerciales para certificar incidencias en las vías.
Dicho de otro modo (y de forma resumida), cuando se detecta una pequeña anomalía en la red de AV no se moviliza necesariamente a los técnicos. En ocasiones, antes debe comprobarla el siguiente convoy que circule por la zona.
¿Qué ha pasado? Que Borja Méndez firma hoy una crónica en ABC en la que revela un protocolo de Adif que hasta ahora había pasado inadvertido: la Ficha Específica LAV2 prevé que cuando se detecte una alteración leve en la red de AV deba ser el siguiente maquinista que pase por la zona quien lo confirme.
Es decir, Adif no tiene por qué cortar el tramo de forma automática y alertar a los técnicos de mantenimiento al instante. Antes puede recurrirse a otro convoy comercial (con su personal y pasajeros) a modo de inspector in situ, una especie de ‘banco de pruebas’ que sirve para descartar falsas alarmas.
¿Qué dice exactamente la orden? La directriz de Adif es clara. Cuando un maquinista detecta una anomalía de “repercusión débil” en una vía, el administrador ferroviario no tiene por qué adoptar una respuesta inmediata que pase por suspender el tráfico en el tramo ‘sospechoso’.
El protocolo es otro: se encarga al siguiente maquinista que pase por la zona que esté atento para comprobar si realmente hay un problema o el aviso de su anterior compañero se debió a otras causas, como un fallo en la suspensión del tren.
¿Qué es una “repercusión débil”? Ahí está la clave. La normativa consultada por ABC, de carácter interno, distingue cuatro escenarios distintos, en función de lo que haya percibido el maquinista que advierte de la anomalía. Hay fallos débiles, moderados, fuertes y muy fuertes.
El protocolo en cuestión se centra en los primeros, los débiles: baches, vibraciones fuera de lo común o sacudidas. Cuando el conductor percibe una anomalía así, el Centro de Control de Tráfico avisa al siguiente maquinista que circule por la zona y le pide que esté atento al comportamiento del tren. El objetivo: corroborar que efectivamente pasa algo en la vía.
Adif utiliza trenes con pasajeros para detectar fallos de «repercusión débil» en las vías @Borjamendez https://t.co/Jr3ygkA1vF
— ABC.es (@abc_es) November 5, 2026
¿Y luego, qué? Cuando se alcanza ese ‘doble check’ sobre el terreno, el escenario cambia. Los trenes adaptan su velocidad (hay diferentes escenarios posibles) y una vez confirmada la sospecha se moviliza a los técnicos. La directriz de Adif deja claro que ese paso no es estrictamente necesario “hasta que [la incidencia] sea confirmada por las circulaciones siguientes”. Como recoge Méndez en su crónica, no todos los profesionales comparten esa forma de proceder, que básicamente utiliza trenes comerciales (con pasajeros a bordo) para confirmar anomalías en la infraestructura.
¿Por qué es importante? Aunque 2026 está siendo un año trágico para el ferrocarril, con dos siniestros en menos de 10 meses (Adamuz y Urda) que suman 115 víctimas mortales y decenas de heridos, no abundan los accidentes de esa gravedad en la historia de la AV española. Y eso habla de sus protocolos.
El problema es el enfoque del protocolo analizado por ABC: su idea de fondo es priorizar la agilidad del tráfico ferroviario para evitar incidencias. Y eso es importante si se tiene en cuenta que el gestor debe compaginar dos valores clave: la fluidez operativa y la seguridad del servicio.
¿Qué hacer si un maquinista sospecha haber detectado un fallo menor en la vía? ¿Debe interrumpirse el tráfico, ordenar una limitación temporal de velocidad y asumir retrasos en el servicio, aunque al final se trate de una falsa alarma? La directriz de Adif deja sobre la mesa otra pregunta: ¿Debe esperarse que sean los maquinistas que están conduciendo trenes comerciales quienes se encarguen de detectar anomalías o confirmar fallos comunicados por sus compañeros? ¿Deberían movilizarse los técnicos siempre al instante?
¿Es algo nuevo? El mantenimiento ferroviario ha protagonizado un intenso debate a lo largo de la última semana. El propio exministro Óscar Puente apuntó las diferencias que hay entre el modelo alemán y el español: aquí las obras de mantenimiento y renovación del ferrocarril suelen ejecutarse en horario nocturno para alterar lo menos posible el tráfico diurno; en Alemania las líneas se cierran para acometer renovaciones de forma integral, sin importar si eso afecta al servicio durante largos períodos.
No se trata de decidir si el servicio ferroviario debe ofrecer mayor o menor seguridad, sino de hasta qué punto se está dispuesto a asumir interferencias en el tráfico.
¿Hay más factores? Sí. El debate sobre el mantenimiento y la gestión de la red de alta velocidad española ha cobrado importancia tras los accidentes de Adamuz y Urda, pero hay otra razón por la que debe ser prioritario: España es uno de los países con más kilómetros de alta velocidad del mundo. Solo nos supera China en extensión de vías. Eso se explica por el despliegue de la infraestructura desde los años 90, lo que ha permitido tejer una malla amplia que, sin embargo, obliga también a un mayor esfuerzo de conservación.
Esta misma semana El Mundo reveló otro documento estratégico de Adif con un aviso a navegantes: a finales de esta misma década el número de sucesos que pueden afectar al tráfico ferroviario y achacables a la infraestructura rondará probablemente los 8.800, un 20% más que el año pasado.
