articles.title: ¡Que 'GTA 6' llegue ya! Rockstar calienta el lanzamiento del juego con estas espectaculares imágenes
articles.text:
Faltan solo 2 semanas para el lanzamiento de GTA 6 y Rockstar Games está calentando motores al máximo. El estudio ha aprovechado para lanzar hoy una nueva colección de imágenes tanto de los escenarios como de los protagonistas del juego, y son verdaderamente espectaculares.
La llamada "Galería de lanzamiento" de GTA 6 incluye decenas de capturas de pantalla hasta aquí nunca vistas. Estas permiten ver con absoluto detalle tanto a Vice City y otras ubicaciones de Leónida, como a Jason, Lucía y demás personajes involucrados en la historia.
Al igual que con materiales previos, las nuevas imágenes de GTA 6 se ven impresionantes. Entornos como la ciudad de Vice City, la playa, el puerto y las discotecas son alucinantes y están llenos de detalles. Esto es una prueba más (como si hiciese falta) de que la experiencia en el mundo del nuevo Grand Theft Auto VI será prácticamente inacabable y que todo el tiempo permitirá descubrir elementos nuevos.
A continuación puedes ver todas las nuevas imágenes de GTA 6, palpitando las últimas dos semanas hacia su lanzamiento en PS5, PS5 Pro y Xbox Series X|S.
Las espectaculares nuevas imágenes de GTA 6
GTA 6 se lanza el próximo 19 de noviembre, aunque la precarga del juego estará disponible con más de una semana de anticipación en ambas plataformas. Vale recordar que en el caso de la PlayStation 5, cada jugador podrá iniciar la descarga anticipada el 10 de noviembre, a partir de las 00:00 de su zona horaria. Quienes lo jueguen desde una Xbox Series X o Series S, en cambio, podrán comenzar el proceso el mismo día a las 00:00 (GMT); es decir, la 01:00 de España, las 21:00 del 9 de noviembre en Argentina o las 18:00 del 9 de noviembre en México.
La apuesta de Rockstar Games por GTA 6 es inmensa y promete suspender todo lo que hemos visto hasta ahora en materia de experiencias de mundo abierto. Una de las revelaciones más curiosas que hemos tenido recientemente es que los jugadores podrán usar hasta caca de perro para atacar a un NPC.
Se espera que el 19 de noviembre millones de personas se ausenten de sus trabajos para disfrutar de GTA 6. Expertos creen que esto se puede traducir en pérdidas por productividad por más de 1.000 millones de dólares en un solo día.
Todavía no hay anuncios oficiales sobre cuándo llegará GTA 6 a PC. No obstante, una filtración sostiene que podría darse en el transcurso del primer trimestre de 2027, aunque hay que tomarla con pinzas. También se espera que el nuevo juego tenga su versión de GTA Online en algún momento del próximo año.

articles.title: Apple MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display review: The screen that every Mac deserves
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display has the best laptop screen I've ever seen, and other changes like reducing weight and moving from the notch to the Dynamic Island add to an excellent, albeit very pricey, machine.
Reasons to buy
- + Gorgeous tandem OLED screen
- + Noticeably lighter than existing model
- + Strong performance
- + Excellent speakers with deep bass
- + Dynamic Island is far more useful than notch
Reasons to avoid
- - Very expensive
- - Still no Face ID
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
Apple's fans know all about waiting. The company tends to polish features, especially in hardware, that some other laptop vendors release faster. The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display ends the wait for two long-requested elements: OLED and touch, both on the platform for the very first time.
That comes at a price. The 16-inch version we have on review starts at $3,399 and is $7,899 as configured. 14-inch systems start at $2,899. Those are $400 bumps over the existing MacBook Pros with identical chips, making the OLED panel a pricey upgrade.
But those who can afford these high-end systems will get the best display on a Mac, if not laptops in general. Add in a significant reduction in weight and improved speakers, and you're getting a lot of small tweaks that add up over what was already one of the best laptops, even if many of the aesthetics haven't changed.
Design
From a distance, this new MacBook Pro doesn't look all that different from the existing models, which are still on the market, which may upset some people looking for a more sweeping redesign. They come in the same colors (space black, like our review unit, and silver) and they largely have the same design. Technically, the new OLED display stack allows for a thinner system, but our 16-inch review unit, at 16 mm thick, is just 0.8 mm shorter than an equivalent 16-inch MacBook Pro with Liquid Retina screen.
The aesthetic differences show up once you open the laptop. For one, the notch in the display is gone with the PROLED XDR models, replaced with the Dynamic Island from the latest iPhones. Let us rejoice; while the notch never bothered me on phones, it always felt in the way, dipping into the macOS menu bar. This isn't perfect, but it feels far more natural and has added functionality (see "Dynamic Island and macOS Touch Features" below).
Then there's the glowing Apple logo on the back of the lid. We haven't seen this for years, and while I could take or leave it, it's definitely going to make some fans nostalgic. The old glowing Mac logos used light from LCD backlights, getting the effect with no extra power. Because OLED panels only light up pixels when they're needed, Apple is making an aesthetic choice to power the logo with a bit of extra electricity this time. The glow matches the brightness of the display, which is a fun touch. I didn't see anything in settings to disable it.
Apple's bezels are thinner, which has let Apple stretch the display to 16.3 inches on this new 16-inch model (it's still 14.2 inches on the smaller one). The displays are now rounded on all four sides. On the Liquid Retina displays, they're rounded on top to match the curves in the chassis, but are squared on the bottom. It's not a huge change, but it does cut some pixels on the bottom of the screen and looks a bit like an iPad.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Otherwise, the system looks largely the same. You have the same ports: MagSafe 3, two Thunderbolt 5 ports, and a 3.5 mm headphone jack on the left; and an SD card reader, an additional Thunderbolt port, and HDMI output on the right.
But the OLED laptop feels different when you pick it up or put it in a backpack. Changes to cooling in the new 16-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR and the switch to an OLED screen get the laptop down to 4.1 pounds with M5 Max (4.0 pounds with M5 Pro), whereas the Liquid Retina versions are 4.7 pounds. You can really feel the half-pound difference. (The 14-incher is down from 3.5 pounds to 3 pounds, too.)
And that's lighter than some of its new competition, too. Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra with Nvidia's RTX Spark chip is 4.4 pounds and thicker at 0.75 inches. The Lenovo Pro 9n, also with RTX Spark and its own OLED screen, is a lighter 3.64 pounds and is thicker at 16.7 mm.
There has been talk of a sturdier hinge, but it does still wobble when you touch it. No one has gotten around that issue. Comparing it to my personal MacBook Pro with the old design, the display goes back ever so slightly more, which is nice for touch but not a game-changer. It would be nice to see a 180-degree hinge for people who really want to write or draw on a flat surface (Apple Pencil support would be nice for that, too). For now, people who want that will need to stick to an iPad.
I spent some of the time reviewing this laptop thinking of Microsoft's Surface Laptop Studio, a touch-focused workstation with a hinge that lets the screen sit in three positions: a standard laptop, pulled forward over the keyboard, or lying like a tablet. That didn't succeed (neither did similar designs from Acer), but it took a stab at changing how a touch-based laptop worked. The new MacBook Pro design isn't a radical rethink of the ergonomics that have plagued touch laptops for over a decade. It's just a powerful Mac that happens to have a touchscreen.
Specifications
| CPU | Apple M5 Max (18 cores: 6 super cores, 12 performance cores) | 
| Graphics | 40-core GPU (integrated) | 
| Memory | 128GB LPDDR5 unified memory | 
| Storage | 2TB SSD | 
| Display | 16.3-inch tandem OLED display (PROLED XDR), 3472-by-2266 native resolution, 254 PPI, touch, True Tone, ProMotion (VRR 10-120 Hz), Standard glass | 
| Networking | Apple N1 with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread | 
| Ports | 3x Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C), 3.5 mm headphone jack, SD card reader, HDMI, MagSafe 3 | 
| Camera | 12MP Center Stage camera (1080p HD video recording) | 
| Battery | 99.6 WHr | 
| Power Adapter | 140W | 
| Operating System | macOS Golden Gate 27.2 | 
| Dimensions (WxDxH) | 14 x 9.62 x 0.63 inches (355.5 x 244.2 x 16 mm) | 
| Weight | 4.1 pounds (1.84 kg) | 
| Price (as configured) | $7,399 | 
PROLED XDR Display
We had to wait a long time to get OLED on a Mac. PROLED XDR is a silly name, but I'll give Apple this: The screen is absolutely stunning. It's the best screen I've ever seen on a notebook, and it makes me jealous when I look back at my personal system with plain old mini LED. Everything from the default wallpaper in macOS Golden Gate to videos and photos pop on this display. The blacks are deep, the colors pop, and it can get intensely bright.
Our review unit came with the 16.3-inch (slightly enlarged thanks to thinner bezels from 16.2-inches on non-PROLED models) with 3472-by-2266 native resolution, a variable refresh rate of 10 - 120 Hz, and, of course, touch support.
I used the PROLED XDR display to watch the finale of the latest season of Slow Horses. In one scene, where the mastermind of the season's plot shows up to a restaurant to meet with the head of MI5, I was wowed by the deep blacks. The restaurant was sparsely lit, and both characters were wearing black coats. The display brought out the highlights in the environment, as well as a few red accent walls.
In our instrumented testing, the PROLED XDR screen covered 83.6% of the DCI-P3 color gamut by volume and 118% sRGB, actually slightly lower than the mini LED version. I've seen them side-by-side. Trust my eyes; there's no contest here.
The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR measured 542.6 nits in our SDR brightness test, falling below the Surface Laptop Ultra, with its near-blinding 944 nits with its mini LED display. But again, PROLED simply looks better. The Surface Laptop Ultra has some light bleed and not enough local dimming zones to catch up.
The OLED panel on the Lenovo Pro 9n is the most vivid on each gamut by volume. I think it's a bit oversaturated, but if you prefer extreme pops of color, you may prefer that screen. The tandem OLED on the Dell XPS 16 was also more vivid on measurements, but was far less bright, which mutes the best aspects of OLED.
The PROLED screen showed how bright it could get with HDR content, outputting 1,964 nits in our 40% HDR test.
While I love how the display looks out of the box, Apple is offering more reference modes than ever before on a laptop, including various video, cinema, web and photography standards, and even DICOM medical imaging at 350 and 600 nits. There's also a display calibrator to fine-tune white points or perform full recalibration with external measurement tools.
Apple is far from the first company to add OLED (or, in this case, tandem OLED) to a laptop, but this stands out among the best OLED laptop displays I've seen in recent memory. The price hike to get it — $400 over mini LED models with the same chips, will be out of reach for many (though that hike also shaves half a pound off the weight). I desperately hope Apple starts bringing its brand of OLED down to the rest of the MacBook Pro and MacBook Air line, too. After all, the iPad Pro and iPad Mini both have it.
We tested the MacBook Pro with a standard screen. While I haven't spent significant time with a PROLED with the matte nano-texture display, I can tell you that this looks so good with a glossy finish that I'm not sure I could risk letting the matte displays (which I usually love!) take away any of the color saturation or context on display here. And as far as reflections go, they were minimal, even next to a window.
Dynamic Island and macOS Touch Features
Outside of OLED, there are two other additions to the MacBook Pro's screen.
The first is the Dynamic Island, a group of black pixels around the punch-hole webcam that can be used to show system alerts, notifications, and ongoing activities. (If you plug in a monitor, Dynamic Island activities show up to the left of your menu bar apps and icons.) It matches modern iPhones, and it's a huge change over the notch in other Macs, which took up far too much space in the menu bar. Now, the area around the camera is at least useful, though the camera still doesn't offer Face ID.
One of my biggest annoyances with the old design was that your mouse could fall behind the notch, with no indicator of where it was. The mouse can still move behind the Dynamic Island, but now the black area grows to indicate where the pointer is, and even wiggles if you make very small movements, to remind you where the cursor is.
The other much-discussed addition is the touchscreen. Apple hasn't reinvented the wheel here. Like most Windows and Chromebook makers, it added touch functionality onto a standard laptop. Apple's announcement mentions that the "touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it," suggesting the use of technology similar to the iPhone and flagship Windows laptops.
Apple has made slight adjustments to macOS 27 Golden Gate to accommodate touch. My personal favorite is that the "traffic lights" for maximizing, minimizing, or closing a window expand when you tap on them, to ensure you can hit the right one. When you click on a menu with your finger, the spacing is larger for easier touch targets. Like the iPhone, you can swipe down from the dynamic Island to invoke Siri. You can also flick windows to the sides to organize your windows, though you can already do that with a mouse or keyboard.
Many gestures that work on the trackpad also work on the touchscreen, like pinch to zoom, accessing Mission Control (swiping up with three fingers), showing Notification Center (swiping left from the edge of the screen), and moving between virtual desktops by swiping left or right with three fingers. Many apps have already been optimized for touch, but if they haven't, touch translates to a click, so it all still works fairly well.
One of my many experiments with the touch screen included swiping across the timeline in Final Cut Pro. But in a sample project I put together, I didn't find it any better than using the keyboard and mouse — just another option. In Maxon's Cinema 4D, I felt the same way moving a model car and adjusting virtual cameras. It's an option, but it's no better than the existing way of doing things.
Perhaps my favorite use was in Blender, making adjustments to a 3D model I was sculpting. You could do everything I did with a mouse, but some features, like changing the angle of the sculpture, felt very natural with touch. That being said, after a few minutes, my arm was tired. I couldn't see using this all the time, as there are no changes to ergonomics over the usual laptop design.
For those who never want to use touch, you can turn it off in disability settings. That being said, as someone who would likely only use it for occasional scrolls, I don't see the harm in having it on, even if I don't see myself ever pulling to refresh on Safari when CMD + R is right there. (I do wish Apple included the polishing cloth with the glossy screen on our review unit and not just matte screens, however. Touch screens get fingerprints!).
I found touch most useful for iPad apps on the App Store that work natively on Mac. For instance, my go-to podcast app is Overcast, which is great on my iPhone but designed for touch on Mac. While I'm very used to navigating it with a mouse, the choice to use touch made sense here. It's also great for the iPhone simulator in Xcode, where developers can try out touch-based apps on their touchscreen Mac instead of using a pointer. The same goes for iPhone Mirroring.
There's no touch tutorial. Touch is clearly a feature on these new MacBook Pros, but not the feature. Keyboard and mouse are clearly still king.
Audio
The six-speaker sound system in the 16-inch MacBook Pro's new design, complete with updated woofers and tweeters, keeps the crown in Apple’s camp for the best laptop speakers I've ever heard.
When I listened to Justice's "Flower in a Hurricane" with the MacBook Pro, I was floored by the drums. While the rest of the speakers don't sound superbly better than the existing Pros, the low-end has improved, and deep drums and bass easily filled my apartment with deep, well-rounded sound. Everything sounded incredible, from the audio to the synths. This may be the best way I've heard this song since I've had it on a loop after its debut in a Grand Theft Auto VI trailer.
Apple has made some adjustments to how the speaker sounds with the lid shut, too. It's surprisingly good, with The Beaches' cover of "I Ran (So Far Away)" getting surprisingly loud, with the laptop plugged into a Thunderbolt dock and the lid shut, though the drums in that song weren't as snappy. Everything was slightly dampened until I opened the lid, but honestly, I could use it like this. It's still better than many other laptop speakers, with better bass.
Productivity Performance
We tested the new MacBook Pro with an M5 Max, 128GB of unified memory, and a 2TB SSD. That's the same chip and RAM as in the 14-inch MacBook Pro we tested earlier this year, though that had a 4TB drive.
The main competitors we looked at featured Nvidia's RTX Spark N1X chips, including the Surface Laptop Ultra (20-core version) and the Lenovo Pro 9n (18-core version). We also tossed in the Dell XPS 16 with a Core X7 358H — another 16-inch system with a Tandem OLED.
Unsurprisingly, this MacBook Pro can tear through most people's everyday workloads. Apple has re-tooled the cooling in this system, and it was often close to, if not ahead of, the M5 Max we tested earlier this year in a 14-inch chassis.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
On Geekbench 6, the 16-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR earned a score of 4,353 and a multi-core score of 29,430, coming close to the other M5 Max machine. Both of those scores are far ahead of the RTX Spark laptops and the Intel-based Dell.
The 2TB SSD copied roughly 25GB of files at a rate of 1,917.69 MBps, which is fast, though the 4TB SSD in the MacBook Pro we tested earlier this year was far faster. The Surface Laptop Ultra was ever-so-slightly ahead at 1,998.59 MBps.
On Handbrake, the 16-inch MacBook Pro transcoded a 4K video to 1080p in 1 minute and 43 seconds, the fastest of the bunch.
On the Xcode benchmark, in which Macs compile large code bases, the new 16-inch MacBook Pro beat the older 14-inch model with the same M5 Max by 7 seconds, completing the task in 80 seconds.
Our Cinebench 2026 stress test has systems go through ten runs of multi-core rendering, which is particularly stressful. In the automatic performance mode, Apple's default out of the box on macOS 27, the system started at a score of 9,080, before eventually settling in the 8,050's due to throttling. With high performance mode, which runs the fans harder and louder, the Mac started at a score of 9,647 and was far more stable, with its lowest score (9,479) at the very end. If you need to get some tough work done faster, switching to high performance mode could help, as long as you're OK with fan noise.
Gaming and Graphics
The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display came with the same 40-core M5 Max GPU as the MacBook Pro we reviewed earlier this year.
In the new chassis, the M5 Max scored 4,355 on 3DMark Steel Nomad, beating the old system (3,865) as well as both configurations of the RTX Spark.
Running Cyberpunk 2077's benchmark at 1920 x 1200 using our typical test settings (Ray tracing ultra), the game ran at 36.24 frames per second. This is slightly faster than the 14-inch we tested earlier this year with the existing chassis, at 30.84 FPS. With the "For This Mac" preset, including MetalFX and a resolution of 2316 x 1448, the benchmark ran at 94.20 FPS.
Keyboard and Touchpad
Of all the things that haven't changed on the MacBook Pro, the most familiar are the keyboard and touchpad. That may be of some comfort to stalwarts of indirect input methods.
I was blazing fast on the keyboard, hitting 131 words per minute with a 99% accuracy rate on the monkeytype.com typing test. Both stats are on the high side for me, but I also can't blame Apple for making a comfortable keyboard with chiclet keys and a smart layout. I will praise any company that uses an inverted T for arrow keys as long as I live. Apple may not offer the deepest travel of the laptop market, but it does the job.
The massive trackpad features smooth glass, comfortable haptics, and intuitive gesture support in macOS. The 16-inch MacBook Pro's touchpad is luxuriously huge. After years of Windows laptops adding haptic trackpads to catch up, Apple's touchpad still feels great.
Upgradeability
While there are just four Torx Screws on the bottom of the MacBook Pro, there isn't much in the way of upgrading. Apple puts the RAM in the chip, and the storage is soldered down. If you need a repair, your best bet is probably Apple's Genius Bar.
Like other Macs, you should make sure you get the spec you need when you buy. Though, as you'll see in the configuration section, that could cost you quite a bit for some RAM and storage upgrades. Unfortunately, that's not unusual given the price of memory in the greater industry right now.
Battery Life
Apple's 99.6 WHr battery allows for a longer-lasting OLED laptop than its competitors, but in our testing, mini-LED model still lasts longer. On our battery test, laptops browse the web, run OpenGL tests, and stream video with the display set to 150 nits of brightness.
The 16-inch MacBook Pro with the PROLED XDR display lasted 15 hours and 57 minutes, far ahead of the OLED screen on the Lenovo Pro 9n (10:30) and the tandem OLED panel on the Dell XPS 16 (13:03). It also beat the mini-LED screen on the Surface Laptop Ultra.
The nearly 16-hour runtime is slightly short of Apple's "up to 17 hours" claim for web browsing. The only laptop that did better on our battery test was the 14-inch M5 Max laptop we tested earlier this year. That machine, with a smaller, mini-LED screen, ran for just shy of 18 hours.
Heat
The MacBook Pro can get a bit toasty under heavy load, though it's nothing I would deem unusable. Heavy workloads are probably best on a desk, though. New cooling changes the direction of the airflow in the machine, moving it out and through the back rather than out from vents near the display, in order to extend the display's lifespan.
During our Cinebench 2026 stress test, the keyboard measured 106.6 degrees Fahrenheit, which is definitely hot enough to notice. The touchpad was a cooler 88 F, while the hottest point on the bottom measured 107 F.
Our usual monitoring was not able to identify the heat on the CPU yet (this may require some software updates), but the overall temperature from the computer's other sensors was an average of 51 degrees Celsius.
Webcam
The 12-megapixel Center Stage webcam on the MacBook Pro will serve you well even on the most professional call. It looked great in meetings, even in one difficult lighting scenario when I had a lamp on one side and post-Daylight Savings Time early evening light coming in from a window next to me. The system gracefully balanced the mix of warm yellow and the products of blue hour.
I could easily smooth that mix out using the MacBook Pro camera's studio light or edge light effects, too.
Software and Warranty
We tested this new MacBook Pro with macOS 27 Golden Gate, which we highlighted on the Mac Studio, with new Apple Intelligence features, and the new Siri based on Apple Foundation Models and Gemini.
Apple's software suite includes Safari, Messages, Photos, Maps, Notes, and Reminders. Its services, including News and Apple TV, also have applications. Pages, Keynote, and Numbers are still in the dock by default, but they're the Creator Studio subscription versions, which require a subscription to get full features, including AI functionality, royalty-free graphics, and additional templates.
Apple sells the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display with a one-year warranty. AppleCare+ extends protection for $17.99 per month or $179.99 per year, and also adds accidental damage and drop coverage.
Configurations
We reviewed the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display in a high-end, $7,399 configuration with an M5 Max (18 CPU cores, 40 GPU cores), 128GB of memory, and 2TB of storage.
The cheapest versions of these machines are a $2,899 14-inch system with a cut-down M5 Pro featuring 15 CPU cores and 16 GPU Cores or a $3,399 16-inch laptop with the M5 Pro featuring an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU. Both base configurations come with 24GB of RAM and 1TB of storage, as well as the glossy screen option. (Adding the matte "Nano-texture" glass adds $150 and also nets you a polishing cloth, which isn't included with the glossy screen.)
Moving to the M5 Max moves you to $4,499 on the 14-inch laptop and $4,799 on the 16-incher for an 18-core CPU and a cut-down 32-core GPU. The full 40-core GPU is another $300.
RAM starts at 24GB, and costs $600 to goto 48GB or, on the 16-incher, $1,000 for 64GB. There's also 36GB and 128GB RAM options that also require 2TB of storage and an M5 Max (like our review unit). Storage prices are also astronomical, with a $1,000 jump between the 2TB and 4TB tier. (If you want 16TB, which I think will be a relatively rare choice, it's a $7,000 bump that requires the high-end M5 Max).
These are exceptionally expensive computers. Apple's 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pros without the OLED screens are still there, however, starting at $1,999 for a 14-inch notebook with M6.
Apple sells the systems at full price, or divided up into 12 monthly payments through an installment plan. They're also available for lease through Apple Upgrade.
Bottom Line
The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display isn't a radical redesign, but it has a bunch of small changes that add up to significant improvements over previous models. The tandem OLED screen is a treat to look at, and the weight reduction is significant for anyone carrying their laptop around on the go. Even the deeper bass from the speakers is a real treat.
Performance from the M5 Max is still strong, though if you're doing simple work, you can get much better single-core performance out of an M6 Macbook Pro (though you'll give up everything else).
With no major redesign, however, Apple hasn't done anything to make touching the laptop any more comfortable than its competitors. It ultimately does get tiring. That being said, the few gestures and adjustments Apple has made to macOS are helpful, if not revolutionary. Touch really is here because it's table stakes at this point. Some will use it and others won't. It's not the selling point, other than that it's a debut for the feature.
Far more Mac user deserves a screen this good, and I hope that some flavor of OLED, even if it's not tandem OLED, eventually makes it to the entry-level MacBook Pro and even the MacBook Air. Touch, too, could be popular with younger people who grew up with all touch screens and go for the Air or the MacBook Neo.
But the starting price for the systems with PROLED displays are high, and upgrades make them exceptionally expensive. For now, the best screens in the Mac lineup (and arguably the industry) are limited to just these systems. We've waited a long time for OLED on the Mac, and for many, they'll still be waiting until it gets more affordable.
Those with the deep pockets to make the investment, though, are in for one heck of a screen.
Andrew E. Freedman is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware focusing on laptops, desktops and gaming. He also keeps up with the latest news. A lover of all things gaming and tech, his previous work has shown up in Tom's Guide, Laptop Mag, Kotaku, PCMag and Complex, among others. Follow him on Threads @FreedmanAE and BlueSky @andrewfreedman.net. You can send him tips on Signal: andrewfreedman.01

articles.title: Telus says it restored wireless services after outages hit several provinces
articles.text:
Telus is facing an outage impacting its mobile network, particularly phone calls, as of around 9 a.m. ET on Nov. 5.
MobileSyrup received some reports from readers impacted by the outages, and some of our writers have also confirmed issues with phone and voicemail services, but problems appear to be sporadic.
Moreover, outage tracker Downdetector saw a spike in outage reports starting shortly before 9 a.m. ET, with the map showing reports concentrated in Toronto, Ottawa, Calgary, Edmonton, and Vancouver.
Update Nov. 5, 2026, at 2:13 p.m. ET: In an email to MobileSyrup, Telus confirmed a “small number” of service interruptions in eastern Canada on Nov. 5, and said services had been restored.
“A small number of calls in Eastern Canada may have experienced interruptions this morning. All services have been restored, and calls to emergency 911 services remained fully operational. Customers in Western Canada were not affected. We thank our customers for their patience and understanding.”
However, at the time of this update, there was still an ongoing outage impacting Maidstone and Tecumseh, Ont.
Further, Telus noted that customers in western Canada weren’t impacted by the broader wireless outage, but the company’s outage site shows numerous long-running, localized outages impacting people in B.C. and Alberta.
The original story continues below.
The carrier’s own outage website details multiple problems across Ontario, Quebec, Alberta, and B.C. These include wireless outages as well as problems impacting home phone, internet, and TV services. Most of these started in November, though some of the listed outages date back to October or even the summer.
Ontario
Telus reported a “degradation of wireless services” that started at 9:39 a.m. in Maidstone and Tecumseh, Ont. Data, text, voice, and 911 are all impacted.
The carrier says it offers 911 wireless fallback that uses other carriers’ networks in the area, but notes that customers may need to set their mobile device network to automatic in order for it to work.
Also in Ontario, around the Ottawa area, Telus reported a wireless services failure impacting voice calls, but only when calling landlines.
Quebec
A Nov. 4 outage linked to a damaged cable is ongoing but could be fixed as early as the afternoon of Nov. 5, according to the Telus outage page. This outage impacts data, voice, and text services in Chateauguay, Kahnawake, Lery, Mercier, Saint-Constant, and Saint-Remi.
Alberta
Telus’ website lists 11 active outages in Alberta, most of which date back to October or beyond. These outages are mostly related to home phone, landline 911, and internet/TV services. These include:
- Plamondon – home phone, 911 landline, outage due to suspected cable damage, started Nov. 4.
- Athabasca – home phone, 911 landline, outage started Oct. 30, suspected cable damage.
- Edmonton (Jasper Place) – two home phone, 911 landline outages reported, started Nov. 2 and 4, suspected cable damage.
- Valleyview – home phone, 911 landline, outage started Oct. 30, suspected cable damage.
- Peace River – home phone, 911 landline, started Nov. 2, suspected hardware problem.
- Edmonton – three outages for internet and two for Optik TV, one starting Oct. 4, one Nov. 4 and the last on April 17. Caused by hardware problems; investigation and restoration efforts ongoing.
- Edmonton (Bonnie Doon) – home phone, 911 landline outage caused by a cut cable on Oct. 28, restoration efforts ongoing.
- Grouard – home phone, 911 landline, outage started Oct. 24, suspected cable damage.
B.C.
Telus’ outage site lists several issues impacting B.C., including wireless, home phone, 911 landline, internet, and TV. Notably, several of the listed outages stem from the B.C. wildfires earlier this year, but others started in November.
For wireless specifically, Telus reported a degradation of wireless services in Vancouver and Whistler impacting data, text, and voice services, which started on Nov. 4. The carrier hasn’t yet determined a cause
- Gibsons – multiple home phone, 911 landline outages under investigation; suspected hardware problem.
- Hope – home phone, 911 landline, internet, Optik TV outages, suspected hardware issue, started Nov. 2.
- Delta – internet and Optik TV outage with undetermined cause, started Nov. 1.
- Several outages dating back to July and August related to wildfires.
If you’re with Telus, let us know down below whether you’re impacted by any of these outages.

articles.title: Galaxy Watch 9 tem oferta imbatível na Black November do Mercado Livre • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Watch 9 tem oferta imbatível na Black November do Mercado Livre
Galaxy Watch 9 atinge menor preço desde lançamento; novo smartwatch da Samsung vem com Snapdragon e novas funcionalidades de saúde
O Galaxy Watch 9 BT de 40 mm está saindo por apenas R$ 1.710,22 no Pix com o cupom AQUITEMPROMO na Black November do Mercado Livre. Esta é a melhor promoção já vista pelo smartwatch da Samsung desde seu lançamento, representando um desconto de 43% sobre o preço original de R$ 2.999.
Dentre os principais destaques deste lançamento de 2026, estão o novo processador da Qualcomm e as novas funcionalidades de saúde. Além disso, o Galaxy Watch 9 é um ótimo acessório para prática esportiva e monitoramento de saúde.
O Galaxy Watch 9 é o primeiro da linha base de smartwatches da Samsung a vir com processador da Qualcomm. Ele traz um Snapdragon SW6100 Wear Elite de 3 nanômetros, que permite uma navegação fluida entre as telas e rápida abertura dos aplicativos de monitoramento.
Outro destaque do relógio inteligente da Samsung frente ao seu antecessor (o Galaxy Watch 8) são duas novas funcionalidades avançadas de saúde. A primeira é a dos Sinais Vitais, que cruza dados de diversos sensores para trazer informações mais completas ao acordar, e a segunda é a Pontuação de Saúde do Coração.
O monitoramento de saúde é completo com o sensor BioActive, que mede pressão arterial, faz eletrocardiograma e avalia o índice antioxidante. Com isso, você pode acompanhar o condicionamento físico de perto e a entender as reações do seu corpo de maneira simples e muito detalhada.
A tela Super AMOLED alcança um brilho de até 3.000 nits e traz proteção de cristal de safira. Na prática, essa alta luminosidade permite visualizar as informações nitidamente mesmo sob a luz direta do sol, enquanto o vidro ultra resistente evita riscos causados por batidas acidentais.
Com GPS de dupla frequência (L1+L5) e Bluetooth 6.0, a precisão ao registrar corridas ao ar livre é muito maior, mesmo entre prédios altos. O armazenamento interno de 32 GB ainda permite baixar suas músicas favoritas diretamente no relógio, dispensando a necessidade de carregar o smartphone.
Aproveite a oferta no Mercado Livre para comprar o Galaxy Watch 9 BT de 40 mm por apenas R$ 1.710,22 no Pix com o cupom AQUITEMPROMO, um cupom do mês da Black Friday 2026.
Este e outros cupons do mês da Black Friday você encontra no compilado de cupons da Black November aqui no Achados do TB. Acompanhe também as principais ofertas divulgadas pela nossa curadoria através dos nossos canais no Telegram ou WhatsApp.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Samsung drops its best-ever deal on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 for Black Friday — plus 5 more offers I'd recommend on TVs, phones, tablets, and more
articles.text:
6 of the best deals from the Samsung Black Friday sale — up to £300 off the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Galaxy S26, Buds 4 Pro, Micro-LED TVs, and more
Includes a best-ever deal for the brand's brilliant new foldable
After teasing us with a few of its deals last month, the full Samsung Black Friday sale has now started in the UK, featuring savings on phones, TVs, appliances, tablets, wearables, and more. With some strong discounts and big trade-in savings available, here are the offers that I think are worth considering if you're looking to upgrade.
• Browse the full Samsung Black Friday sale
If there's one deal that has me tempted more than anything in the sale, it's this £300 saving on the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 when you use the discount code 'NOV26'. When combined with an extra £100 off when paying with PayPal, plus a trade-in rebate of up to £713, there's an opportunity here to get the fantastic foldable for a seriously low price.
We're huge fans of the phone too, as you can see in our 4.5-star Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 review. By changing the form factor to a more portable and pocketable passport-sized design, packing in all the performance you need for daily use, and a solid battery life to match, it feels like Samsung finally worked out the ideal foldable with this release.
Elsewhere in the Black Friday sale, you can get up to £500 off several of Samsung's excellent premium TVs, or up to £500 off appliances if you're planning a kitchen refit. There are also price cuts on its latest Galaxy Watch and the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra.
All offers are backed by the Samsung Black Friday Price Promise, which means that if you find the same product for cheaper elsewhere from now until December 1, you can get a refund for the difference. A welcome bit of peace of mind during the hectic end-of-year shopping period.
Here are all of my top picks from the Samsung Black Friday sale. Just be aware that some offers end on November 17. Chances are we'll see even more deals as we get closer to Black Friday proper, too.
Samsung UK Black Friday sale — quick links
- Appliances: up to £500 off
- Audio: £50 off the Buds4 Pro
- Laptops: save up to £400
- Phones: up to £250 off
- Smartwatches: get Bupa Well+ free
- Tablets: up to £730 off with a trade-in
- TVs: VAT back + free soundbars
My top 6 deals at Samsung
Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8: £300 off with the code 'NOV26' — plus £100 off with PayPal
This is one of the best offers I've seen yet on the latest Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8. You can combine the discount code 'NOV26' to get £300 off, plus the extra £100 off you get for paying with PayPal, to make a big saving on the excellent foldable. Equally, you can combine the code with the £10 per month Three plan for an even better price – one you can reduce further with a trade-in. We gave the Z Fold 8 an incredible 4.5 stars in our review for its power, smart design, vibrant display, good cameras, and respectable battery life.
Read moreRead less▼
Samsung Galaxy S26: get £250 off — and an extra £100 off with PayPal
There's a flat £250 discount on the Samsung Galaxy S26 for Black Friday, plus an extra £100 off when you pay using PayPal. It's a good offer, but I've seen the phone cheaper elsewhere. What will make it an even better deal, though, is if you have a phone to trade in, as Samsung offers some of the biggest rebates out there. That'll knock the solid Android flagship down to a very tempting low price.

articles.title: Serve Robotics launches new business to become the AWS for robots | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Serve Robotics, a maker of self-driving sidewalk delivery robots, is expanding beyond its autonomous delivery operations in a bid to become a technology supplier to other companies building robots.
The company, which spun out of Uber’s acquisition of Postmates in 2021 and went public in 2024, said Thursday it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services.
Specifically, Serve Robotics will offer customers its connectivity and data tools. Bedrock Robotics, a startup developing self-driving systems for construction equipment, is a customer, according to Serve. It’s also working with T-Mobile to bring AI computing power closer to robots, Serve announced alongside its third-quarter earnings on Thursday.
“We are solving the problem of robots in human spaces,” Serve Robotics CEO and co-founder Ali Kashani told TechCrunch.
Serve Robotics already makes two kinds of robots, the cute googly-eyed sidewalk delivery robot and one designed for hospitals that it got through its acquisition of Diligent Robotics.
Those businesses are not going away, Kashani emphasized in a recent interview. Instead, he said there is opportunity to sell the technology it developed for its own robots to other companies developing robots for farms, warehouses, and other uncontrolled environments.
“I kind of think of it as the AWS moment where we are taking the technology we’ve built for us, and we’re opening it up for more people to build on,” he said, adding this wouldn’t have been possible without developing its own robot fleet.
The expansion comes as Serve’s sidewalk delivery business expands, but is shifting away from Uber and toward other partners, including DoorDash and Wonder.
Its new Physical AI Services business line will offer three products. Serve Link helps connect robots in the field to AI systems running in data centers, which would allow companies to potentially tap into more powerful AI models without having to put all that computing power onboard.
“Any robotic application generally needs to connect the robots to some offline intelligence, whether it’s to collect data or do exception handling or whatever,” said Kashani. “It’s the connectivity piece that has to be really high performance. You need to be able to manage really unreliable networks and still reliably connect, and that’s what we solve.”
It’s also launching a data curator tool that helps companies find edge cases in the reams of real-world data a robot collects, which can then be fed back into a training model to improve performance. Its third product is a real-world, foundation-model data catalog built from Serve’s own sidewalk robots that can teach AI models how to understand complex human environments.
Kashani said he’s been thinking about this idea — a playbook he learned from Amazon — for years.
“When the technology is so nascent, you have got to build the end-to-end application because that’s the only way you know what to build, but then over time, as the technology gets more advanced, a lot more people are going to be wanting to build similar things,” he said. “And what you want to do is to open your technology so others build with you and on your platform.”

articles.title: El Galaxy Fit 4 se filtra y hay una novedad que muchos llevaban años esperando
articles.text:
A unas semanas de su presentación, el Galaxy Fit 4 se ha filtrado gracias a Samsung. Un análisis de la aplicación Galaxy Fit 4 Manager reveló una buena parte de sus funciones, las cuales mantienen la línea de su predecesor al enfocarse en el monitoreo de actividad física y salud. Sumado a ello, la próxima pulsera inteligente de Samsung incluirá características que hasta ahora estaban reservadas para dispositivos más avanzados.
De acuerdo con SammyGuru, la app Galaxy Fit 4 Manager, un complemento que opera junto a Galaxy Wearable, apareció por sorpresa en la Galaxy Store. Un análisis a fondo de esta herramienta encontró que el Galaxy Fit 4 ofrecerá más opciones de personalización, como cambiar esferas, asignar funciones al botón lateral y configurar a detalle el comportamiento de las notificaciones. Además de eso, los usuarios podrán añadir fotos como fondo de pantalla en el dispositivo.
En el apartado de salud y actividad física, el Galaxy Fit 4 mantendría la fórmula que distingue a esta categoría. Los usuarios podrán llevar un seguimiento de pasos, calorías, tiempo activo y entrenamientos, así como un registro del sueño con fases de descanso, puntuaciones personalizadas y recomendaciones basadas en varios días de uso. También se ofrecen las funciones típicas de monitorización del ritmo cardíaco, alertas por frecuencia elevada o baja y medición de oxígeno en la sangre.
La filtración menciona algunas mejoras en la conectividad, gracias a una función que emite un sonido para encontrar la pulsera en caso de que olvides en dónde la dejaste. Esto sería posible gracias a un nuevo altavoz integrado, que abriría la puerta a responder llamadas desde la muñeca cuando el Galaxy Fit se conecta a tu móvil.
El Galaxy Fit 4 deja fuera un componente clave que podría mejorar la experiencia de uso
Si bien las filtraciones dejan ver un dispositivo bien equipado, la realidad es que el Galaxy Fit 4 no tendrá una característica importante. De acuerdo con Android Headlines, la pulsera llegará sin GPS integrado, por lo que los usuarios tendrán que depender del móvil si quieren registrar actividades al aire libre como correr o andar en bicicleta.
La ausencia de GPS es común en las pulseras fitness, ya que las empresas prefieren no incluirlo para reducir costes, tamaño y consumo de batería. Estos chips se reservan para relojes inteligentes como el Galaxy Watch o pulseras dedicadas de gama alta, por lo que el Galaxy Fit 4 seguirá por la misma línea de su predecesor y tomará el GPS del teléfono para marcar la ruta y las mediciones.
El reporte también menciona que la batería será peor que la del Galaxy Fit 3, ofreciendo una autonomía de unos cuatro días por carga. Como referencia, el Fit 3 duraba de 4 a 7 días por carga con uso estándar, pudiendo extenderse hasta 10 días en uso mínimo. Es probable que las nuevas funciones y componentes tengan impacto en el consumo, aunque tendremos que esperar unos días hasta conocer su rendimiento real.
Según las filtraciones, el Galaxy Fit 4 podría anunciarse en las próximas semanas a un precio similar al del Galaxy Fit 3, que se vendió en 65 euros o 999 pesos mexicanos cuando debutó a principios de 2024.

articles.title: Daksham Capital raises Rs 125 Cr in first close of Rs 300 Cr fund
articles.text:
Daksham Capital raises Rs 125 Cr in first close of Rs 300 Cr fund
The fund will invest in startups at the pre-Series A and Series A stages, with cheque sizes ranging from Rs 5 crore to Rs 20 crore. It will focus on D2C brands, consumer enablers, B2B2C businesses, supply chains and consumer AI.
Daksham Capital, a multi-family office and private wealth management group, has raised Rs 125 crore as the first close of its Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV) Fund I.
According to a statement, DGV Fund I has a target corpus of Rs 300 crore, comprising a base corpus of Rs 150 crore and a greenshoe option of another Rs 150 crore. The first close was anchored by family offices, HNI/UHNI families and entrepreneurs.
The fund will invest in startups at the pre-Series A and Series A stages, with cheque sizes ranging from Rs 5 crore to Rs 20 crore. It will focus on D2C brands, consumer enablers, B2B2C businesses, supply chains and consumer AI.
According to the statement, the fund's preferred entry range is businesses with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of Rs 25–75 crore, with a focus on companies that have the potential to scale to Rs 300–500 crore in revenue.
“Over the last decade, we have backed consumer start-ups that went on to deliver strong outcomes. What is changing now is how consumers discover, choose and buy. We believe the next decade of consumption will be shaped by brands and start-ups working alongside AI – from discovery and personalisation to fulfilment, trust and credit,” said Shivam Diwan, Co-Founder & Managing Partner, Daksham Growth Ventures.
Beyond capital, DGV will also work closely with portfolio companies on governance, financial reporting, brand positioning, leadership development and distribution expansion.
“We see considerable potential in businesses that understand their consumers, have built a strong foundation and are ready to expand their ambitions. Our focus is to build long-term partnerships that align capital with the opportunities ahead,” said Saket Lakhotia, Co-Founder & Group CEO, Daksham Capital.
Daksham Capital is a wealth and asset management group that acts as family office advisor and investment banker to HNI and UHNI families, business houses, CXOs, promoters of listed companies and family trusts.

articles.title: Fake OpenAI, SpaceX events used to steal Microsoft, Google accounts
articles.text:
Hackers are using fake OpenAI, SpaceX, and Anthropic event invitations to lure employees into phishing attacks, using two different phishing-as-a-service platforms to steal Microsoft and Google account credentials and authentication sessions.
According to a new report from Push Security, the attackers use convincing event registration pages offering free access to premium AI services and other rewards to trick victims into signing in with their corporate accounts.
What makes the attacks interesting is that the same phishing pages integrate two separate phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platforms, Kali365 and VoidProxy, to target Microsoft and Google accounts using different authentication attacks.
Kali365 conducts Microsoft device code phishing attacks, while VoidProxy acts as an adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) reverse proxy to intercept Google sign-ins and steal authentication session cookies.
The Microsoft attack also uses VoidProxy as a second stage, allowing attackers to capture credentials and session cookies after obtaining authentication tokens through Kali365.
Push Security says it detected and blocked visits to the malicious event registration pages in late October 2026.
The campaign comes after a similar campaign documented by ANY.RUN in July, when attackers abused legitimate Zoom event pages to promote fake Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic events that led to device code and AiTM phishing attacks.
Cofense also recently reported on phishing emails impersonating Anthropic event invitations that were distributed through GoTo Webinar's email infrastructure and redirected recipients through multiple websites to fake registration pages.
Fake AI events lead to account phishing
While it is unclear how the attackers initially distribute the phishing links, Push Security found that they redirect victims to a malicious event registration page using links from trusted services, including Google and Zapier URL shorteners.
Invitations from earlier versions of the campaign were also distributed through GoTo Webinar's email systems or legitimate Zoom event pages.
Push Security says the attackers use two custom phishing kits, tracked as ZoomMock and MSDRoot, to create fake event pages that then direct victims to the Kali365 and VoidProxy phishing services.
The researchers believe the same threat actors operate both kits, as they use shared infrastructure and the same targeting.
The campaign impersonates events hosted by OpenAI, SpaceX, and Anthropic, with registration pages designed to resemble legitimate event websites.
One phishing page advertises an OpenAI event titled "ChatGPT for Social & Digital Marketing Teams" that promises three months of ChatGPT Pro to participants.
Another promotes a private SpaceX event on November 12, offering registrants either three months of Grok Heavy or a "SpaceX share."
The researchers also found a phishing page impersonating an Anthropic event at AWS re:Invent 2026 that was already taken down.
The fake registration pages tell visitors they must sign in with their work accounts to register and claim the advertised rewards.
Before displaying the fake registration pages, the websites show a Cloudflare CAPTCHA to "Confirm you're not a robot." This prevents automated security platforms from scanning the phishing site.
Once visitors reach the event registration page, they see two options: "Continue with Microsoft" and "Continue with Google."
When victims select the Microsoft option, the phishing page contacts the Kali365 platform to generate a Microsoft device authentication code.
A device code phishing attack occurs when an attacker abuses the legitimate OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant flow to obtain authentication tokens for the victim's Microsoft Entra account.
This can then be used to access the user's resources and connected SSO applications, such as Microsoft 365, Salesforce, Google Workspace, Dropbox, Adobe, SAP, Slack, Zendesk, Atlassian, and many others.
Device code phishing attacks have been used in the past for data theft and cyberespionage attacks.
The visitor is instructed to copy the code and enter it on Microsoft's legitimate device login website, where they authenticate and approve the request.
This allows the Kali365 phishing platform to steal Microsoft authentication tokens without requiring the victim to disclose their password directly.
After the device code authentication succeeds, the page redirects the victim to a VoidProxy Microsoft login page, where attackers can also capture the victim's password and session cookie.
When victims select the Google authentication option, the phishing page instead opens a pop-up containing a Google login page from the VoidProxy PhaaS.
The platform operates as an adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) platform that sits between the victim's browser and Google's login page, proxies the login forms, and steals credentials, MFA responses, and session cookies.
Both the Kali365 and VoidProxy platforms let attackers bypass multifactor authentication by capturing an already authenticated session or, in the case of device code authentication, bypassing MFA entirely.
To protect against these attacks, employees should avoid entering Microsoft device authentication codes provided by unfamiliar websites and be cautious of event invitations that require signing in with corporate accounts to claim rewards.
Organizations can also restrict device code authentication where it is not needed and use phishing-resistant MFA, such as FIDO2 security keys, to help prevent session hijacking.

articles.title: iPhone 18e : voici la seule amélioration qu'Apple proposerait sur son « iPhone pas cher »
articles.text:
Fin février 2025, Apple sortait son iPhone 16e, remplaçant de sa gamme SE, avec un téléphone moins cher que les autres iPhone, tout en proposant des compromis sur sa fiche technique. Rebelotte l’année d’après avec l’iPhone 17e, avec la même recette. Apple semble bien parti pour sortir son iPhone 18e en même temps que l’iPhone 18, en mars ou en avril prochain. Parmi les changements attendus, la seule vraie amélioration serait au niveau de la puce.
Une meilleure puce et c’est tout ?
C’est le leaker Fixed Focus Digital qui a publié un message sur le réseau social chinois Weibo pour nous en dire plus sur l’iPhone 18e. Il a indiqué que l’iPhone 18 et l’iPhone 18e partageraient certains procédés de fabrication, sans qu’on sache lesquels. Mais il a surtout insisté sur le fait que le seul changement majeur serait une nouvelle puce ; et c’est le seul changement qu’il dit confirmer.
Récemment, un autre leaker du nom de Digital Chat Station avait indiqué que l’iPhone 18e serait équipé d’une puce A20, gravée en 2 nm. Pour le moment, cette puce est inconnue, puisque que les iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max, iPhone Duo et iPad mini de 2026 sont tous équipés d’une A20 Pro. On peut supposer que l’A20 serait une version un peu moins puissante (et moins chère) de cette puce haut de gamme.
Fixed Focus Digital en a profité pour rappeler qu’il avait vu juste avec l’iPhone 17e. Alors que beaucoup de rumeurs évoquaient l’arrivée de la Dynamic Island, il avait toujours laissé entendre que ce ne serait pas le cas. De quoi subtilement sous-entendre que l’iPhone 18e en serait aussi dépourvu, au profit de l’encoche qu’on connaît bien.
Ce qu’on sait de l’iPhone 18e
Jusqu’à maintenant, les autres rumeurs n’ont pas évoqué de grands changements sur l’iPhone 18e. Rien ne changerait sur l’écran : il s’agirait toujours d’une dalle Oled de 6,12 pouces, toujours limitée à 60 Hz. Côté mémoire vive, ce modèle serait équipé de 9 Go de RAM. Avec la puce A20, cela devrait offrir de meilleures performances, notamment pour les usages d’IA générative en local.
Quant au volet photo, il faudrait toujours compter sur un seul capteur à l’arrière de 48 Mpx, sans ultra-grand-angle, ni téléobjectif. À l’avant, Apple ferait un petit effort : le capteur selfie passerait de 12 à 24 Mpx. Cet iPhone 18e est attendu pour le premier trimestre 2027, vraisemblablement en mars, aux côtés de l’iPhone 18 standard ainsi que de l’iPhone Air 2. Quant au prix, impossible de le connaître pour le moment, mais au vu de la crise des composants, on peut s’attendre à une augmentation : pour rappel, l’iPhone 17e avait été lancé à 719 euros.

articles.title: IBM, AMD and Oak Ridge join forces to launch quantum computing error-correction platform - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
IBM, AMD and Oak Ridge join forces to launch quantum computing error-correction platform
IBM Corp., Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and the Quantum Science Center at Oak Ridge National Laboratory today announced a new quantum error-correction platform that integrates quantum and high-performance computing.
Gaining high performance and correctness in quantum computing requires protecting quantum information from noise. In many cases, researchers have paired quantum computers with classical computers to achieve superior performance for running industry-relevant problems. The challenge today is scaling up these advances with classical computing.
Today’s physical quantum qubits make errors roughly once every few hundred operations. Without correction, errors compound rapidly, rendering long or complex calculations completely untenable. Game-changing algorithms such as Shor’s algorithm for factoring or for molecular-scale simulations in chemistry require billions of error-free operations.
This launch uses a co-design platform for quantum error correction using IBM’s quantum computers, including the 120-qubit Nighthawk with ORNL’s Umbra High-Performance Computing system powered by AMD’s Instinct MI355X graphics processing units and 5th Gen EPYC central processing units.
“ORNL’s strength in high-performance computing, combined with the expertise of our QSC partners – like IBM and AMD – creates an opportunity to push the boundaries of what is possible,” said Director of the Quantum Science Center Travis Humble. “With Umbra, we will now test new ideas, evaluate approaches at scale, and build the foundation for more reliable quantum computers.”
Jay Gambetta, an IBM Fellow and director of IBM Research, added that the biggest contributor to today’s research is no longer whether error correction will work on quantum hardware, but how to accelerate and optimize it to build systems scientists can use to tackle problems.
IBM said the Nighthawk’s square-lattice connectivity enables industry-leading speed and real-time control to test error-correction techniques. GPU accelerators, such as AMD’s nodes in the Umbra system, can help with this fine-tuning. The co-design platform connected at Oak Ridge will help explore quantum as part of a broader artificial intelligence and scientific computing infrastructure.
“This new co-design platform for quantum error correction allows us to evaluate different approaches and determine the architectures, software and workflows that will scale,” said Gambetta.
Researchers can measure qubits mid-calculation and act on the results in real time, set the exact timing for the signals that protect the qubits from noise, and see exactly what the hardware ran while working with raw measurement signals. This will provide error-correction research with the raw data needed for the next generation of approaches to build sophisticated capabilities for large systems running real code.
Earlier this year, IBM and ORNL unveiled results showing how workloads running on both quantum and classical computers and the Frontier supercomputer can simulate real magnetic materials and calculate molecular configurations of a promising material for fusion fuel.
The simulation of magnetic materials could lead to breakthroughs in superconductors, more efficient batteries and novel drugs. A promising fusion fuel could provide a stepping stone to abundant energy superior to nuclear fission, which powers current nuclear power plants.

articles.title: Comment la France veut faire tenir un canon électromagnétique dans un navire de guerre
articles.text:
Avoir un canon électromagnétique, c’est bien. En avoir un qui puisse tenir sur un bateau, c’est mieux. Or, voilà tout le problème auquel font face les armées désireuses de compter sur ces armements : l’encombrement. Ces systèmes prennent beaucoup trop de place, tout particulièrement du côté du générateur énergétique.
Le principe de ce canon est de propulser des projectiles à très haute vitesse grâce à une impulsion électrique très intense, sans poudre. L’Agence de l’innovation de défense (AID) parle d’un besoin de plus d’un million d’ampères en une fraction de seconde pour tirer un boulet à plus de 2 kilomètres par seconde (près de six fois la vitesse du son).
Or, constate l’AID, les condensateurs à film qui fournissent ce courant aujourd’hui sont bien trop volumineux pour une frégate, et les batteries lithium-ion du commerce testées se heurtaient à des limites de courant, en plus de prendre trois fois trop de place. Il faut donc trouver un moyen de miniaturiser davantage leur alimentation.
C’est là qu’entre en jeu un nouveau projet qui rassemble l’AID mais aussi la société française Hemeria, spécialisée dans la conversion et le stockage d’énergie embarquée, et l’Institut franco-allemand de recherches de Saint-Louis (ISL), déjà impliqué dans des travaux sur ces railguns. Ce partenariat est annoncé pour deux ans.
Une alimentation cinq à dix fois plus compacte visée
Comme l’explique aussi le communiqué d’Hemeria, le démonstrateur doit associer des supercondensateurs, des composants qui stockent l’énergie et la relâchent bien plus vite qu’une batterie, à un générateur XRAM, un montage à bobines qui multiplie le courant au moment de la décharge. Les supercondensateurs sont fournis par Hemeria, le générateur XRAM par l’ISL.
Plus spécifiquement, Hemeria « assurera le développement du système de gestion des supercondensateurs, comprenant le chargeur, le logiciel de conduite des essais ainsi que les organes de contrôle-commande et de sécurité ». L’ISL, de son côté, gérera « la validation des supercondensateurs au cours d’essais représentatifs de ses besoins ».
Le banc d’essai vise un courant de crête de plus de 50 000 ampères, soit environ vingt fois moins que le million d’ampères nécessaire à un tir. Ici, « l’objectif [est] de ne pas dépasser les capacités des composants de commutation qualifiés disponibles et de réduire d’un facteur 5 à 10 le volume et la masse de la chaîne d’alimentation » par rapport aux condensateurs à films
La quête du canon électromagnétique est difficile. L’US Navy a fini par stopper son propre programme en 2021, après avoir englouti environ un demi-milliard de dollars (près de 450 millions d’euros) en quinze ans, en invoquant ses contraintes budgétaires et la difficulté d’intégrer l’arme à ses systèmes de combat.
Outre l’alimentation électrique qu’il faut réussir à fournir, d’autres défis ne sont pas complètement réglés pour le canon électromagnétique : c’est en particulier le cas de la chaleur et de la pression observées à chaque décharge électrique, qui usent significativement les matériels utilisés. Le calibre est un autre facteur limitant, tout comme les performances attendues (portée, vitesse).
Malgré les obstacles, plusieurs pays sont engagés dans des projets de recherche. L’AID range toujours les États-Unis, malgré l’abandon de l’US Navy, parmi les principaux acteurs de la recherche, aux côtés de la Chine. Le Japon, lui, a signé en 2024 un accord de coopération sur ces armes avec la France et l’Allemagne. Tokyo a d’ailleurs déjà testé son canon.

articles.title: Moins de consoles vendues, des bénéfices records... L'incroyable paradoxe de PlayStation !
articles.text:
Entre juillet et septembre, la chute des livraisons de consoles n’a pas freiné les affaires du fabricant japonais. Les jeux et le PlayStation Plus soutiennent les résultats de sa division jeu vidéo, au point de pousser le groupe à relever ses ambitions pour l’année.
Chez Sony, une PS5 continue de rapporter bien après son achat. Les résultats publiés ce 5 novembre l’illustrent avec un chiffre d’affaires de 6,8 milliards d’euros pour la division Game & Network Services en hausse de 8,6% sur un an. Les dépenses des joueurs compensent largement le recul des livraisons de consoles.
Les PS5 se vendent moins, mais plus cher
Sony a livré 2,6 millions de PS5 entre juillet et septembre, contre 4 millions un an auparavant, soit une baisse de 35%. Depuis son lancement, la machine totalise ainsi 97,9 millions d’unités livrées. Il s’agit des consoles expédiées aux distributeurs, pas nécessairement déjà achetées par les joueurs.
Le recul est bien moins marqué dans les comptes. Les revenus du matériel diminuent de seulement 4,9%, à 1,2 milliard d’euros. Les hausses de prix et la faiblesse du yen amortissent la baisse des volumes, la monnaie japonaise dépréciée augmentant la valeur des recettes réalisées à l’étranger lorsqu’elles sont converties en yens.
Les joueurs déjà équipés font tourner la boutique
Si les ventes de matériel ralentissent, les achats de jeux continuent eux de progresser. Sur PS4 et PS5, Sony comptabilise 88,2 millions de jeux complets vendus, soit 7,9 millions de plus qu’un an auparavant. Les titres de ses propres studios représentent 8,2 millions d’exemplaires, en hausse de 30%. Marvel’s Wolverine atteint pour sa part 2,4 millions de ventes au 4 novembre, cinquante jours après sa sortie.
Les revenus des jeux progressent logiquement de 12,6%, à environ 4 milliards d’euros. Les recettes des ventes de jeux complets en téléchargement bondissent même de 23% alors que 78% des jeux complets sont désormais vendus en numérique, contre 72% un an plus tôt.
À ces achats s’ajoutent les services réseau, qui regroupent notamment le PlayStation Plus et la publicité. Leurs revenus augmentent de 19,5%, à 1,2 milliard d’euros alors que PlayStation recense 127 millions de comptes actifs mensuels contre 119 millions un an auparavant. La base de joueurs actifs continue à s’élargir malgré le ralentissement des livraisons de nouvelles consoles.
Une envolée des bénéfices à remettre en perspective
En hausse de 83% sur un an, le bénéfice opérationnel de la division PlayStation atteint ainsi environ 1,2 milliard d’euros, un record pour un deuxième trimestre fiscal. Le bond profite toutefois d’une comparaison favorable avec l’an dernier, lorsque 280 millions d'euros de charges exceptionnelles avaient pesé sur le trimestre, dont 177 millions liés à des dépréciations de Bungie. En réintégrant ces charges au résultat de l’époque, la progression ressort autour de 29%.
Sony relève désormais sa prévision de bénéfice opérationnel annuel de 3,70 à 3,93 milliards d'euros, avec un objectif de chiffre d’affaires également rehaussé, à 27 milliards.
La crise de la RAM n'a donc plus rien d’une mauvaise nouvelle pour Sony. Entre les jeux, les extensions et les abonnements, le fabricant a encore de nombreuses occasions de vous faire passer en caisse, sans même avoir besoin de vous vendre une nouvelle console.
Source : Sony via Wccftech
