articles.title: Motorola asalta la gama alta con un nuevo móvil de casi 2000 euros llamado Signature 27 y su impresionante sistema de cámaras
articles.text:
Motorola pone al día su catálogo de smartphones con un nuevo modelo con el que busca llevar la mejor tecnología de la marca a un mercado cada vez más competitivo en la gama alta. La compañía apuesta por este segmento con el nuevo Motorola Signature 27, al que ha bautizado como el más avanzado hasta la fecha.
Y razones no le faltan. La propuesta de Motorola con el Signature 27 parte de un diseño bastante diferenciador en su parte trasera, nuevos materiales de fabricación premium y mucha IA. Sin olvidar, eso sí, un sistema de cámaras totalmente renovado y con el sello de Gold Label de DxOMark.
Aunque, como decimos, su punto fuerte es su sistema de cámara, uno de los grandes protagonistas del Motorola Signature 27 es su pantalla. Monta una Extreme AMOLED Duo con tecnología tándem, la más brillante disponible en un smartphone. Su cerebro es un Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 refrigerado con el sistema ArcticMesh de Motorola, y remata el conjunto un sistema de audio con la firma de Bang & Olufsen.
El Motorola Signature 27 quiere plantar cara en la gama alta con sus cámaras
Destaca, sobre todo, su sistema de cámaras, compuesto por una cámara principal Sony LYTIA L910 de 50 MP con la tecnología LOFIC, un teleobjetivo periscópico de 200 MP con Super Zoom de 100x, un sensor de acción EVS dedicado en un smartphone y una cámara ultra gran angular de 50 MP, además de una cámara frontal de 50 MP. Respecto al vídeo, el Signature 27 cuenta con el Video Enhancement Engine de Motorola, que utiliza la IA para optimizar de forma inteligente y en tiempo real el color, el contraste y el rango dinámico y es totalmente compatible con Dolby Vision.
Además, todo trabaja en conjunto con la estabilización electrónica de imagen de Qualcomm y el estabilizador óptico (OIS) de 3,5° de la cámara principal, por lo que promete algunas de las fotos más nítidas del mercado, al menos sobre el papel. La calidad de imagen de las fotos también se traslada a la pantalla, que incluye la tecnología necesaria para ver esas imágenes y vídeo a máxima calidad: 12.000⁴ nits de brillo máximo, resolución 1,5K Super HD y, como decimos, Dolby Vision.
Respecto a su autonomía, el Motorola Signature 27 incorpora una batería de silicio-carbono de 7.000 mAh, un 35 % mayor que la de la generación anterior, y carga TurboPower de 90 W.
Respecto a su precio y disponibilidad, el Motorola Signature 27 estará disponible en dos colores, Coal Smoke y Capulet Olive, a un precio recomendado de 1.899 €, aunque llegará con una oferta de lanzamiento que incluye un Moto Watch Ultra y los Moto Sound Flow, valorados en 628 €.
Motorola también tiene nuevos smartwatch y auriculares con sello de Bose
Además, Motorola también ha presentado los nuevos auriculares moto buds 2 ultra que siguen con la firma de Bose e incluyen sus dos tecnologías más importantes: Bose SoundDesign y Bose QuietControl ANC para ofrecer una experiencia de audio inmersiva y una cancelación de ruido avanzada.
Incluye un sistema de seis micrófonos de alta relación señal-ruido (SNR) y dos unidades de captación de voz (VPU), que, según la compañía, consiguen una captura de voz de gran calidad y estrenan nuevas funciones inteligentes como AI Live Translate y gestos con la cabeza. Tienen hasta 8 horas de reproducción continua con una sola carga y hasta 37 horas en total con su estuche de carga. ¿Su precio? 199 €.
Junto con estos nuevos auriculares, Motorola también ha presentado el nuevo Moto Watch 2 Fit, un reloj inteligente de nueva generación que combina análisis deportivos avanzados con tecnología de Polar y promete 12 días de autonomía.
Algunas de estas funciones de análisis incluyen opciones muy interesantes como Running Index, que ofrece una puntuación basada en la forma aeróbica y la eficiencia de carrera, Daily Activity Goal y Daily Activity Score, que ofrecen objetivos y datos personalizados según el nivel de actividad de cada usuario, para ayudar a crear hábitos deportivos.
constantes, Active Intensity Zones, que divide la actividad física en niveles de intensidad ligera, moderada e intensa, y una especialmente interesante llamada Energy Sources, que muestra cómo utiliza el cuerpo las grasas, los hidratos de carbono y las proteínas durante el ejercicio.
Cuenta con protección IP68 2 y resistencia al agua 5 ATM, pantalla gOLED de 1,85" con 1500 nits y marco de aluminio. Todo por un precio de 99 euros.

articles.title: Billig-Tastatur oder Profi-Modell? Worauf es bei der richtigen Gaming-Tastatur ankommt
articles.text:
Schnelle Reaktion und individuelle Tastenbefehle: Welche Gaming-Tastaturen sich wirklich lohnen
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Einfache Tastaturen sind oft schon für unter zehn Euro erhältlich. Für die gelegentliche Online-Recherche oder das Verfassen von E-Mails kann ein solches Modell durchaus reichen. Wenn du allerdings am PC zocken möchtest, lohnt es sich, in eine spezielle Gaming-Tastatur zu investieren. Sie erkennt Tastenanschläge besonders schnell, was in Shootern oder anderen temporeichen Spielen den entscheidenden Unterschied machen kann. Viele Modelle verfügen außerdem über programmierbare Tasten, mit denen sich einzelne Befehle oder ganze Eingabefolgen festlegen lassen. Wir stellen dir drei empfehlenswerte Gaming-Tastaturen vor – vom günstigen Einsteiger- bis zum Profi-Modell.
Unter den Pioneers Picks stellen wir dir regelmäßig weitere praktische Tools und Gadgets vor.
Bei der Auswahl der passenden Tastatur solltest du einige Dinge beachten, die je nach Art deiner bevorzugten Games variieren können. Eine RGB-Beleuchtung und eine extrem hohe Polling-Rate sind nette Extras, aber nicht das Wichtigste. Was wirklich zählt, ist stattdessen das Tippgefühl, das Rollover sowie eine individuelle Tastenbelegung. Für reines Gaming sind lineare oder Hall-Effect-Switches meist die beste Wahl. Außerdem lohnt sich eine kabelgebundene Tastatur, weil der Akku nicht mitten in einer langen Gaming-Session schlapp machen kann. Zudem profitierst du von einer niedrigen Latenz und musst keine Funkstörungen befürchten.
Sharkoon Skiller SGK4: Gaming-Tastatur für unter 25 Euro
Die Skiller SGK4 von Sharkoon zählt zu den beliebtesten Gaming-Tastaturen für den kleinen Geldbeutel. Es handelt sich um eine Rubberdome-Tastatur: Unter jeder Taste sitzt ein elastischer Gummi-Dom, der beim Drücken nachgibt, den elektrischen Kontakt herstellt und die Taste danach wieder nach oben federt. Während andere Tastaturen dieser Sorte nur wenige Tastenanschläge gleichzeitig registrieren, beherrscht das Sharkoon-Modell N-Key-Rollover. Das heißt, du kannst beliebig viele Tasten gleichzeitig drücken – jede Eingabe wird korrekt erkannt. So behältst du auch bei komplexen Spielmanövern die volle Kontrolle. Zahlreiche Funktionstasten mit Multimedia-Aktionen runden das Erlebnis ab.
Über vier Profiltasten auf der Oberseite des Skiller SGK4 kannst du Spielprofile mit benutzerdefinierten Tastenbelegungen oder -effekten auswählen. Die deutsche Qwertz-Tastatur ist auf Windows-PCs optimiert. Mit Mac sind die Funktionen nur eingeschränkt nutzbar. Der Gaming-Modus mit deaktivierter Windows-Taste verhindert, dass die Technik beim Zocken dazwischenfunkt. Das Modell ist in der Farbe Schwarz erhältlich und mit einer RGB-Hintergrundbeleuchtung ausgestattet. Käufer:innen schätzen an dem Modell vor allem das gute Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis und die individuell konfigurierbaren Einstellungsmöglichkeiten. Bei Amazon kostet die Gaming-Tastatur von Sharkoon 24,99 Euro.
Individuelle Qwertz-Gaming-Tastatur von Omoton
Die mechanische Gaming-Tastatur von Omoton lohnt sich, wenn du Wert auf ein flexibles und kompaktes Setup legst. Per Bluetooth kannst du sie mit bis zu drei Geräten verbinden. Der integrierte 4000-mAh-Akku sorgt laut Hersteller für eine lange Ausdauer im drahtlosen Betrieb. Die RGB-Beleuchtung zeigt den Akkustand an und erinnert rechtzeitig ans Aufladen. Alternativ kannst du in den latenzarmen Kabelmodus wechseln. Die Tastatur ist mit Windows und Mac sowie mit Playstation und Xbox kompatibel. Da das Modell auf den Nummernblock verzichtet, gewinnst du auch auf kleinen Schreibtischen Platz für präzise Mausbewegungen – ideal für Shooter oder Strategie-Games.
Die Tastatur unterstützt QMK und VIA und lässt sich damit sehr umfassend individuell anpassen. Du kannst beispielsweise Makros festlegen, also Abläufe, bei denen eine einzelne Taste mehrere Eingaben nacheinander auslöst. Außerdem erstellst du eigene Ebenen, auf denen dieselbe Taste unterschiedliche Aufgaben übernimmt. So stellst du jeden Tastenanschlag genau nach deinen Bedürfnissen ein. Ein zusätzlicher Multimedia-Knopf dient dazu, die Lautstärke zu regulieren oder den Ton stummzuschalten. Dank der Hot-Swap-Funktion kannst du die Tasten zudem einfach austauschen. Das Design zeichnet sich durch einen Farbverlauf in Anthrazit aus. Der Preis liegt bei 79,99 Euro.
Gaming auf Profi-Niveau mit der Logitech G Pro X TKL Rapid
Laut Herstellerangaben wurde die Logitech G Pro X TKL Rapid zusammen mit E-Sport-Athlet:innen entwickelt und richtet sich gezielt an Gamer:innen, die Reaktionsfähigkeit und Präzision auf Turnierniveau suchen. Sie arbeitet mit analogen Magnetschaltern, die auf dem Hall-Effekt beruhen und berührungslos über ein Magnetfeld messen, wie weit eine Taste gedrückt ist. Die Betätigungskraft beträgt 35 Gramm, sodass die Tasten mit wenig Druck auslösen. Das sorgt für flüssige Eingaben und eine zuverlässige Erkennung jedes Anschlags. Der Rapid-Trigger-Modus dieser Tastatur reaktiviert Tasten, ohne dass du sie vollständig loslassen musst. Das ist besonders bei First-Person-Shootern von Vorteil, in denen jede Millisekunde zählt.
Die Qwertz-Tastatur ist komplett individuell anpassbar. Mit den Modi der Funktionstaste legst du selbst fest, an welchem Punkt eine Taste auslöst. Außerdem kannst du jeder einzelnen Taste einen eigenen Befehl zuweisen und Tastenkombinationen erstellen, die mehrere Aktionen nacheinander auslösen. Die vollständig anpassbare RGB-Beleuchtung lässt sich mit der Musik oder dem Bildschirmgeschehen des Spiels synchronisieren und bietet so ein immersives Gaming-Erlebnis. Die Tastatur ist mit Windows, Linux und Mac kompatibel und in den Farben Schwarz, Weiß und Pink erhältlich. Die unverbindliche Preisempfehlung liegt bei 169,99 Euro. Bei Amazon ist das Modell aktuell schon ab 129,29 Euro erhältlich.

articles.title: Nigeria’s Mytherapist wants to close the gap between needing therapy and getting it - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian startup Mytherapist is helping people find qualified therapists, book appointments and attend sessions via video, audio or chat, while also offering tools to support their wellbeing between sessions.
Founded in 2021 by Oluwaseun Raphael Afolayan and Dedoyin Ajayi, Mytherapist launched a pilot in October 2022 before going public and beginning paid therapy bookings in January 2023.
“The idea came from the difficulty of finding reliable, affordable support during the pandemic and the aftermath of the EndSARS protests. That experience affected me and people around me,” Afolayan told Disrupt Africa.
Mytherapist is built around what Afolayan describes as the practical questions people face when looking for help. “Who should I speak to? What will it cost? When are they available? How do I fit a session into my day?” he said.
“We saw a gap between deciding you need support and actually receiving it. Someone may be willing to try therapy but still struggle to identify a suitable professional, understand the price or arrange an appointment.”
Alongside therapy sessions, the platform offers mood tracking, journaling, meditation and breathing exercises. “These give users ways to reflect and support their everyday wellbeing alongside professional care,” said Afolayan.
The startup serves individuals and couples, and also offers access pathways through employers and health maintenance organisations (HMOs).
“Our approach combines therapist discovery, booking and remote sessions with tools people can use between appointments. We also now offer routes through employers and HMOs, so access does not depend entirely on someone paying out of pocket,” he said.
Mytherapist makes money by taking a commission on therapy sessions booked through the platform. It also offers paid corporate wellbeing services and Prime, an optional membership, which provides additional features and benefits.
Traction has been solid. The startup has more than 25,000 users and over 4,000 completed paid bookings, and has onboarded more than 120 therapists, with over 90 active. Afolayan, however, was careful to put those figures in context.
“Those measures represent different things. Users are not the same as paying clients, and bookings are not the same as completed sessions,” he said. “The next stage is improving how reliably people move from signing up to receiving care and returning when they need further support.”
The startup was initially bootstrapped, and in 2024 received a US$5,000 grant from 54Collective, as well as around US$7,500 in combined grants from Wema Bank Nigeria, ABC Health and FATE Foundation. Afolayan cited the launch of paid bookings, the introduction of couples sessions and corporate wellness services, and the addition of Prime as key milestones.
Nigeria remains Mytherapist.ng’s core market, though it has seen users access the platform from abroad.
“We distinguish that cross-border usage from establishing a local operation in another country,” said Afolayan.
“Our priority is to strengthen the care experience and distribution in Nigeria. Any expansion needs suitable professionals, workable payments and dependable delivery, and we’re currently working on expanding properly, while still maintaining low operational costs, with the help of Paystack and the Startbutton Africa team.”

articles.title: Custom Pins for Tech Events: Premium Finishes vs. Eco Materials - Tech Guide
articles.text:
At developer conferences, hackathons, and global tech summits, custom enamel pins serve as tangible social currency. Attendees collect and trade them across exhibitor booths, wear them on conference lanyards, and display them on laptop sleeves and backpacks long after closing remarks. Designing an effective pin requires balancing visual branding with material durability, volume economics, and event logistics.
Hard Enamel vs. Soft Enamel: Matching Finishes to Event Formats
How your audience engages with your merch comes down to how hard‑enamel and soft‑enamel pins look and feel. You’ll want to pick the proper finish based on your event level and how you plan to hand out the items.
Hard Enamel: Polished Credentials for VIPs and Speakers
Hard enamel pins are baked and polished several times during production. This process brings the enamel and metal edges to the same level, leaving a smooth, shiny surface. The finish is durable enough for pins that are handled often or worn regularly at events.
- Best For: Keynote speakers, VIP sponsors, hackathon judges, and executive summit attendees who want a keepsake from the event.
- Aesthetic Pairing: Polished silver works well with the clean, modern look of software and cloud technology brands. Gold plating or matte black nickel may be a better fit for established tech companies or executive-level events.
Soft Enamel: Dimensional Detailing for Community and Swag Bags
Soft enamel pins have raised metal lines with color filled in between them. You can feel the difference when you run your finger over the surface. They work well for logos, mascots, and pixel-style designs.
- Best For: DevCon swag bags, booth activities such as scan-and-collect pin challenges, gifts for community contributors, and open-source project merchandise.
Design Tip (Format & Sizing): If attendees will be collecting or trading pins at different booths, 0.75-inch mini pins are worth considering. Their smaller size makes them easier to carry on a lanyard, especially when people collect designs from multiple sponsors. This size works with both hard and soft enamel.
Enamel Specification & Decision Matrix
| Dimension | Hard Enamel (Cloisonné Style) | Soft Enamel (Die-Struck Relief) | 
| Surface Profile | Flush, flat, mirror-polished plane | Recessed paint fills with raised metal borders | 
| Tactile Texture | Glass-smooth, jewelry-grade glide | Dimensional, textured 3D relief | 
| Durability Grade | High; highly resistant to abrasion and daily friction | Moderate; raised metal protects paint, but enamel can scuff | 
| Fine Line Tolerance | Moderate (≥ 0.3 mm); lines can widen during polishing | High (≥ 0.15 mm); raised ridges hold crisp micro-details | 
| Cost Baseline | 15% to 25% premium due to multi-stage polishing | Cost-effective baseline for mass distribution | 
| Primary Tech Use | Speaker honors, VIP credentials, executive summits | DevCon swag bags, booth trading quests, contributor drops | 
Sustainable Swag: Aligning Materials with ESG Tech Summits
Companies are paying more attention to the materials used in event giveaways as ESG becomes a bigger part of IT reporting. Brass and zinc are still widely used for pins, but events related to clean energy or climate technology may need other options with a smaller environmental footprint. Organizers may also need documents to back up those claims.
- Recycled Metal (Brass/Zinc): Recycled brass and zinc can achieve the same fine details and polished finish as newly mined metals, with less reliance on virgin resources. They’re a good choice for tech companies that want to use more recycled materials without compromising the look of their pins.
- FSC-Certified Wood (Walnut, Cherry, or Maple): Wood pins have a look and feel that’s quite different from metal pins. Each piece has its own grain, and logos or text can be added through laser engraving. They may suit open-source meetups, cybersecurity events, and smaller tech conferences looking for a simple alternative to traditional enamel pins.
- Bamboo: Lightweight and fast-growing, bamboo gives pins a simple, modern appearance. Its natural texture pairs well with geometric logos and minimalist tech branding.
Evaluating Environmental Claims: A material labeled “eco-friendly” isn’t necessarily the better choice in every situation. For example, untreated wood or poorly finished bamboo may wear out quickly when attached to bags used every day, leading to more frequent replacements. Before ordering, check for credible third-party sourcing certifications and ask suppliers whether their coatings, adhesives, and other finishes are lead-free and non-toxic.
Tiered Pricing and Production Economics
When ordering custom pins, you may need to pay for the mold first, then pay for each pin. Ask the supplier to break down both costs before ordering so you know what you’ll actually spend.
- Tooling and Mold Costs: Each new pin design usually needs its own steel mold, and the setup fee generally stays the same whether you order 100 or 5,000 pieces. For events with different attendee groups, you can reuse one design and change the enamel colors for each group—for example, black and gold for speakers and blue and white for attendees. This helps avoid paying for multiple molds.
- Order Quantity and Leftovers: Ordering more pins can bring down the price per piece, but that doesn’t mean a bigger order is always the better deal. Check the number of people registered before deciding how many to buy. It’s also worth asking suppliers about price differences at 100, 300, 500, 1,000, and 2,500 pieces. Adding 10%–15% to your estimated attendance should leave a few spares without going too far over budget.
- Finishes and Material Costs: Hard enamel pins generally cost 15%–25% more than soft enamel because of the extra polishing involved. Wooden pins and those made with certified recycled metals may also come at a higher price. This is especially noticeable with small orders, where material and production costs are divided among fewer pieces.
Production Timelines, Proofing, and Supplier Sourcing
Managing technical production requires disciplined milestone planning well before event week.
Brand Color Precision & Proofing
- Pantone Color Matching: Colors can look different on a computer screen than they do on a finished enamel pin. To get a closer match to your brand colors, provide vector artwork in AI or EPS format with the correct Pantone (PMS) codes specified.
- Digital Proofs vs. Physical Samples: A digital proof gives you a chance to review the design before production starts, including the metal lines, enamel colors, and cutout shapes. For most orders, this is enough to catch design issues. If you’re ordering more than 2,500 pins or using an unfamiliar eco-friendly material, ask for a physical sample so you can see the finish and quality for yourself.
Lead Times and Event Deadlines
Custom metal pins can take around 2–4 weeks to make, with shipping time added on top. Getting a physical sample first may add another 7–10 business days. To avoid last-minute problems, try to have everything delivered at least 10 business days before the event, especially if the order is coming from overseas.
Supplier Quote Checklist
Choosing a supplier comes down to order size, delivery location, and how quickly you need the pins.
- Bulk Orders: For businesses ordering large quantities, suppliers like GS-JJ offer different styles of custom enamel pins and custom lapel pins to help keep branding consistent across an order.
- Australia and New Zealand: If your event is taking place in Australia, New Zealand, or elsewhere in Oceania, a local manufacturer may be a practical choice for shorter shipping times and fewer cross-border delays. You can start by comparing options in this guide to the Top 6 Custom Pin Manufacturers in Australia.
Some conference pins are handed out as branded gifts, while others are made for attendees to take home and collect. Hard enamel has a flat, polished surface, whereas soft enamel leaves the metal edges standing above the colored sections. Either finish can suit an event logo or mascot, depending on the artwork. For organizers who want something different from standard metal pins, recycled materials or wood are also options. The right choice depends on how the pins will be used, who they’re intended for, and what the event budget allows.

articles.title: VC funding into Indian B2C ecommerce companies dips 33%: Tracxn
articles.text:
VC funding into Indian B2C ecommerce companies dips 33%: Tracxn
Late- and seed-stage funding nearly halved in the period between January 1 and November 3 this year, while early-stage funding remained stable compared to last year.
Venture capital funding into business-to-consumer (B2C) ecommerce companies in India dropped 33% in the ten months of the year, according to a report by Tracxn.
The report titled 'India B2C E-Commerce' noted that, between January 1, 2026 and November 3, 2026, B2C ecommerce companies raised $1.6 billion across 356 rounds, compared with $2.4 billion from 621 rounds in the similar period of 2025.
According to the report, funding and rounds declined, with late- and seed-stage funding nearly halving, while early-stage funding remained stable in 2026 compared to 2025.
The key funding rounds during the period included FS Life ($110 million), Ultrahuman ($65 million), Yulu ($63 million), Snabbit ($56 million), FirstClub ($55 million), and Nua ($50 million).
Early-stage funding reached $872 million in 2026, up 3% from $846 million in 2025. In contrast, late-stage funding declined 51% to $587 million from $1.2 billion, while seed-stage funding fell 50% to $169 million from $339 million. Early-stage accounted for 54% of total funding in 2026, with 97 rounds, compared with 125 in 2025.
Bengaluru raised $686 million in 2026, accounting for 43% of the $1.6 billion raised for the year till now. Mumbai ranked second, with $286 million, while the third place was taken by Gurugram at $199 million.
On the exit front, acquisitions declined to 19 in 2026 compared with 25 in 2025, while IPOs nearly halved to 7 compared to 13 in 2025. L’Oréal’s acquisition of Innovist for $434 million was the largest acquisition of the year by deal value, while Purple Style Labs recorded the highest market capitalisation among companies that went public in 2026, at $488 million. Astrotalk was the only new unicorn in 2026 from the ecommerce category.

articles.title: Hackers backdoor Linux servers using trojanized CWP web server
articles.text:
A new Linux malware called CWPdoor is being distributed through a trojanized version of cwpsrv, the web server behind the Control Web Panel (CWP) management interface.
CWPdoor acts as a passive backdoor that sits dormant on the compromised system until the attacker sends a specially crafted request.
Researchers at XLab, the cybersecurity research arm of QiAnXin Technology Group, describe CWPdoor as "exceptionally stealthy" due to its passive triggering and log suppression feature.
CWP, formerly known as CentOS Web Panel, is an open-source web hosting administration solution similar to cPanel and Plesk that allows users to manage web servers and services such as email, DNS, and databases.
According to XLab, more than 340,000 CWP instances have been exposed on the public web over the past month.
The researchers discovered the CWPdoor malware on June 29 after capturing a script posing as an updater that replaced the legitimate 'cwpsrv' binary with a malicious version.
The script replaces cwpsrv versions 1.15.10 and 1.24.0, and takes several steps to hide the switch, like restoring file and directory timestamps, deleting temporary files, and wiping the command-history log.
The malware operators activate the backdoor by sending it commands to be executed, in the form of an encrypted HTTP header (X-Ngx-Integrity-Data). The request also contains headers for the timestamp (X-Ngx-Integrity-Time) and the RSA signature (X-Ngx-Integrity-Sig).
Commands and their output are encrypted using the AES-256-CBC cipher to keep them protected.
The backdoor checks whether the timestamp falls within a five-minute window and verifies the RSA signature before decrypting the command and passing it to a helper process for execution.
“Changing either the timestamp or the ciphertext independently invalidates the signature,” XLab explains.
“By binding the three fields together and enforcing a ±300-second time window, the mechanism provides replay protection and authorization control.”
The backdoor also interferes with the server’s logging module to prevent the triggering request from appearing in the access logs.
After finding the initial infection script, the researchers saw CWPdoor uploaded to VirusTotal on September 30 in an archive that included the Ebury backdoor.
What caught their attention was that the malicious cwpsrv file (cwpsrv.suspeito) in the archive had zero detections.
"This indicates that the campaign was not merely experimental: real victims already exist in the wild," the researchers say, adding that the connection between Ebury and CWPdoor remains unclear.
Ebury is a Linux backdoor and credential stealer botnet operation active since at least 2009. A report from cybersecurity company ESET in May 2024 said that the malware had infected nearly 400,000 servers since it emerged.
The researchers recommend that administrators check for the ngx_http_integrity_helper Unix socket, suspicious cwpsrv helper processes, and X-Ngx-Integrity strings in the server binary.
If a compromise is confirmed, replace the backdoored binary with a legitimate copy, upgrade to the latest version, rotate all control panel credentials, and investigate the host for additional malware.

articles.title: GTA 6 : Rockstar publie 39 nouvelles images de Vice City pour vous faire saliver — Frandroid
articles.text:
GTA 6 est le jeu le plus attendu de l’année (et peut-être de la décennie). Il s’agit du premier épisode principal de la série depuis GTA 5, sorti en 2013, et Rockstar en a déjà beaucoup montré avec la toute dernière bande-annonce mise en ligne mi-octobre. Le studio n’a pourtant pas fini de jouer avec l’impatience des fans.
Le 19 novembre, Vice City vous attend. Et votre PS5 ? Avec Next Mobiles, pas besoin de payer 600 € d’un coup, louez-la sur la durée que vous souhaitez, dès 16,90 €/mois.
Rockstar a ainsi ouvert ce jeudi 5 novembre une « Galerie de lancement » sur le site officiel du jeu. « Découvrez Vice City et sa région » peut-on lire en en-tête. Au programme : 39 nouvelles images de Vice City et du reste de l’État de Leonida (la Floride revisitée par Rockstar), où se dérouleront les aventures de Lucia et Jason. On n’y apprend rien de neuf sur le gameplay, mais cela permet de se plonger dans l’univers et l’atmosphère du jeu, qui sortira le 19 novembre sur les consoles de jeux PS5 et Xbox Series X|S.
    À lire aussi : 
GTA 6 : où le précommander, date de livraison, consoles, version PC, date de sortie – tout ce qu’il faut savoir
Beaucoup de Vice City et aucune légende
Rockstar n’a mis aucune légende sous ses images, donc ni nom de mission ni indice sur l’histoire. Le site australien TweakTown a compté les captures à partir de leurs noms de fichiers et arrive bien à 39, quand d’autres médias en annonçaient entre 35 et 38. Vice City en occupe 15, Jason Duval apparaît seul sur neuf d’entre elles, Lucia Caminos sur quatre et le duo ensemble sur sept. Le reste sort de la ville, avec deux images des marécages de Grassrivers, une des Leonida Keys et une de Port Gellhorn. Côté scènes, on croise une boîte de nuit, le bar The Rusty Anchor, Jason en pleine séance de développé couché et une chasse à l’alligator de nuit en hydroglisseur. D’autres captures montrent la police qui encercle un superyacht, ou Jason penché par la fenêtre d’une voiture, fusil automatique en main, avec des hélicoptères de police à ses trousses.
Prévoyez de la place pour le pré-chargement
Le pré-chargement, qui permet de télécharger le jeu avant sa sortie pour y jouer dès le premier jour, ouvre le mardi 10 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Libérez de la place d’ici là : le fichier pèse jusqu’à 212 Go selon la console.
Si vous n’avez pas encore précommandé le jeu, l’édition standard de GTA 6 coûte 79,99 euros et l’édition Ultime 99,99 euros, sur PS5 comme sur Xbox Series X|S.

articles.title: Renault écrase la concurrence en octobre : la Twingo championne des ventes électriques suivie de près par la R5
articles.text:
Les voitures électriques continuent leur percée sur le marché français en représentant plus de 4 ventes sur 10 en octobre. Leurs immatriculations ont ainsi augmenté de 81,7 % par rapport à octobre 2025. Les véhicules essence, eux, ont vu en parallèle leurs livraisons se contracter avec une baisse de 44,2 %. Ce ralentissement profite naturellement aux nouveautés françaises qui inondent le top 10. Renault a notamment de quoi sourire.
La dernière Twingo tient en effet sa première victoire en arrivant en tête des ventes avec 4 747 exemplaires sur le mois d’octobre, et 19 230 ventes depuis sa commercialisation au printemps. Ancienne favorite, la R5 garde toujours la forme en décrochant la deuxième place avec 4 666 modèles écoulés, ce qui lui permet de talonner la grenouille. Et entre janvier et octobre, 36 664 exemplaires de la citadine ont encore été vendus.
Peugeot et Citroën distancés par l’offensive au Losange
Cela représente une hausse de 39,5 % par rapport à la même période l’année passée. Elle tient donc le pavé comme la Peugeot e-208, qui a enregistré 3 221 livraisons. La lionne est suivie des 3 037 exemplaires du Renault Scénic. Ce dernier devrait d’ailleurs connaître une nouvelle dynamique grâce à sa version restylée fraîchement commercialisée. En cinquième place pointe la Citroën ë-C3 avec 2 736 modèles vendus.
Le Peugeot e-3008 s’empare de la sixième place avec 1 875 unités écoulées, suivi des 1 786 exemplaires de la Renault 4. Le petit SUV est d’ailleurs le modèle connaissant la plus forte hausse de ses immatriculations avec 145,4 % de ventes en plus sur la période comprise entre janvier et octobre 2026 par rapport à la même période en 2025. Premier modèle étranger du classement, le bien connu Tesla Model Y arrive en huitième position.
Allemandes hors du Top 10 : le réveil annoncé du groupe Volkswagen
Ses 1 748 unités écoulées en octobre lui permettent d’arriver devant le nouveau Kia EV2 et ses 1 506 exemplaires. Le Peugeot e-2008 clôture le top 10 avec 1 412 modèles vendus. Ironiquement, la chinoise la plus vendue est l’anonyme Leapmotor T03 avec 832 exemplaires en 19ème position. Et comme on peut le voir, le groupe Volkswagen n’a pas non plus réussi à intégrer le haut du classement. Son modèle ayant le mieux performé n’arrive qu’à la 13ème place. Il s’agit du Skoda Elroq et ses 1 067 unités.
Un petit passage à vide, donc, qui devrait cependant être rapidement compensé avec l’arrivée des petites électriques connaissant un succès retentissant. Nul doute que nous verrons apparaître dans les prochains mois les Volkswagen ID. Polo, Cupra Raval et Skoda Epiq dans les tableaux. Cette belle dynamique est donc appelée à perdurer avec de futurs modèles électriques toujours plus abordables.

articles.title: Apple quiere que Siri IA esté en todas partes. Al mismo tiempo, limita a 200 dólares el gasto de tokens para sus empleados
articles.text:
Apple quiere que sus usuarios usen todo el rato la nueva Siri AI en sus dispositivos. Apple lo vende como su gran remontada en IA. Pero de puertas para adentro, alguien ha mirado el Excel (o Numbers, en su caso) de gastos en IA de sus empleados y ha empezado a meterle la tijera a los presupuestos diarios de tokens que los equipos de Apple pueden usar para mejorar su trabajo.
Este recorte en el presupuesto de tokens para sus empleados no es cosa solo de Apple. Muchas de las empresas que hasta hace solo unos meses invitaban a sus empleados a usar la IA en su trabajo, han recibido ya su primera factura de esos tokens consumido. El susto ha debido ser tan grande que les han cerrado el grifo.
Apple mete la tijera a los tokens. De acuerdo a lo publicado por Bloomberg, el mes pasado Apple redujo de forma discreta el límite diario de uso de tokens de algunos ingenieros de 300 a 200 dólares. Ahora, la compañía de Ternus estudia rebajarlo todavía más y dejarlo en 100 dólares para determinados equipos.
Fuera de ingeniería, algunos grupos de empleados pasarían de 100 dólares en tokens a 25 dólares diarios. Quien necesite más puede pedir una excepción y se estudiará su uso. Los empleados de Apple disponen de acceso a Claude, ChatGPT y Gemini. Aun así, algunos equipos ya habrían recibo la consigna de usar modelos más baratos o que funcionen de forma local en el propio dispositivo.
¿Tan cara es la factura? Este recorte presupuestario para el uso de IA entre su plantilla llama la atención por venir de la tecnológica con mayor capitalización del mercado. ¿Si Apple no puede pagar la barra libre de tokens para sus empleados, quién puede?
Según sus cuentas, la compañía gastó 45.765 millones en I+D en su último ejercicio, un 32% más que en el anterior. Apple atribuye esa subida en parte a la inversión en IA. Entonces, ¿por qué recortar? Empleados citados por Bloomberg sostienen que "pocos trabajadores utilizaban la totalidad de su asignación diaria de 300 dólares", por lo que el ahorro real puede ser mínimo. Otros empleados manifestaban su temor a que esta limitación presupuestaria pueda ser la antesala de mayores recortes o posibles despidos, como está sucediendo en otras empresas tecnológicas.
Nvidia piensa justo lo contrario. Jensen Huang lo dejó claro en el podcast All-In. Le preocuparía mucho que un ingeniero con 500.000 dólares de sueldo gastara menos de 250.000 dólares en tokens de IA. Cuando le preguntaron si Nvidia gasta unos 2.000 millones al año en tokens para sus ingenieros, el CEO respondió: "Lo estamos intentando".
Las declaraciones de Huang tienen su lógica. Nvidia vende los chips donde se ejecutan esos modelos, por lo que cada token que se quema supone un poco más de inversión en potencia de cómputo y más ventas para sus chips. En Cupertino, que solo pagan la factura, el mensaje es muy diferente.
Apple no es la primera. El frenazo en el fenómeno conocido como tokenmaxxing viene de meses atrás. En Meta hubo una carrera interna por ser quien más tokens gastaba. En Amazon cerraron un ranking parecido en mayo. Su memorando posterior desaconseja el tokenmaxxing, pero la empresa asegura que no ha puesto límites.
En Microsoft, un solo empleado llegó a quemar 28.000 dólares en tokens en solo un mes. Microsoft reaccionó. Su vicepresidente Jay Parikh escribió en un correo interno al que tuvo acceso 404 Media que "el tokenmaxxing no es lo que estamos optimizando".
Revolut cambia de modelo. Con las facturas de los tokens en el punto de mira, algunas empresas buscan otra salida. Revolut ha puesto a unos 2.000 ingenieros a programar por defecto con GLM, un modelo chino de pesos abiertos. Sus parámetros son públicos y se pueden ejecutar en servidores propios, lo cual contribuye a reducir considerablemente el coste en tokens.
El responsable de infraestructura de Revolut, David Abitbol, contó que pagan una décima parte de lo que cuestan los modelos de frontera. Además, la factura es fija y no sube con cada petición. Antes, los 300 dólares mensuales por ingeniero para Claude Code no duraban todo el mes, ahora el límite de consultas la definen sus propios servidores.

articles.title: The Enough Phone is a $499 Android with a small screen, a removable battery, and fewer distractions
articles.text:
First look: The conversation about increasing smartphone screen sizes has mainly centered on phablets and foldables, but standard-sized phones have also grown over the years. A recent Kickstarter aims to gauge interest from users who want to reverse the trend with an Android device smaller than all but the tiniest currently supported iPhones.
The makers of the Sleke phone have launched a Kickstarter for a new model that packs its deliberately low-key feature set into a more compact form factor. Expected to ship in mid-2027, the device highlights how much smartphones have grown since Apple debuted the original iPhone nearly two decades ago.
Early iPhones measured just 3.5 inches with a 320 x 480 pixel resolution before gradually growing past the four-inch mark. Apple's first phablet, the iPhone 6 Plus, expanded to 5.5 inches, but later standard and phablet-sized phones outgrew it by shrinking the bezels.
The iPhone X, for example, reached 5.8 inches, while the iPhone 17 and 18 now sit at 6.3 inches, just two-tenths of an inch smaller than the iPhone 11 Pro Max and nearly twice as large as the original iPhone. However, Apple still supports a few models in the same ballpark as the Enough Phone's 5.3-inch screen: The iPhone 13 mini is just one-tenth of an inch bigger, at 5.4 inches, while the 3rd-generation iPhone SE is still only 4.7 inches.
However, the Enough Phone also targets users looking for an essentials-only smartphone experience with fewer distractions. The phone comes with either a standard Android 17 installation or Sleke's Odyssey OS, an Android fork that supports only communication and utility apps, with pared-back browser functionality.
Measuring just 133 x 64 x 12mm with a 1,500 x 720 screen resolution and a matte finish, the Enough Phone features a MediaTek Dimensity 7500 processor, clocked at 2.4 GHz, a removable 3,500 mAh battery, 8GB of memory, 128GB of storage, and microSD card support. It includes a 50MP Sony IMX766 rear camera and a 32MP front camera that supports face unlock. The power button also supports fingerprint unlock. Software support is planned through 2032.
Pricing starts at $499, with shipments expected to begin in May 2027. However, the creators admit the Enough Phone is still undergoing product tooling, and working samples have yet to be produced. Some technical specs could change before mass production, which is set for April.

articles.title: Bank Phishing Sites Show Fake ‘Suspended’ Pages to Evade Takedowns
articles.text:
A threat actor has been relying on fake ‘suspended account’ notices to hide phishing content from users revisiting its look-alike bank websites, cybersecurity firm Kela reports.
The campaign, active since May, has been relying on more than 300 fake domains, including 248 impersonating 189 US financial institutions. The first were registered in late 2025, but most of them appeared between July and September 2026.
As of October 25, 183 of the targeted organizations still had live look-alikes, mainly targeting mid-sized regional banks. Last week, 49 new domains appeared.
“What ties them together is one mechanism: the kit remembers every visitor’s IP address, so the first visit gets a bank login page, and any return visit gets what looks like a closed hosting account. We call this cluster the ‘Suspended’ infrastructure,” Kela notes.
Most of the identified domains follow a similar naming pattern containing a keyword such as ‘secure’, ‘disable’, ‘protect’, ‘cancel’, ‘authorize’, ‘terminate’, ‘credentials’, and ‘commercial’ followed by a hyphen and the targeted bank’s name.
“A smaller, growing group uses help-desk, live-support, treasury-portal, and ‘primary device’ names built on the bank’s name. About half of the 49 domains that went live in the week to October 25 use these templates, including help-desk and live-chat look-alikes of JPMorgan, Citi, BMO, and Santander,” Kela notes.
While the cybersecurity firm has not discovered how victims are lured to the phishing pages, it did conclude that the campaign is largely targeting business banking and treasury logins rather than personal accounts.
First-time visitors are served pages that contain the targeted bank’s branding, ask for a user ID and password, and may show a reCAPTCHA.
The tab title, “Attention required”, copies Cloudflare’s challenge page name, while a script on the page blocks the browser’s developer tools.
Users who visit the page again are shown a ‘This account has been suspended’ page that copies the notice a hosting provider shows after an account has been closed.
“That design targets exactly the people who could shut a site down. A victim typically follows a link once. A scanner, a security team, or a takedown provider checks a reported site, then checks it again to confirm, and the second check shows what looks like a completed takedown. In practice, a takedown provider can mark a look-alike domain as down while it is still serving the phishing page to new visitors. Seeing the live content requires a new IP address for every check,” Kela notes.
While the fake suspended page was seen across multiple phishing domains, some of them served other fake notices, while others redirected to Google instead, preventing public scanning services from capturing the full campaign.
The domains sit behind Cloudflare, but some briefly resolved to their real servers, which allowed Kela to trace their actual hosting and to discover that the campaign also targets victims in the UK, Australia, and New Zealand.
“Four things make this infrastructure hard to stop: a naming formula simple enough to repeat for any bank; Cloudflare, which hides where the sites are hosted; a kit that shows anyone checking twice a fake ‘suspended’ screen, so a live domain can pass for an inactive one; and shared servers that outlast any single domain,” Kela notes.

articles.title: Motorola's new Signature 27 has it all if you can stomach the $1,600 price tag
articles.text:
Motorola is patching a hole in its US lineup with a non-folding flagship phone, but the pricing puts this device dangerously close to the company’s expensive tablet-style foldable. The long-rumored Motorola Signature 27 is real, featuring top-of-the-line specs, a super-bright OLED screen, and a ton of cameras. But all this high-end hardware won’t come cheap in the age of AI. Motorola’s new flagship smartphone will run a whopping $1,600 when it arrives later this month.
The Signature 27 is a new take on flagship smartphones from Motorola, leaving behind the middling legacy of the Edge series. However, you’ll still immediately clock this as a Motorola device due to its distinctive use of materials and Pantone colors. The phone is metal, ceramic, and glass, but the backs are textured polycarbonate. The device comes in Coal Smoke (black) or Capulet Olive (green) colors. The former has a “tactical weave” finish inspired by automotive design, and the latter is “textile-inspired.”
This device will include the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, the most powerful mobile chip Qualcomm offers right now. While some smartphones have flirted with 16GB of memory, that’s less common these days. The Signature 27 will have 12GB like Samsung’s base model flagships. However, there’s not going to be an upgrade option for more. You will, however, get a generous 512GB of storage.
| Specs at a glance: Motorola Signature 27 |  | 
|---|---|
| SoC | Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 | 
| Memory | 12GB | 
| Storage | 512GB (UFS 4.1) | 
| Display | 6.8-inch Extreme AMOLED Duo, 120Hz, 12,000 nits brightness | 
| Cameras | 50 MP f/1.6 primary, 50 MP f/2 ultrawide, 200 MP 3x periscope telephoto, EVS action sensor; 50MP f/1.9 selfie | 
| Software | Android 17, GrapheneOS installable | 
| Battery | 7,000 mAh, 90 W wired charging, 15W(Qi) wireless | 
| Connectivity | 5G, LTE, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth, SIM+eSIM | 
| Measurements | 162.01×77.04×7.99mm, 227 g | 
| Colors | Coal Smoke, Capulet Olive | 
The phone is fairly thin in most places, but it tapers outward near the camera module. It’s easy to see why Moto needed a little more space up there with four image sensors. Note: That’s not four cameras. There are three standard cameras: a 50MP primary, a 50MP ultrawide, and a 200MP 3x optical zoom (100x digital zoom). Joining the cameras is an event-based vision sensor (EVS) to power a feature called Action Shot.

articles.title: Investidores duvidam que Anthropic consiga valer R$ 8,19 trilhões em IPO
articles.text:
O plano da Anthropic de realizar abertura de capital com avaliação de US$ 1,5 trilhão (aproximadamente R$ 8,19 trilhões) enfrenta resistência de grandes investidores. A recente onda de vendas de ações ligadas à inteligência artificial (IA) aumentou as dúvidas sobre o valor que a empresa poderá alcançar na bolsa e até sobre a realização da operação no calendário previsto.
Segundo informações publicadas pelo The Wall Street Journal, três grandes investidores que pretendem participar da oferta consideram que a avaliação precisará ser reduzida. Um deles acredita que o valor de mercado da companhia poderá ficar mais próximo de US$ 1 trilhão (cerca de R$ 5,46 trilhões).
A Anthropic pretende realizar o IPO na semana anterior ao feriado de Ação de Graças, nos Estados Unidos, e esperava levantar até US$ 100 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 546 bilhões). A operação poderia se tornar a maior abertura de capital da história.
Os investidores ouvidos pelo jornal também demonstraram preocupação com a disposição de fundos institucionais para voltar a apostar pesado no setor de IA depois das perdas recentes. Um deles chegou a questionar a possibilidade de a empresa adiar a oferta.
Outra alternativa seria captar menos dinheiro do que o inicialmente planejado. A Anthropic tinha US$ 146,6 bilhões (cerca de R$ 800 bilhões) em caixa em 30 de setembro, segundo o relatório.
Queda das ações de tecnologia muda cenário para o IPO
- A mudança de percepção ocorre após forte onda de vendas no mercado de tecnologia. Nesta quinta-feira (5), empresas do índice Nasdaq Composite perderam US$ 2,5 trilhões (aproximadamente R$ 13,65 trilhões) em valor de mercado;
- O movimento foi associado ao recuo de investimentos relacionados à IA e ocorreu dois dias depois das eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos, que levaram ao poder um grupo de políticos críticos à expansão da tecnologia e aprovaram moratórias que podem desacelerar a construção de data centers no país;
- Mesmo antes da queda mais recente, a disposição dos investidores para financiar empresas de IA já apresentava sinais de enfraquecimento;
- A OpenAI, principal concorrente da Anthropic, havia buscado levantar US$ 30 bilhões (cerca de R$ 163,8 bilhões) em sua rodada mais recente de financiamento. No entanto, recebeu até então US$ 11 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 60 bilhões), menos da metade da meta inicial, com avaliação de US$ 1,25 trilhão (cerca de R$ 6,83 trilhões).
Leia mais:
- Anthropic quer impedir que empresas escondam qual IA estão usando
- Claude agora pode acessar contas bancárias para analisar gastos
- IA acelera em quase duas vezes o desenvolvimento de modelos da Anthropic
Anthropic tem conexões com gigantes da tecnologia
O desempenho do IPO também pode ter consequências para o mercado mais amplo. A Anthropic mantém relações comerciais e financeiras com algumas das maiores empresas de tecnologia do mundo, incluindo Google, Amazon e Nvidia.
A expectativa era de que a companhia superasse o recorde estabelecido pela abertura de capital da SpaceX, em junho, e protagonizasse a maior oferta pública inicial já realizada.
Executivos da Anthropic e seus assessores devem se reunir nos próximos dias para discutir os planos. Até agora, a empresa evitou assumir compromissos definitivos sobre os detalhes da operação, preservando a possibilidade de ajustar sua estratégia conforme as condições do mercado.
Com a recente turbulência nas ações de tecnologia, a avaliação pretendida de US$ 1,5 trilhão passou a enfrentar questionamentos justamente entre investidores que demonstravam grande interesse em participar da oferta.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: US government warns of 'ongoing cyber threat' amid mass hacks of industrial retail and military freezers | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The U.S. government is warning of an “ongoing cyber threat” facing industrial refrigeration units, after reports of cyberattacks targeting freezers and fridges in supermarkets around the world, U.S. military bases, and at least one blood bank.
U.S. cybersecurity agency CISA, the FBI, and several other federal government departments warned in a joint statement on Thursday that hackers are targeting and compromising internet-connected refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems in grocery stores and cold storage facilities. The statement said that the hacks are hitting critical infrastructure, such as the food, agriculture, transportation, and medicine-shipping industries.
“If successfully exploited, the actors could change the temperature and possibly cause physical impacts such as fire hazards, loss of inventory and changes to the service life of the system,” the agencies warn.
The warning comes after several waves of cyberattacks targeting industrial refrigeration units across the United Kingdom and Europe in recent weeks. Two separate waves of attacks allowed hackers to crank up the temperature on freezers and chilling units in at least a dozen countries, spoiling defrosted food and destroying produce. Some of the affected systems included remote-controlled refrigeration units made by Danish company Danfoss, which had stopped providing security updates to its customers’ freezers.
Hackers also targeted a blood bank in France, causing its refrigerated units to boost temperatures in its cold units containing donated blood supplies — but were stopped before the attack could compromise blood stores. The U.S. Department of Defense is investigating a spate of hacks targeting freezers run by the military, according to Reuters. The hacks were first reported by Signal and Silence.
The U.S. has not attributed the hacks to a particular group or government, but security researchers have broadly attributed the attacks to Iran; U.S. officials also reportedly suspect Iran is the likely culprit.
CISA, the FBI, and the Departments of Agriculture, Health and Human Services, and Transportation urged affected industries to remove remote control systems from the internet, change and strengthen passwords, apply patches where possible, and retire equipment that’s no longer supported by the vendor.
In a separate fact sheet, the departments said that hackers may attempt to “force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, which can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards.”
“Every organization that depends on refrigeration and monitoring systems should assume it could be a target,” said CISA’s acting cybersecurity chief Chris Butera.

articles.title: Hackers target French blood service fridges following supermarket attacks — Russia-aligned hackers claim intrusions are just to expose bad security
articles.text:
Hackers target French blood service fridges following supermarket attacks — Russia-aligned hackers claim intrusions are just to expose bad security
Once again, the root cause is a lack of essential cybersecurity practices, rather than super-intelligent AI bots.
European fridges are so hot right now. Right on the heels of repeated cyberattacks on supermarket freezers, a fresh wave of attacks has hit units used by France's blood service (EFS). Thankfully, no biomaterials were lost, as the attack triggered the EFS' alerts, prompting staff to move the affected goods to proper storage.
The French Health Ministry said that the situation is being closely monitored and that no assets were lost. The attack seemed focused on refrigeration units at three sites, with Burgundy-Franche-Comté reportedly among them. The EFS' communiqué says the intrusion was on a service provider, which some outlets are reporting as Coolworld.
Coolworld has posted a notice stating that the incident was due to "remote monitoring software" used in its systems, pinning the cause on "a component from a third-party supplier." There are no technical details available yet, so it's not yet clear if the hackers found internet-reachable equipment, as they did with the supermarket attacks.
It's possible that Coolworld keeps the controllers inside its own network and that malfeasants had to first gain entry to said network. However, it's worth noting that it was the EFS' monitoring and alarm system that noticed something was up — not the vendor's.
We don't know which brand of refrigerator controllers Coolworld uses, but the ongoing attacks seem to be happening on a per-vendor basis. Danfoss is the most-mentioned name — particularly, but not only, in the recent Nov. 1 - 2 attacks. Copeland/Dixell controllers were named in the Oct. 13 - 14 attacks.
A Danfoss datasheet recommends that its controllers are installed with "appropriately configured firewalls and secure LAN," and not "on any public or non secure network." That's not saying much, as punching holes in a firewall is nearly the same as having the unit directly reachable. The firm did issue a recent support bulletin clearly stating that the units should be installed with a VPN, but that document only appeared in October 2026. We couldn't find previous mention of this advice in our searches.
The manuals for the Copeland/Dixell controller units that were hit in earlier attacks advise installers to map ports 80 (web) and 22 (Secure Shell) to the internet so that the units can be reachable from the outside, suggesting a VPN only as an option. The firm has since published a security advisory recommending that the units only be reachable from inside a VPN. This was published Oct. 14, after the first wave of attacks.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Many news outlets claim to have seen materials — namely, in now-deleted Telegram posts — in which Russia-aligned hacking groups Noname057(16) and Z-Pentest are claiming responsibility for the attacks. Z-Pentest reportedly posted 2,500 lines of Danfoss code, but none of these alleged materials have been published. The purported hackers claim the attacks are about highlighting bad cybersecurity practices.
It's tempting to once again bring up AI agents as vehicles of cyber-destruction, but the reality is that, just like what happened with PHP, most of the time all bots are actually doing is revealing shoddy security practices and/or copious amounts of technological debt.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 isn't Apple's flashiest new laptop, but it might be its best-value one
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Like its predecessors, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro delivers excellent performance for most tasks, long battery life, and better connectivity, all in a familiar build. If you already own a recent M-series MacBook Pro, it's not an essential upgrade; but if you're coming from an older Intel MacBook, or even an older M-series MacBook Air, and you need a powerful, well-rounded laptop that doesn't skimp on features or performance, it's an easy recommendation. Even with a new model sitting above it that offers a touchscreen PROLED display, Apple's most powerful chips, and a lighter build, there's still no arguing with the value proposition of the 14-inch MacBook Pro.
Reasons to buy
- + Excellent M6 performance
- + Strong battery life
- + Vibrant 14.2-inch Liquid Retina XDR display
- + A familiar build with plenty of ports
Reasons to avoid
- - No changes to the design or colors
- - Still has the display notch
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
At a glance: Apple 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6) Review
Apple's latest update to the 14-inch MacBook Pro doesn't change much, but it keeps the line ticking over with the new M6 chip for improved overall performance and better connectivity, all in the same familiar build.
The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starts at $1,999 / £1,999 / AU$3,199, with 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. You can configure it with up to 32GB of RAM and 4TB of storage, add a Nano-Texture display, or step up to the more powerful M5 Pro or M5 Max chips.
If you need more power or a bigger screen, there's the 16-inch MacBook Pro with M6, or the 14-inch and 16-inch models with M5 Pro or M5 Max. The 13-inch and 15-inch M5 MacBook Air are better picks if you want a more portable build and can live with slightly less performance. If you want an OLED touchscreen and a thinner, lighter design, you'll need to look at the more expensive PROLED 14-inch or 16-inch models with the M5 Pro or M5 Max.
Apple MacBook Pro 14-inch (2026, M6) scorecard
How the Apple MacBook Pro 14-inch (2026, M6) scored in our review
| Group 1 Data |  |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Product | Value () | Design () | Performance () | Battery life () | Overall () | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apple MacBook Pro 14-inch (2026, M6) | 4 | 4 | 4.5 | 4.5 | 4 | 
Apple 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6) Review: Value for money
No, this isn't the headline-grabbing new MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen and a thinner, lighter build. Alongside introducing those new models, Apple is sticking with a trend I'm a big fan of: yearly updates that ensure the entry-level MacBook Pro remains a solid proposition, with Apple's latest silicon and other top-end specs under the hood.
Apple hasn't changed much with the 2026 14-inch MacBook Pro, but it didn't need to. As the entry-level Pro, and a step up from the MacBook Air in terms of specs, it offers more ports in a familiar design that's slightly bulkier than the Air, but still plenty portable. You also get a very capable 14-inch Liquid Retina XDR mini-LED display with a notch at the top, a clicky-clacky keyboard with nice travel, a larger trackpad, and great sound with Spatial Audio and Dolby Atmos support.
The big change is the M6 chip under the hood, with this model joining the still-available M5 Pro and M5 Max models. Those chips, while older, are more powerful, but don't let the M6 Pro's entry-level positioning fool you: Apple's latest silicon is no slouch, delivering excellent everyday performance with plenty of power for more intensive tasks, including photo and video editing, coding, and AI work.
I've been using the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 for the best part of a week, and it's been smooth sailing. It's handled my daily mix of productivity and creative work in apps like Slack, Safari, Google Chrome, Notes, Pages, Pixelmator Pro, and Final Cut Pro, running alongside Messages and FaceTime, effortlessly, without me needing to quit or close anything. The configuration I'm testing pairs the M6's 12-core CPU — split between two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores — with a 12-core GPU and Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and the base 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage.
Just like the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5, the new-for-2026 model with M6 starts at $1,999 / 1,999 / AU$3,199. Yes, that M5 model got a price hike earlier this year, but it’s good to see that Apple didn’t push this further, and with this price tag getting you the M6 chip, 16GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage, it's excellent value.
Apple 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6) Review: Design
- Same design as M5 Pro, with plenty of ports
- Excellent 14.2-inch Liquid Retina XDR display with ProMotion
- Comfortable keyboard, oversized trackpad, and 12MP Center Stage camera
The M6 14-inch MacBook Pro sticks with the well-loved and well-tested design of recent Pro models. It's a little bulkier than the Air on account of its plentiful connectivity options, which include three Thunderbolt 4/USB-C ports, an HDMI port, an SD card slot, a headphone jack, and a MagSafe 3 port.
It's the same sleek design as the M5, M4, and even M3 versions that came before it. It's a design I know well, and one I use daily myself, and I appreciate that it doesn't feel too light or flimsy, but also not too heavy at just 3.4 pounds.
It keeps the same overall dimensions as last year's 14-inch Pro at 12.31 x 8.71 x 0.61 inches. You also get the same two color choices, Space Black or Silver; my review model is Silver, and it contrasts quite nicely with the darker, mirrored Apple logo on the rear — unlike the logo on the newly redesigned touchscreen MacBook Pro, though, this one doesn't light up.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The M6 Pro also doesn't pack Apple's fancy new tandem OLED display, which is a stunner, with especially impressive contrast and the added benefit of not having the notch. The 14.2-inch Liquid Retina XDR display here is no slouch, though, and even with that higher-end model's arrival, this remains one of the best laptop screens on the market.
It supports refresh rates up to 120Hz thanks to ProMotion, and delivers a 3024 x 1964 resolution with vibrant colors and excellent contrast, including wonderfully inky blacks. I've found it great for photo editing in Photos or Pixelmator Pro, video editing in iMovie, CapCut, or Final Cut Pro, streaming videos, FaceTime calls, and even the more straightforward task of writing this review. I always appreciate those inky blacks as I type away.
I've become used to the rectangular cutout notch centered at the top of the display, and I'm still confident that if you've never experienced it before, any initial annoyance at its presence will quickly fade. I am eyeing the pill-shaped Dynamic Island on the more expensive MacBook Pro, but it's really not a necessity.
Here, the menu bar wraps around the notch, which houses a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera that keeps you in the frame and looking sharp during video calls. It also supports Portrait mode to blur your background, and you can use the edges of the screen as a ring light in low lighting conditions.
The keyboard still offers excellent travel, and a decidedly satisfying typing experience. I've written a few articles on this machine, including this review, and I still appreciate the Touch ID sensor baked into the top-right key. It's handy for unlocking your Mac, authenticating, and Apple Pay transactions. Equally, the oversized trackpad makes navigation easy, whether you're using classic point-and-click controls or gestures.
Apple 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6) Review: Specs
| Apple MacBook Pro 14-inch (M6/M5 Pro/M5 Max) specs |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Header Cell - Column 0 | MacBook Pro 14-inch (M5) | MacBook Pro 14-inch (M5 Pro) | MacBook Pro 14-inch (M5 Max) | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Price | $1,999 / £1,999 / AU$3,199 | $2,199 / £2,199 / AU$3,499 | $3,599 / £1,999 / AU$5,799 | 
| CPU | M6 12-core | M5 Pro 15-core | M5 Max 18-core | 
| GPU | 12-core | 16-core | 32-core | 
| RAM | 16GB unified memory | 24GB unified memory | 36GB unified memory | 
| Storage | 1TB SSD | 1TB SSD | 2TB SSD | 
| Display | 14-inch Liquid Retina XDR display (3024 x 1964), 120Hz | 14-inch Liquid Retina XDR display (3024 x 1964), 120Hz | 14-inch Liquid Retina XDR display (3024 x 1964), 120Hz | 
| Ports | 3x Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C), HDMI, SDXC card slot, 3.5mm headphone jack, MagSafe 3 | 3x Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C), HDMI, SDXC card slot, 3.5mm headphone jack, MagSafe 3 | 3x Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C), HDMI, SDXC card slot, 3.5mm headphone jack, MagSafe 3 | 
| Wireless | Wi‑Fi 7 (802.11be), Bluetooth 6, and Thread | Wi‑Fi 7 (802.11be), Bluetooth 6, and Thread | Wi‑Fi 7 (802.11be), Bluetooth 6, and Thread | 
| Weight | 3.4 lbs (1.55kg) | 3.5 lbs (1.60kg) | 3.6 lbs (1.62kg) | 
| Dimensions | 12.31 x 8.71 x 0.61 inches (31.26 x 22.12 x 1.55cm) | 12.31 x 8.71 x 0.61 inches (31.26 x 22.12 x 1.55cm) | 12.31 x 8.71 x 0.61 inches (31.26 x 22.12 x 1.55cm) | 
Apple 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6) Review: Performance
- M6 is an excellent chip
- Handles everyday multitasking, creative apps, and gaming with ease
- Apple's N1 chip brings support for latest Wi-Fi and Bluetooth standards
Any Mac with Apple silicon really pushes the value meter, and the M6 inside the MacBook Pro is no different. But that also means that if you have an M5, M4, M3, or even an older MacBook Pro or MacBook Air, and its performance is still good enough for your needs, you likely don't need to rush to upgrade just yet.
The M6 14-inch Pro sits alongside the M5 Pro and M5 Max, and only one chip configuration is available as the entry-level option. It's a 12-core CPU — made up of two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores — alongside a 12-core GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine. While the M5 Pro and M5 Max can outperform it on the GPU front, those chips don't feature efficiency cores in the CPU or the doubled-up Neural Engine. The M6 starts with 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage — the configuration I've been testing — but can be specced with up to 32GB of RAM and 4TB of storage.
So just how good is the M6 chip inside the 14-inch MacBook Pro? Well, quantitatively, it scored 4,752 in Geekbench 6's single-core test and 21,184 in multi-core. In Geekbench 7, it hit 4,027 single-core and 22,305 multi-core. Compare that to the M5-powered 14-inch MacBook Pro, which scored 4,288 and 17,926 in Geekbench 6, respectively. That's a considerable improvement of around 11% in single-core performance and 18% in multi-core. It also shows off the M6's multitasking chops and efficiency, the latter of which is mission-critical for a laptop with a battery inside — more on that below.
On the storage front, the SSD is largely unchanged. In the Blackmagic Disk Speed Test, the M6 MacBook Pro clocked read speeds of 6,684.6 MB/s and write speeds of 6,501.6 MB/s. That's essentially on par with the M5 model, which managed 6,619.7 MB/s read and 6,517 MB/s write. So, no major improvement here, but not a step backwards either.
Over the past few days, I've put the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 through its paces as my daily machine. I regularly use Slack, Google Chrome, Safari — both browsers with dozens of tabs open, as I don't love closing them — Notes, Photos, Pixelmator Pro, Siri, and Music, alongside Messages and the occasional FaceTime or iPhone Mirroring session. I also put it through some video exports and project-creation work, mainly for social video at 2K or 4K, using iMovie, Final Cut Pro, and Edits. I also spent some time gaming with titles like Mini Metro, Mini Motorways, and Disney Dreamlight Valley.
Apple Intelligence is another area where the M6 feels right at home. Siri AI was particularly quick in my testing, especially with multimodal tasks, such as asking it about items on-screen or handling multi-step processes. Apple's Creator Studio improvements also ran smoothly, including Generative Fill in Pixelmator Pro. These are the kinds of tasks that show off the M6's Neural Engine, and I didn't have to wait around for results.
Generative Fill in Pixelmator Pro, as part of Creator Studio, is really impressive, and while it can take a beat to process, it's on a par with Photoshop's Generative Fill. Take a look at the example below, where I added a river below a photo of a Rivian R2 in a parking garage.
With plenty of apps open and a demanding workload running, I did occasionally hear the fans kick in, but never for sustained periods. For the most part, the MacBook Pro remained quiet, even with my usual mix of productivity and creative apps running.
The M6 doesn't quite beat the M5 Pro or M5 Max 14-inch MacBook Pro models for more intensive tasks, like larger video exports. It can certainly hold its own, but those jobs take a little longer, and the fans might kick in along the way. For everyday use and then some, though, whether that's photo or video editing, music creation, or even gaming, the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 easily holds its own.
And that's the case whether you're plugged in or unplugged and running on battery. I didn't notice any performance throttling when switching to battery power, so you can expect the same capable performance without being tethered to an outlet.
Beyond adding the M6 chip, Apple also upgraded the connectivity specs, with the in-house-made N1 wireless chip bringing support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and the Thread smart-home standard.
I’ve found the Pro offers fast connectivity, mostly through my at-home network powered by Eero Pro 6s, and Bluetooth 6 provides a stable connection with my AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and Beats 360.
Apple 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6) Review: Battery Life
- All-day battery life
- Beats Apple's own web-browsing estimate of 16 hours
- Lasted an impressive 19 hours and 5 minutes in our browsing test
Unsurprisingly, the 14-inch MacBook Pro remains a battery-life champ with the M6 inside. Since Apple switched to its own in-house chips, performance, efficiency, and battery life have all improved compared to its previous Intel-powered laptops.
The M6 model features a 72.4-watt-hour lithium-polymer battery like the M5 before it, with Apple promising up to 24 hours of video playback, 16 hours of web browsing, and, as always, "all-day battery life." You can still charge it either with MagSafe — Apple includes a USB-C to MagSafe cable in the box — or via USB-C.
Even with pretty heavy use, the 14-inch MacBook Pro can comfortably last a full workday, and might stretch to multiple days without charging, depending on what you're doing. That's seriously impressive — and as I noted above, performance stays fast whether you're plugged in or running on battery.
In the TechRadar and Future PLC labs test, the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 lasted an impressive 19 hours, 5 minutes, and 30 seconds in our web-browsing test. That's a fantastic result, beating Apple's own 16-hour web browsing estimate, and around 50 minutes longer than the previous M5-powered 14-inch MacBook Pro.
Should I buy the Apple 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6?
✅ You're ready for an M-series MacBook Pro
You get the modern MacBook Pro experience, plenty of performance from the M6 paired with 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage to start, an excellent display, and long battery life. If you're still holding onto an Intel-powered MacBook Pro, now is an excellent time to make the jump to Apple silicon.
✅ You want excellent performance and battery life
The M6 handles creative workloads with ease, and the 14-inch MacBook Pro lasted over 19 hours in our web-browsing test.
❌ You need a bigger screen
If you want a bigger screen you'd be better off looking at the 15-inch MacBook Air, 16-inch MacBook Pro, or the 16-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display.
❌ You need the most powerful MacBook Pro
Since this only has the M6 inside, those who need even more performance — say, to run powerful AI models on-device or handle more creative, intensive tasks — should look at the M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pros, available with or without the PROLED XDR Display.
How I tested the Apple 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6
I spent five days using the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 as one of my daily work machines, taking it through the kind of workload I'd typically throw at my own MacBook. That meant plenty of writing, editing, and multitasking, with dozens of tabs open across Safari and Chrome, with Slack, Notes, Messages, and other everyday apps running alongside creative tools like Pixelmator Pro.
I also tested how well the M6 handled more demanding tasks, including video exports, Apple Intelligence features, and gaming. I compared its performance with the M5 Pro-powered 14-inch MacBook Pro and an M4 14-inch MacBook Pro, and I also used it plugged in and on battery to see whether performance changed when untethered.
First reviewed November 2026.
Jacob Krol is the US Managing Editor, News for TechRadar. He’s been writing about technology since he was 14 when he started his own tech blog. Since then Jacob has worked for a plethora of publications including CNN Underscored, TheStreet, Parade, Men’s Journal, Mashable, CNET, and CNBC among others.
He specializes in covering companies like Apple, Samsung, and Google and going hands-on with mobile devices, smart home gadgets, TVs, and wearables. In his spare time, you can find Jacob listening to Bruce Springsteen, building a Lego set, or binge-watching the latest from Disney, Marvel, or Star Wars.
